fields.name: Time
fields.doc:
Time is when the collection started; zero when the profile does not
say.

fields.name: SampleTypes
fields.doc:
SampleTypes names what each of a sample's values measures, in order:
{cpu nanoseconds}, {inuse_space bytes}.

fields.name: Samples
fields.doc: Samples are the measured stacks.

fields.name: Comments
fields.doc: Comments are the profile's free-text comments.

fields.name: PeriodType
fields.doc:
PeriodType and Period say how often a sample is taken: every Period
PeriodType — 10 000 000 nanoseconds of CPU, 524 288 bytes allocated.

fields.name: DefaultSampleType
fields.doc:
DefaultSampleType is the sample type a viewer shows first; empty when
the profile does not say, and the last sample type is the convention.

fields.name: Duration
fields.doc: Duration is how long the collection lasted; zero when not recorded.

fields.name: Period
fields.doc: Period is the sampling period, in PeriodType's unit.

symbols.doc:
ProfileValue is a decoded pprof profile: what was measured, and every
sample with its stack, its values and its labels. It is plain data — the
profile.proto message with its tables resolved — and safe to share once
built.

symbols.name: ProfilerBusy

code.public: A CPU profile is already being recorded

symbols.doc:
ProfilerBusy refuses a CPU capture while the process's one CPU profiler
is running — started by another capture, or by anyone's
pprof.StartCPUProfile. It is not queued: the caller decides whether to
wait.

symbols.name: SampleTypeMissing

code.public: The profile does not measure that

symbols.doc:
SampleTypeMissing refuses a fold asked for a sample type the profile
does not measure — "cpu" of a heap profile.

symbols.name: SampleTypeValue

fields.name: Type
fields.doc: Type is what is measured: "cpu", "samples", "inuse_space".

fields.name: Unit
fields.doc: Unit is its unit: "nanoseconds", "count", "bytes".

symbols.doc:
SampleTypeValue names what a value measures and its unit — {cpu
nanoseconds}, {inuse_space bytes}.

symbols.name: SampleValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Labels map[string][]string; NumLabels map[string][]int64; Stack []FrameValue; Values []int64}
symbols.canonical: struct{Labels map[string][]string; NumLabels map[string][]int64; Stack []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/profiling.FrameValue; Values []int64}

fields.name: Labels
fields.doc:
Labels are the pprof labels of the goroutine, by key: set with
pprof.Do or pprof.SetGoroutineLabels. A CPU profile carries them; a
heap profile does not.

fields.name: NumLabels
fields.doc:
NumLabels are the numeric labels, by key — a heap sample's "bytes",
the size of each object it counts.

fields.name: Stack
fields.doc:
Stack is the sample's call stack, innermost frame first. A call the
compiler inlined is a frame of its own, before the frame it was
inlined into.

fields.name: Values
fields.doc: Values holds one value per ProfileValue.SampleTypes entry.

symbols.doc:
SampleValue is one sample: a stack, a value per sample type, and the labels
the goroutine carried when it was taken.

symbols.name: WindowInvalid

code.public: A CPU profile needs a window longer than zero and at most five minutes

symbols.doc:
WindowInvalid refuses a CPU window that is not positive — a profile
of no time is empty by construction — or that exceeds MaxCPUWindow.

symbols.name: AvailableExporters
symbols.doc: AvailableExporters returns the sorted list of registered ExporterNames.

symbols.name: Carrier
symbols.spelled: interface{Get(key string) string; Set(key string, value string)}
symbols.canonical: interface{Get(key string) string; Set(key string, value string)}
symbols.doc:
Carrier is the two-method surface a header set has to present for a span
context to travel through it.

It is exactly http.Header's Get/Set pair, on purpose and to the letter, so
the engine's `trace.Inject(ctx, req.Header)` compiles with no adapter — and
so this package still imports no net/http, which would drag an HTTP opinion
into a contract that also has to serve a message queue and a gRPC metadata
map.

IFACE-PLUGIN: it is FROZEN at two methods (ADR 0039). Adding a third — Del,
Values, a multi-value read — would break every downstream two-method double at
compile time with no deprecation window, and every one of those additions is
reachable as a sibling interface instead. Two is also what makes http.Header
satisfy it structurally, which is the whole ergonomics.

symbols.name: CodeDuplicateRegistration
symbols.doc:
CodeDuplicateRegistration identifies a boot-time SpanExporter registry
collision: a nil exporter, or a distinct exporter claiming a taken Name.

symbols.name: CodeEntropyFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeEntropyFailed identified a crypto/rand.Read failure while drawing the
bytes of a trace or span identifier. Nothing returns it since Go 1.24,
whose crypto/rand.Read cannot fail; the code stays allocated and published.

symbols.name: CodeExportFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeExportFailed identifies a span exporter that returned an error while
shipping a batch (the exporter's cause rides the wrap trail).

symbols.name: CodeInvalidAttribute
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidAttribute identifies an attribute set a span, an event, a link or
a Resource cannot carry: an attribute with an empty Key, the same Key twice,
or a value no constructor ever set (AttrKindInvalid). The rules are the
shared model's (internal/core/observe/otel); this code is the trace signal's own,
where it used to borrow the metrics one (0.2.9.4) because the model lived in
internal/core/observe/metrics.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidSampleRatio
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidSampleRatio identifies a Ratio sampler asked for a fraction that
is not one: NaN, negative, above 1, or exactly 0 — which is NeverSample under
a name that also spells "unconfigured" (ADR 0031).

symbols.name: CodeInvalidSpanName
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidSpanName identifies a Start call with an empty span name. A span's
name is the low-cardinality operation label every backend groups on, so an
empty one produces a trace nobody can search for.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidTraceParent
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidTraceParent identifies a traceparent header that cannot be read as
a span context: a malformed field, the invalid version "ff", or an all-zero
trace-id or parent-id — the two values W3C Trace Context declares invalid.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidTraceState
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidTraceState identifies a tracestate header that does not match the
W3C list grammar: a key or value outside its character set, more than 32 list
members, or the same key twice.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPEndpointInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPEndpointInvalid identifies an OTLP/HTTP exporter configured with an
endpoint that is not an absolute http(s) URL carrying a path — the address
the POST would otherwise be sent to blind.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPExportRejected
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPExportRejected identifies a collector that refused the payload
PERMANENTLY: an HTTP status outside the specification's retryable set, so
replaying the same bytes would fail the same way.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPExportUnavailable
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPExportUnavailable identifies a TRANSIENT OTLP/HTTP failure — a
transport fault, or one of the four statuses the specification lists as
retryable. The same bytes may succeed later.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPInvalidSpanContext
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPInvalidSpanContext identifies a span handed to the OTLP/JSON encoder
whose trace-id or span-id is all zeroes. Both are declared invalid by W3C
Trace Context and required by the schema, so there is no honest hex to emit.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPPartialSuccess
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPPartialSuccess identifies a collector that accepted the request
(HTTP 200) but rejected some of its spans. The specification forbids retrying
it, so the loss is reported rather than replayed.

symbols.name: CodeOTLPSpanNotEnded
symbols.doc:
CodeOTLPSpanNotEnded identifies a span handed to the OTLP/JSON encoder with no
EndTime. `end_time_unix_nano` is required, and a zero would claim the span
ended at the Unix epoch.

symbols.name: CodeUnknownExporter
symbols.doc:
CodeUnknownExporter identifies an Export/Lookup naming a span exporter that no
imported package has registered.

symbols.name: ContextWithSpanContext
symbols.doc:
ContextWithSpanContext returns a copy of parent carrying context.

An INVALID context is still stored rather than skipped. Storing it is what
makes "this scope deliberately has no trace" expressible: a handler that ran
under an unsampled or absent traceparent shadows any outer context instead of
silently re-parenting its children onto it.

symbols.name: DefaultScopeName
symbols.doc:
DefaultScopeName names this SDK's TRACE package as the instrumenting library
when a caller declares no scope of their own.

It is a separate constant from metrics' DefaultScopeName, and the difference is
not cosmetic: an InstrumentationScope names the library that produced THIS
signal, so stamping a span batch with `…/pkg/v1/observe/metrics` would tell a backend
that the metrics package emitted spans. Sharing the value would have been the
one place where sharing the model stopped being reuse and started being a
wrong answer — which is exactly the line ADR 0051 §Decision 2 draws, and why
internal/core/observe/otel takes the default as a parameter rather than owning one.

symbols.name: DuplicateRegistration

code.public: A trace exporter is already registered under that name

symbols.doc: DuplicateRegistration is the boot-time SpanExporter-registry panic sentinel.

symbols.name: EntropyFailed

code.public: Trace identifier generation failed to read secure random bytes

symbols.doc:
EntropyFailed was the wrap of a crypto/rand.Read failure while drawing
trace or span id bytes. Nothing returns it since Go 1.24, whose
crypto/rand.Read never fails; it stays published with its value.

symbols.name: EventValue

fields.name: Time
fields.doc:
Time is when it happened. An unset instant encodes as 0, which is what
the schema means by an unknown timestamp.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the event's low-cardinality label.

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc: Attrs are the event's typed dimensions, sorted by Key.

symbols.doc:
EventValue is one thing that happened at an instant during a span, rather than
over an interval — `opentelemetry/proto/trace/v1.Span.Event`.

An event is not a cheap child span, and the distinction is worth stating
because the wrong choice is invisible until a trace is unreadable: an event
has no identity, no duration and no children, so nothing can be a child of it
and nothing can link to it. Use one for a moment worth marking on a span's
timeline (a retry, a cache miss, an exception); use a child span for work that
took time.

symbols.name: Normalized
symbols.doc:
Normalized returns the event a span actually records: attributes sorted,
validated and owned, so the caller's slice cannot be mutated afterwards
through the span.

symbols.name: ExceptionEventName
symbols.doc: ExceptionEventName is the reserved event name for a recorded error.

symbols.name: ExceptionMessageKey
symbols.doc: ExceptionMessageKey names the error's message.

symbols.name: ExceptionStacktraceKey
symbols.doc:
ExceptionStacktraceKey names the error's stack trace. This SDK never
fills it: a Go error carries no stack, and inventing one from the
recording site would name the wrong goroutine.

symbols.name: ExceptionTypeKey
symbols.doc: ExceptionTypeKey names the error's type.

symbols.name: Export
symbols.doc:
Export ships spans through the SpanExporter registered as name. A missing
exporter returns UnknownExporter; an exporter failure wraps as ExportFailed.

symbols.name: ExportFailed

code.public: The trace exporter failed to ship the spans

symbols.doc: ExportFailed wraps an exporter's failure while shipping spans.

symbols.name: ExporterName
symbols.doc:
ExporterName is the typed key under which a SpanExporter registers (e.g.
"otlpjson"). The zero value ExporterName("") is reserved invalid.

The registry is deliberately the same shape as core/observe/metrics' — the same
kernel/plugin.Registry underneath, named, reached by blank-importing the
exporter's package, config-addressable. It EARNS its
keep here for the reason it earns it there and for one more: ADR 0051
§Decision 5 requires the OTLP/HTTP emitter to be absent from it, and "absent
from the registry" is only a statement anyone can check if there is a registry
to be absent from. A test pins that absence.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc: String returns the raw name.

symbols.name: FlagSampled
symbols.doc:
FlagSampled is the sampled bit: the least significant one. When set, the
caller "may have recorded trace data" (§3.2.2.5.1), which is what makes the
sampling decision a property of the TRACE rather than of each span.

symbols.name: InvalidAttribute

code.public: An attribute key is empty or repeated, or its value was never set

symbols.doc:
InvalidAttribute is the panic sentinel for an unusable attribute set on
a span, an event, a link or a Resource.

symbols.name: InvalidSampleRatio

code.public: A sampling ratio must be greater than 0 and at most 1

symbols.doc:
InvalidSampleRatio is returned when Ratio is handed a fraction it will
not turn into a sampler.

symbols.name: InvalidSpanName

code.public: A span name must not be empty

symbols.doc: InvalidSpanName is the panic sentinel for a Start call with no name.

symbols.name: InvalidTraceParent

code.public: The traceparent header is not a valid W3C trace context

symbols.doc:
InvalidTraceParent is returned when a traceparent header cannot be read.
Its Public never echoes the header: it is attacker-controlled text.

symbols.name: InvalidTraceState

code.public: The tracestate header is not a valid W3C trace state list

symbols.doc: InvalidTraceState is returned when a tracestate header cannot be read.

symbols.name: LinkValue

fields.name: Context
fields.doc:
Context identifies the linked span. A link whose context is invalid is
dropped rather than emitted — it names nothing.

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc: Attrs describe the relationship, sorted by Key.

symbols.doc:
LinkValue points at a span that is causally related to this one but is not its
parent — `opentelemetry/proto/trace/v1.Span.Link`.

The canonical case is a batch: one consumer span processes fifty messages
produced by fifty different traces. Making any one of them the parent would be
a lie about forty-nine, and making the batch a child of all fifty is not a
tree. A link says "related, elsewhere" without claiming ancestry.

It carries a whole SpanContextValue rather than a loose trace-id/span-id pair
because the linked context's tracestate and sampled bit are part of what a
backend needs: a link into a trace that was never sampled points at spans
nobody stored.

symbols.name: IsValid
symbols.doc: IsValid reports whether the link names a joinable span.

symbols.name: Normalized
symbols.doc:
Normalized returns the link a span actually records: attributes sorted,
validated and owned.

symbols.name: LookupExporter
symbols.doc:
LookupExporter returns the SpanExporter registered under name.

IFACE-PLUGIN: the registry stores plug-in exporters behind the SpanExporter
interface — concrete backend types stay unexported.

symbols.name: MaxTraceStateKeyLen
symbols.doc:
MaxTraceStateKeyLen is the longest legal key: `simple-key = lcalpha
0*255(...)` is 1 + 255 characters.

symbols.name: MaxTraceStateMembers
symbols.doc:
MaxTraceStateMembers is the list cap: `list = list-member 0*31( OWS ","
OWS list-member )` is 32 members, no more.

symbols.name: MaxTraceStateValueLen
symbols.doc:
MaxTraceStateValueLen is the longest legal value: `value = 0*255(chr)
nblk-chr` is 255 + 1 characters.

symbols.name: NewStateBuilder
symbols.doc:
NewStateBuilder returns an empty builder with room for size members. A size
above MaxTraceStateMembers is clamped to it — no list holds more — and a
negative one is read as zero.

symbols.name: NormalizeResource
symbols.doc:
NormalizeResource returns the ResourceValue a Tracer publishes: attributes
sorted, validated, owned, and carrying ServiceNameKey whether or not the
caller supplied it. An unusable attribute set panics with InvalidAttribute,
at construction, rather than at the first export.

symbols.name: NormalizeScope
symbols.doc:
NormalizeScope returns the ScopeValue a Tracer publishes, filling an empty Name
with DefaultScopeName. Version is left exactly as supplied: it is optional in
the specification, and inventing one would be a claim about code this package
cannot see.

symbols.name: OTLPEndpointInvalid

code.public: The OTLP endpoint must be an absolute http(s) URL with a path

symbols.doc: OTLPEndpointInvalid is returned when an OTLP/HTTP endpoint is unusable.

symbols.name: OTLPExportRejected

code.public: The trace collector rejected the export

symbols.doc: OTLPExportRejected reports a permanent refusal by the collector.

symbols.name: OTLPExportUnavailable

code.public: The trace collector is unavailable

symbols.doc: OTLPExportUnavailable reports a transient failure worth retrying.

symbols.name: OTLPInvalidSpanContext

code.public: A span carries an all-zero trace or span identifier

symbols.doc: OTLPInvalidSpanContext is returned when a span carries an unusable id.

symbols.name: OTLPPartialSuccess

code.public: The trace collector accepted the request but rejected some spans

symbols.doc: OTLPPartialSuccess reports an accepted request with rejected spans.

symbols.name: OTLPSpanNotEnded

code.public: A span reached the exporter without an end time

symbols.doc: OTLPSpanNotEnded is returned when a span reaches the encoder unended.

symbols.name: ParseSpanID
symbols.doc:
ParseSpanID reads 16 lowercase hex digits into a SpanID, refusing an all-zero
result for the reason ParseTraceID does.

symbols.name: ParseTraceID
symbols.doc:
ParseTraceID reads 32 lowercase hex digits into a TraceID, refusing an
all-zero result.

Uppercase is refused rather than folded: the traceparent grammar is 32HEXDIGLC
and a producer emitting uppercase is producing a header other vendors will
reject, so accepting it here would hide the defect exactly one hop from where
it was introduced.

symbols.name: RegisterExporter
symbols.doc:
RegisterExporter inserts e under e.Name() and returns it for singleton
binding. Panics on a nil exporter or a distinct exporter on a taken Name.

IFACE-PLUGIN: the registry hands plug-in SpanExporter instances back to
callers so each backend keeps its concrete type unexported.

"Nil" here means UNUSABLE, not only an untyped nil: a typed nil pointer and a
plug-in whose type is not comparable both satisfy the port and neither can
serve one call (see internal/kernel/plugin).

symbols.name: Sampler
symbols.doc:
Sampler decides whether a span is recorded and exported. It reports true to
keep the span, false to drop it.

It is a FUNC port, not an interface, applying ADR 0041 structurally: a
published func type cannot grow a method at all, so there is no widening to
forbid and no sibling to invent later.

# The decision is taken ONCE, at the root

This is the load-bearing rule of the whole domain and it is not a convention —
it is what the `sampled` bit of traceparent is FOR. A Tracer consults a
Sampler only when it is starting a root span; every child, in this process or
in any process downstream, inherits the answer through
SpanContextValue.IsSampled.

Deciding per span produces a trace with holes in the middle, and a trace with
holes is worse than no trace: a span whose parent was dropped becomes an
orphan a backend renders as its own root, so one request appears as several
unrelated ones and the latency of the whole is unrecoverable. The failure is
also invisible at the point that causes it — the process that dropped the
parent shows nothing wrong at all.

A Sampler is therefore consulted on ROOT spans only. That is a property of the
Tracer, stated here because this is where a reader will look for it.

# Concurrency

A Sampler MUST be safe for concurrent use and MUST NOT block: it runs inline
on the goroutine starting the span, before any work the span measures.

symbols.name: SamplingParams
symbols.spelled: struct{Parent SpanContextValue; TraceID TraceID; Name string; Kind SpanKind; Attrs []coreotel.AttrValue; Links []LinkValue}

fields.name: Parent
fields.doc:
Parent is the context this span descends from, or the invalid zero
value when this is a root.

fields.name: TraceID
fields.doc: TraceID is the trace the new span belongs to.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the span's operation name.

fields.name: Kind
fields.doc: Kind is the span's relationship to its neighbours.

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc:
Attrs are the attributes supplied at Start, sorted by Key. Attributes
added AFTER Start are invisible here — the decision has already been
taken by then, which is the price of taking it once.

fields.name: Links
fields.doc: Links are the links supplied at Start.

symbols.doc:
SamplingParams is everything a Sampler sees. It describes a span that does not
exist yet, which is the point: the decision is taken before the span is
created, so an unsampled span costs no recording at all.

TraceID is present and Parent may not be. On a ROOT span the trace id has just
been minted and there is no parent; on a CHILD it is the parent's, inherited
unchanged. A ratio sampler reads it either way, which is what makes the same
sampler usable at both ends without a special case.

symbols.name: SortAttrs
symbols.doc:
SortAttrs returns a sorted, validated, owned copy of attrs — what a span, an
event and a link record, so the caller's slice cannot be mutated afterwards
through the span. An unusable set panics with InvalidAttribute, at the call
site that wrote it rather than at the first export.

symbols.doc:
Span is one live, recording span.

IFACE-PLUGIN: FROZEN at five methods (ADR 0039). Two things a reader will
expect and not find, each deliberate:

  - There is no RecordError. It would have to decide what an error's TYPE is,
    which is a judgement about the caller's error model, and it is expressible
    as one AddEvent call. pkg/v1/observe/trace ships it as a HELPER over this port
    instead, which is exactly the shape that does not freeze a decision into a
    port.
  - End takes no timestamp. A span that ends at a time other than "now" is
    either replaying history or working around a clock, and both want a sibling
    interface rather than a parameter every caller has to pass a zero value to.

Every method is safe for concurrent use and every one is a NO-OP on an
unsampled span, so instrumentation costs nothing when sampling is off. End is
idempotent: the second call is ignored rather than emitting the span twice.

symbols.name: AddEvent
symbols.doc: AddEvent records a timestamped point inside the span.

symbols.name: End
symbols.doc: End closes the span and hands it to the Tracer's SpanSink.

symbols.name: SetAttrs
symbols.doc: SetAttrs adds or replaces typed dimensions on the span.

symbols.name: SetStatus
symbols.doc: SetStatus records the operation's outcome.

symbols.name: SpanContext
symbols.doc: SpanContext returns the span's identity — what Inject propagates.

symbols.name: SpanContextFromContext
symbols.doc:
SpanContextFromContext returns the span context carried by ctx, or the invalid
zero value when there is none.

It never returns an error and never panics on a nil-ish context value: an
absent trace is the normal state of most code, not a fault.

fields.name: TraceID
fields.doc: TraceID identifies the whole trace. Shared by every span in it.

fields.name: SpanID
fields.doc: SpanID identifies this span within the trace.

fields.name: Flags
fields.doc:
Flags is the traceparent flag byte, kept EXACTLY as received. Undefined
bits are masked at format time (TraceFlags.Sanitized), never on receipt.

fields.name: State
fields.doc:
State is the tracestate list travelling beside the traceparent. It is
propagated verbatim; this SDK adds no entry of its own.

fields.name: Remote
fields.doc:
Remote reports whether this context was EXTRACTED from a carrier rather
than created in this process. OTLP carries the fact as a span flag, and
a backend needs it to tell "my caller" from "my own parent span".

symbols.doc:
SpanContextValue is the immutable identity of a span: what traceparent and
tracestate carry between two processes, and what a child span inherits.

It is a VALUE, not a handle. A span context can be copied, compared field by
field and stored on a context.Context without any of it referring back to a
live span — which is what makes propagation across a process boundary the
same operation as propagation across a function call.

The zero value is the INVALID context, and that is deliberate rather than
incidental: an all-zero TraceID is exactly what W3C Trace Context §3.2.2.3
declares invalid, so "no trace here" and "a trace nobody may join" are one
value with one spelling. Every consumer therefore has exactly one check to
make — IsValid — instead of a nil test and a validity test that can disagree.

symbols.name: IsSampled
symbols.doc:
IsSampled reports whether the sampled bit is set on this context.

It is the ONLY sampling question anything downstream asks. The decision is
taken once, at the root of the trace, and travels in this bit; re-deciding per
span produces a trace with holes in the middle, which is worse than no trace
at all because it looks complete.

symbols.name: IsValid
symbols.doc:
IsValid reports whether the context names a joinable span: both identifiers
present and non-zero.

symbols.name: WithState
symbols.doc:
WithState returns a copy of c carrying state. It exists so a caller who
mutates the vendor list does not have to rebuild the identity around it.

symbols.name: SpanExporter
symbols.doc:
SpanExporter ships a batch of finished spans to a backend.
Implementations MUST be safe for concurrent use.

IFACE-PLUGIN: the registry stores plug-in exporters behind this interface;
concrete exporter types stay unexported per package.

symbols.name: SpanID
symbols.doc:
SpanID identifies one span within a trace: 8 bytes, 16 lowercase hex digits.
The all-zero value is invalid for the same normative reason TraceID's is
(§3.2.2.4), and is additionally how "this span has no parent" is spelled —
a root span's ParentSpanID is the zero value, which OTLP encodes as an
omitted parentSpanId.

symbols.name: IsValid
symbols.doc: IsValid reports whether s is a usable span identifier, i.e. not all zeroes.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc: String renders the identifier as 16 lowercase hex digits.

symbols.name: SpanIDHexLen
symbols.doc: SpanIDHexLen is the span identifier's length in lowercase hex.

symbols.name: SpanIDLen
symbols.doc: SpanIDLen is the span identifier's length in bytes.

symbols.name: SpanKind
symbols.doc:
SpanKind says how a span relates to its parent and its children, which is what
lets a backend assemble a latency waterfall instead of a flat list.

The five values and their integers are
opentelemetry/proto/trace/v1.Span.SpanKind, copied from the schema so the OTLP
encoder emits the integer directly (OTLP/JSON encodes an enum as its NUMBER,
never as its name).

symbols.name: Resolved
symbols.doc:
Resolved returns the kind a span actually carries: SpanKindUnspecified clamps
to SpanKindInternal, every declared value is honoured, and anything else — a
cast, since there is no other way to produce one — clamps too.

It clamps where Temporality refuses (ADR 0044 §Decision 3), and the asymmetry
applies the clamp-or-refuse question honestly: an unstated temporality changes what a
NUMBER means, so no default can be chosen for the caller; an unstated kind
changes only how a span is drawn, and the specification itself names the
default. A clamp is right exactly when the SDK is not substituting judgement.

symbols.name: String
SpanKindClient
symbols.doc:
SpanKindClient is SPAN_KIND_CLIENT (3): making an outbound synchronous
request and waiting for it.

symbols.name: SpanKindConsumer
symbols.doc:
SpanKindConsumer is SPAN_KIND_CONSUMER (5): handling a message that was
enqueued earlier. Its parent finished long before it started, which is
why it is not simply a SERVER span.

symbols.name: SpanKindInternal
symbols.doc:
SpanKindInternal is SPAN_KIND_INTERNAL (1): work inside one process,
with no remote counterpart.

symbols.name: SpanKindProducer
symbols.doc:
SpanKindProducer is SPAN_KIND_PRODUCER (4): enqueuing a message whose
handling happens later, and elsewhere.

symbols.name: SpanKindServer
symbols.doc:
SpanKindServer is SPAN_KIND_SERVER (2): handling an inbound synchronous
request. Its parent is normally a remote CLIENT span.

symbols.name: SpanKindUnspecified
symbols.doc:
SpanKindUnspecified is SPAN_KIND_UNSPECIFIED (0). It is the zero value,
and the schema's own comment says an implementation should set INTERNAL
instead — so it CLAMPS rather than travels (ADR 0031 §clamp): a span
created with no stated kind is doing work inside this process, which is
what INTERNAL means. Nothing this SDK emits carries it.

symbols.name: SpanParams
symbols.spelled: struct{Kind SpanKind; Attrs []coreotel.AttrValue; Links []LinkValue; StartTime time.Time}

fields.name: Kind
fields.doc:
Kind is the span's relationship to its neighbours. The zero value
resolves to SpanKindInternal (SpanKind.Resolved).

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc:
Attrs are the dimensions known at Start. They are the ONLY ones a
Sampler sees, so anything the sampling decision depends on belongs here
rather than in a later SetAttrs.

fields.name: Links
fields.doc: Links point at causally related spans in other traces.

fields.name: StartTime
fields.doc:
StartTime overrides the span's start instant. The zero value means
"now", which is what every caller but a replaying one wants — and it is
a CLAMP rather than a refusal because "now" is a description of what the
tracer does, not a value chosen on the caller's behalf (ADR 0031).

symbols.doc:
SpanParams are the facts a span is born with.

It is a struct rather than a variadic option list because an option type is a
published func the SDK would then have to freeze (ADR 0039), and because the
zero value has to be usable: SpanParams{} is an INTERNAL span starting now
with no attributes, which is the common case and reads as one at the call site.

symbols.name: SpanSink
symbols.doc:
SpanSink receives every span that ends and was sampled. It is where a Tracer
hands its output, and it is a func port for the reason Sampler is.

It is the seam a batching processor would occupy (ADR 0051 §Deferred): a batch
is a SpanSink that buffers and forwards, which is why the port is one span at
a time rather than a slice — a sink that took slices would force every
non-batching consumer to allocate one.

A SpanSink MUST be safe for concurrent use: spans end on whichever goroutine
was doing the work. It runs on that goroutine, so a slow sink slows the
request it is observing.

fields.name: Context
fields.doc: Context identifies this span: trace-id, span-id, flags, tracestate.

fields.name: Parent
fields.doc:
Parent identifies the span this one descends from. The zero value means
this is a root span.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the low-cardinality operation label a backend groups on.

fields.name: Kind
fields.doc:
Kind is the span's relationship to its neighbours, already resolved —
never SpanKindUnspecified on a span a Tracer produced.

fields.name: StartTime
fields.doc: StartTime opens the interval the span covers.

fields.name: EndTime
fields.doc:
EndTime closes it. A span whose EndTime is unset never ended, and no
exporter in this SDK will ship one.

fields.name: Attrs
fields.doc: Attrs are the span's typed dimensions, sorted by Key.

fields.name: Events
fields.doc:
Events are timestamped points inside the interval, in the order they
were recorded.

fields.name: Links
fields.doc: Links point at causally related spans in other traces.

fields.name: Status
fields.doc: Status is the recorded outcome, already resolved.

symbols.doc:
SpanValue is a completed span: the OpenTelemetry trace data model's `Span`
message, in Go.

It is IMMUTABLE and it is what a live Span becomes at End. Splitting the two
is what keeps an exporter from ever seeing a span mid-flight: the recording
type has mutators and no exporter can reach it, this one has no mutators and
is all an exporter is given.

Two fields are whole SpanContextValues rather than loose identifiers, and both
pay for themselves:

  - Context carries the trace-id, the span-id, the sampled bit and the
    tracestate as ONE value — the same value that travelled in the
    traceparent, so nothing has to be reassembled to know what was propagated.
  - Parent carries its own Remote flag, which is the only place the fact is
    recorded that this span's parent ran in another process. OTLP has a field
    for exactly that (`flags`, SPAN_FLAGS_CONTEXT_IS_REMOTE_MASK), and a
    backend uses it to tell a service boundary from an internal call.

A root span's Parent is the invalid zero value, which OTLP encodes as an
omitted parentSpanId — the schema's own spelling for "no parent".

symbols.name: Duration
symbols.doc: Duration reports how long the span covered, or zero when it never ended.

symbols.name: IsRoot
symbols.doc: IsRoot reports whether the span has no parent.

symbols.name: SpansValue

fields.name: Resource
fields.doc: Resource identifies the producer, carried once for the whole payload.

fields.name: Scope
fields.doc:
Scope identifies the instrumentation, carried once for the whole
payload.

fields.name: Spans
fields.doc:
Spans are the finished spans, in the order they ended. That order is
stable and is what makes an exporter's output diffable; it is NOT
causal — a parent ends after its children.

symbols.doc:
SpansValue is a batch of finished spans plus the two facts that describe all
of them at once — the OTLP payload hierarchy flattened into one Go value.

It is the trace counterpart of metrics' SnapshotValue and it is shaped by the
same rule (ADR 0044 §Decision 9): an OTLP encoder must be able to walk it
WITHOUT regrouping or reconstruction.

	SpansValue            -> resourceSpans[0]
	  .Resource           ->   .resource.attributes
	  .Scope              ->   .scopeSpans[0].scope {name, version}
	  .Spans[i]           ->   .scopeSpans[0].spans[]

The two single-element levels are single because one Tracer has exactly one
Resource and one Scope, exactly as one Meter does.

It carries NO StartTime/Time pair, and that absence is the model rather than
an omission: a metrics snapshot is one window shared by every point, while
every span carries its own interval. Copying a payload-level window down onto
a span would overwrite the only timestamps a trace has.

symbols.name: IsEmpty
symbols.doc:
IsEmpty reports whether the payload carries no span. An exporter uses it to
skip a POST that would carry nothing.

symbols.name: StateBuilder
symbols.doc:
StateBuilder assembles a StateValue member by member, LEFTMOST FIRST — the
order a tracestate header lists them in, which is the opposite of Insert's
"newest at the front". It is how the engine's header parser
(internal/service/observe/trace.ParseTraceState) turns the list it read into
a value without this package parsing the header: reading the wire format is
the engine's mechanism, the list's invariants are this value's (ADR 0160 §4).

Every member is checked before it enters the list — the key against
`simple-key` / `multi-tenant-key`, the value against `value = 0*255(chr)
nblk-chr` — and so are the list's own two rules: a key appears once
(§3.3.1.4) and there are at most MaxTraceStateMembers members. So a builder
can only produce a list Insert could have produced, which is why it is not
the "second way in" a from-parts constructor would be.

The zero value is a usable empty builder. A builder is not safe for
concurrent use.

symbols.name: Add
symbols.doc:
Add appends key=value at the right end of the list, reporting whether it
did. It adds nothing and reports false when the key or the value is not one
the grammar can spell, when the key is already in the list, or when the list
already holds MaxTraceStateMembers members. Nothing of either argument is
echoed anywhere: a tracestate is written by a stranger.

symbols.name: State
symbols.doc:
State returns the list built so far, leftmost first, and leaves the builder
empty. The builder hands its storage to the value rather than copying it, so
it lets go of that storage too: a later Add starts a new list instead of
writing into one that is meant to be immutable.

symbols.name: StateValue
symbols.doc:
StateValue is the parsed `tracestate` header: an ORDERED list of vendor
entries, leftmost first.

The order is load-bearing and is the reason this is not a map. §3.5 states it
twice over: "the order of unmodified key/value pairs MUST be preserved" and
"modified keys SHOULD be moved to the beginning (left) of the list", because
the leftmost entry is the system that touched the trace most recently. A map
would lose exactly that, and lose it silently.

The value is IMMUTABLE: Insert and Delete return a new StateValue rather
than mutating the receiver, so a span context handed to a handler cannot be
edited underneath the caller that produced it. The zero value is a valid empty
list.

This SDK writes NO entry of its own. It is not a tracing vendor with state to
carry, and inventing a key would put a name nobody registered on every
outbound request; Insert exists for a consumer who IS one.

A list comes from three places only: the zero value, Insert, and a
StateBuilder — the one the engine's header parser fills, member by member.
Each of the last two checks every member against the grammar before it
enters the list, so no StateValue holds an entry the next hop would refuse.

symbols.name: Delete
symbols.doc:
Delete returns a copy of s without the entry under key. §3.5 asks a vendor
not to delete keys it did not generate; this method is the mechanism, not the
permission.

symbols.name: Get
symbols.doc: Get returns the value recorded under key, and whether it was present.

symbols.name: Insert
symbols.spelled: func(key string, value string) (state StateValue, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(key string, value string) (state github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/trace.StateValue, err error)
symbols.doc:
Insert returns a copy of s carrying key=value at the FRONT of the list,
replacing any existing entry for key.

Front, not in place, because §3.5 says a modified key "SHOULD be moved to the
beginning (left) of the list": leftmost means most recently touched, and that
is the only information the order carries.

When the result would exceed 32 members the OLDEST — rightmost — entry is
dropped, which is §3.3.1.5's "the vendor MUST truncate whole entries". Its
companion rule, "entries larger than 128 characters SHOULD be removed first",
is deliberately NOT implemented: it is scoped to truncation "due to size
limitations", and this list is bounded by member COUNT, never by byte length.
Implementing it would drop a short-lived vendor's entry for being verbose
rather than for being old, which is a different policy wearing the same name.

symbols.name: Len
symbols.doc: Len reports how many list members the state carries.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc:
String renders the list as a tracestate header value: `key=value` members
joined by a comma, leftmost first, with no optional whitespace.

The OWS the grammar allows is not reproduced. It is optional, it carries no
meaning, and omitting it makes the header a deterministic function of the
list — which is what lets a test compare bytes rather than re-parse.

symbols.name: StatusCode
symbols.doc:
StatusCode is opentelemetry/proto/trace/v1.Status.StatusCode. Three values,
and the third is not the negation of the second.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc:
String renders the code as its OpenTelemetry name, for text output and
readable test failures. The wire carries the integer.

symbols.name: StatusError
symbols.doc: StatusError is STATUS_CODE_ERROR (2): the operation failed.

symbols.name: StatusOK
symbols.doc:
StatusOK is STATUS_CODE_OK (1): the developer explicitly asserted
success, which the specification says should override any backend
heuristic. It is therefore a claim, never set by this SDK on its own.

symbols.name: StatusUnset
symbols.doc:
StatusUnset is STATUS_CODE_UNSET (0), the default and the overwhelmingly
common value. It means "no explicit judgement was recorded" — NOT "it
worked". A backend applies its own heuristics (an HTTP 5xx, a timeout);
an SDK claiming OK on the caller's behalf would suppress exactly those.

symbols.name: StatusValue

fields.name: Code
fields.doc: Code is the verdict.

fields.name: Message
fields.doc:
Message describes the failure. It is dropped unless Code is
StatusError, and it is the ONE free-text field a span carries — so it
must not be given a value the operator cannot see safely. It is not an
errs Public: a span message is read by whoever reads the trace.

symbols.doc:
StatusValue is a span's recorded outcome.

The Message field is only meaningful on StatusError, and the schema says so:
"message … SHOULD be used only if the code is ERROR". This type enforces it in
Resolved rather than trusting the caller, because a message hanging off an OK
status is the sort of thing that renders as an error in one backend's UI and
vanishes in another's.

symbols.name: IsUnset
symbols.doc:
IsUnset reports whether the status carries no judgement at all. It is what the
OTLP encoder asks before deciding whether the `status` field is worth a line.

symbols.name: Resolved
symbols.doc:
Resolved returns the status a span actually carries: an undeclared code
clamps to StatusUnset, and a Message survives only on StatusError.

symbols.name: TraceFlags
symbols.doc:
TraceFlags is the 8-bit field traceparent carries as its last component.

Version 00 of the specification defines exactly one bit, and §3.2.2.5.2 is
explicit about the rest: "The behavior of other flags … is not defined and is
reserved for future use. Vendors MUST set those to zero." This SDK therefore
MASKS on output rather than trusting what it was handed — see Sanitized.

symbols.name: IsSampled
symbols.doc: IsSampled reports whether the sampled bit is set.

symbols.name: Sanitized
symbols.doc:
Sanitized returns f with every bit this specification version does not define
cleared.

It is applied on the way OUT, never on the way in. §3.2.2.5.2 says a vendor
MUST set undefined bits to zero, so emitting a bit we did not set would make
this SDK a non-conforming producer; but §3.2.4 says a receiver must not
"assume anything about unknown fields", so clearing them on the way in would
destroy information a future version defines. Keeping the received byte and
masking at format time satisfies both halves at once.

symbols.name: WithSampled
symbols.doc:
WithSampled returns f with the sampled bit set to sampled, leaving every
other bit as it was.

symbols.name: TraceID
symbols.doc:
TraceID identifies one trace: 16 bytes, rendered as 32 lowercase hex digits
on the wire.

The ALL-ZERO value is invalid, and that is normative rather than stylistic —
W3C Trace Context §3.2.2.3 says a receiver "MUST ignore the traceparent" when
the trace-id is all zeroes, and the OTLP schema documents the same. It is
therefore the zero value of this type AND its "unset" spelling, which is why
IsValid exists and why nothing in this package accepts an id without asking.

symbols.name: IsValid
symbols.doc: IsValid reports whether t is a usable trace identifier, i.e. not all zeroes.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc:
String renders the identifier as 32 lowercase hex digits — the spelling both
traceparent and OTLP/JSON use. OTLP/JSON is the one place the protobuf-JSON
mapping is overridden: "the traceId and spanId byte arrays are represented as
case-insensitive hex-encoded strings; they are not base64-encoded".

symbols.name: TraceIDHexLen
symbols.doc: TraceIDHexLen is the trace identifier's length in lowercase hex.

symbols.name: TraceIDLen
symbols.doc: TraceIDLen is the trace identifier's length in bytes.

symbols.name: Tracer
symbols.spelled: interface{Start(ctx context.Context, name string, params SpanParams) (child context.Context, span Span)}
symbols.canonical: interface{Start(ctx context.Context, name string, params github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/trace.SpanParams) (child context.Context, span github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/observe/trace.Span)}
symbols.doc:
Tracer starts spans. It is the only way a span comes into existence.

IFACE-PLUGIN: it is FROZEN at one method (ADR 0039). Everything a caller might
want to add — a second Start taking an explicit clock, a Flush, a Shutdown —
is reachable as a sibling interface or as a method on the concrete type, and
none of them is worth breaking every downstream double for.

Start returns a context carrying the new span's context, so a callee that
starts its own span becomes a child without either function naming the other.
The Span is returned separately rather than fished back out of the context,
because a caller who has to look up the span they just created will eventually
look up the wrong one.

An EMPTY name panics with InvalidSpanName: a span name is the low-cardinality
operation label every backend groups on, it is a literal at the call site, and
it is therefore wrong on the first call or never — the same argument that makes
an unusable attribute key a panic in `metrics`.

ValidateAttrs panics with InvalidAttribute (0.2.20.7) when sorted cannot name
a dimension set: an empty Key, a value no constructor ever set, or the same
Key twice. The rules are the shared model's (internal/core/observe/otel); the code is
this signal's own.

sender credentials did not match the expected supervised process.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidNotification
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidNotification identifies a received sd_notify datagram that could not
be parsed into NAME=value fields.

symbols.name: CodeInvalidSpec
symbols.doc:
CodeInvalidSpec identifies a Start call whose Spec is malformed — an empty
Path or a contradictory attribute combination.

symbols.name: CodeListenFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeListenFailed identifies a failure creating or binding the supervisor-side
sd_notify datagram socket.

symbols.name: CodeNotifyFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeNotifyFailed identifies a failure sending an sd_notify datagram to
$NOTIFY_SOCKET (distinct from the no-op when the variable is unset).

symbols.name: CodeReapFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeReapFailed identifies a wait4 failure during a reap sweep other than the
benign "no children" condition.

symbols.name: CodeRelayFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeRelayFailed identifies a Relay that could not forward a received signal to
its target process or group.

symbols.name: CodeRlimitFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeRlimitFailed identifies a setrlimit(2) failure applying a per-process
resource limit.

symbols.name: CodeSignalFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeSignalFailed identifies a kill(2) failure delivering a signal to a process
or process group.

symbols.name: CodeSpawnFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeSpawnFailed identifies a fork/exec failure when starting the process — a
missing binary, a permission denial, or a kernel resource fault.

symbols.name: CodeStdioCaptureFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeStdioCaptureFailed identifies a StdioCapture spawn whose output copier
could not deliver the child's stdout/stderr to the caller's writer (the writer
itself returned an error). Surfaced from Wait when the process otherwise
exited cleanly.

symbols.name: CodeStopFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeStopFailed identifies a graceful-stop that could not terminate the process
group even after escalating to SIGKILL.

symbols.name: CodeSubreaperFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeSubreaperFailed identifies a prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER) failure when
arming subreaper semantics for a non-PID1 supervisor.

symbols.name: CodeUnknownGroup
symbols.doc:
CodeUnknownGroup identifies a Spec naming a Group or supplementary group that
does not resolve to a gid on the host.

symbols.name: CodeUnknownResource
symbols.doc:
CodeUnknownResource identifies an Apply call naming a Resource the platform
does not map to an RLIMIT_* constant.

symbols.name: CodeUnknownSignal
symbols.doc:
CodeUnknownSignal identifies a Parse call whose name or number is not in the
platform signal table.

symbols.name: CodeUnknownUser
symbols.doc:
CodeUnknownUser identifies a Spec naming a User that does not resolve to a uid
on the host.

symbols.name: CodeUnsupportedPlatform
symbols.doc:
CodeUnsupportedPlatform identifies a primitive invoked on an operating system
that cannot provide it (e.g. cgroup or subreaper off Linux). The no-op stub
returns it instead of panicking.

symbols.name: CodeWaitFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeWaitFailed identifies a wait4 failure while reaping the leader — a host
fault, not a normal non-zero exit (which is reported via ExitValue).

symbols.name: CredentialMismatch

code.public: Datagram sender credentials did not match

symbols.doc:
CredentialMismatch is returned when a received datagram's kernel-verified
sender credentials do not match the expected supervised process.

symbols.name: ExitValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Code int; Signal Signal; Signaled bool; UserTime time.Duration; SystemTime time.Duration; MaxRSS int64}
symbols.canonical: struct{Code int; Signal github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc.Signal; Signaled bool; UserTime time.Duration; SystemTime time.Duration; MaxRSS int64}

fields.name: Code
fields.doc:
Code is the exit status (0–255) when the process exited normally; it is -1
when the process was terminated by a signal.

fields.name: Signal
fields.doc:
Signal is the signal that terminated the process, or the zero Signal when
it exited normally.

fields.name: Signaled
fields.doc:
Signaled reports whether the process was terminated by a signal rather
than exiting on its own.

fields.name: UserTime
fields.doc: UserTime is the CPU time spent in user mode.

fields.name: SystemTime
fields.doc: SystemTime is the CPU time spent in kernel mode on the process's behalf.

fields.name: MaxRSS
fields.doc:
MaxRSS is the peak resident set size in kilobytes, as reported by wait4's
rusage; it is 0 when the platform does not supply it.

symbols.doc:
ExitValue is the immutable outcome of a finished process: its exit status, the
signal that terminated it (if any), and resource-usage accounting. It is the
value returned by Process.Wait.

symbols.name: Success
symbols.doc: Success reports whether the process exited normally with status zero.

symbols.name: Group
symbols.spelled: interface{Add(pid int) error; Delete() error; Freeze() error; Kill() error; SetCPUMax(quota int64, period int64) error; SetIOMax(spec string) error; SetMemoryMax(bytes int64) error; SetPidsMax(n int64) error; Thaw() error}
symbols.canonical: interface{Add(pid int) error; Delete() error; Freeze() error; Kill() error; SetCPUMax(quota int64, period int64) error; SetIOMax(spec string) error; SetMemoryMax(bytes int64) error; SetPidsMax(n int64) error; Thaw() error}
symbols.doc:
Group is a handle to a cgroup v2 control group used to confine a process tree:
set controller limits, attach processes, and remove the group. Implementations
live in internal/service/proc/*; it is Linux-only and non-Linux builds return
a no-op satisfying this interface with UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.

symbols.name: Add
symbols.doc: Add moves the process pid into this group by writing cgroup.procs.

symbols.name: Delete
symbols.doc: Delete removes the (empty) control group; callers move processes out first.

symbols.name: Freeze
symbols.doc:
Freeze quiesces the whole group by writing "1" to cgroup.freeze (kernel
>= 5.2), stopping every member so a consistent signal sweep or snapshot can
run. Returns UnsupportedPlatform when cgroup.freeze is absent. Idempotent.

symbols.name: Kill
symbols.doc:
Kill atomically SIGKILLs every process in the group by writing "1" to
cgroup.kill (systemd KillMode=control-group; kernel >= 5.14). Unlike a
process-group kill, nothing escapes — a member that called setsid is still
in the control group. Returns UnsupportedPlatform when cgroup.kill is absent
(older kernels), so callers can fall back to SignalGroup.

symbols.name: SetCPUMax
symbols.doc:
SetCPUMax writes cpu.max as "quota period" (systemd CPUQuota=); a negative
quota means "max".

symbols.name: SetIOMax
symbols.doc:
SetIOMax writes one io.max line verbatim (systemd IO*Max=), e.g.
"8:0 rbps=1048576".

symbols.name: SetMemoryMax
symbols.doc:
SetMemoryMax writes memory.max (systemd MemoryMax=); a negative value
means "max" (no limit).

symbols.name: SetPidsMax
symbols.doc:
SetPidsMax writes pids.max (systemd TasksMax=); a negative value means
"max".

symbols.name: Thaw
symbols.doc:
Thaw resumes a frozen group by writing "0" to cgroup.freeze. Returns
UnsupportedPlatform when cgroup.freeze is absent. Idempotent.

symbols.name: InvalidNotification

code.public: Received sd_notify datagram is malformed

symbols.doc:
InvalidNotification is returned when a received sd_notify datagram cannot
be parsed into NAME=value fields.

symbols.name: InvalidSpec

code.public: Process specification is invalid

symbols.doc:
InvalidSpec is returned by Start when the Spec is malformed — an empty Path
or a contradictory attribute combination.

symbols.name: LimitInfinity
symbols.doc:
LimitInfinity is the soft/hard value meaning "no limit" (RLIM_INFINITY). Use
it in a LimitValue to lift a resource ceiling rather than setting a number.

symbols.name: LimitValue

fields.name: Soft
fields.doc: Soft is the enforced limit; it must not exceed Hard.

fields.name: Hard
fields.doc: Hard is the ceiling for Soft; raising it typically requires privilege.

symbols.doc:
LimitValue is an immutable soft/hard resource-limit pair for setrlimit(2). The
soft limit is the enforced value; the hard limit is the ceiling an
unprivileged process may raise the soft limit to.

symbols.name: ListenFailed

code.public: Could not create the sd_notify listener socket

symbols.doc:
ListenFailed is returned when the supervisor-side sd_notify datagram socket
cannot be created or bound.

symbols.name: Listener
symbols.doc:
Listener is the supervisor side of the sd_notify protocol: it owns the
AF_UNIX datagram socket a supervised child writes readiness to, and yields one
parsed, credential-verified NotificationValue per received datagram.
Implementations live in internal/service/proc/*.

symbols.name: Close
symbols.doc: Close releases the socket and unblocks any in-flight Recv.

symbols.name: Recv
symbols.doc:
Recv blocks until the next datagram arrives and returns it parsed, with the
sender PID verified by the kernel. It returns a typed error on a malformed
datagram or once the listener is closed.

symbols.name: MemoryLimitValue
symbols.spelled: struct{Allowance int64; Limit int64; Source MemorySource}

fields.name: Allowance
fields.doc:
Allowance is the tightest cgroup memory cap governing this process, in
bytes, or zero when none was read.

fields.name: Limit
fields.doc:
Limit is the Go soft memory limit derived from Allowance, in bytes, or
zero when no limit was applied.

fields.name: Source
fields.doc: Source names what decided the outcome.

symbols.doc:
MemoryLimitValue is an immutable record of one soft-memory-limit derivation:
the cgroup allowance it read, the limit it derived, and what decided the
outcome.

Allowance and Limit are zero on every outcome except MemorySourceCgroup, with
one exception: MemorySourceBelowFloor carries the Allowance it read, because
the reason the limit was discarded is only legible next to the cap that
produced it.

symbols.name: Applied
symbols.doc:
Applied reports whether the derivation installed a limit. It is true for
exactly one source, and it is the predicate a caller wants rather than a
comparison against Limit — a zero Limit and "no limit applied" are the same
state today, and tying call sites to that coincidence would be fragile.

symbols.name: MemorySource
symbols.doc:
MemorySource names what decided the Go soft memory limit, so a caller that
sees no limit applied can tell WHY without re-deriving it.

The zero value is deliberately unclaimed. A MemorySource is produced by a
derivation, never chosen by a caller, so a zero reaching a log line is a value
this package never minted rather than one of the four real outcomes wearing a
default.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc:
String renders the source for a log line. A value this package never mints —
including the zero — renders as "unknown" rather than as a number, because it
is a defect worth reading as one.

symbols.name: MemorySourceBelowFloor
symbols.doc:
MemorySourceBelowFloor reports that a cap was found but the limit derived
from it fell under the usable floor. Holding the runtime beneath it would
spin the collector continuously without averting the kill, so the
derivation declines rather than applying a limit it expects to hurt.

symbols.name: MemorySourceCgroup
symbols.doc:
MemorySourceCgroup reports the only outcome that yields a limit: a real
cap was read from the control-group hierarchy and the derived value is
usable.

symbols.name: MemorySourceOperator
symbols.doc:
MemorySourceOperator reports that GOMEMLIMIT carried a non-empty value.
The Go runtime has already applied it and the derivation stands aside:
overriding an operator's explicit decision would contradict them silently.

The run starts at iota+1 so the zero stays unminted — see the type comment.

symbols.name: MemorySourceUnconstrained
symbols.doc:
MemorySourceUnconstrained reports that no control group governing this
process declares a memory cap: not containerised, capped at "max", or not
Linux at all. There is nothing to derive a limit from.

symbols.name: NotificationValue
symbols.spelled: struct{State map[string]string; Status string; MainPID int; SenderPID int}
symbols.canonical: struct{State map[string]string; Status string; MainPID int; SenderPID int}

fields.name: State
fields.doc:
State is the raw NAME=value field set from the datagram (READY, STATUS,
MAINPID, WATCHDOG, RELOADING, STOPPING, …), preserved verbatim.

fields.name: Status
fields.doc: Status is the free-text STATUS= line, empty when absent.

fields.name: MainPID
fields.doc: MainPID is the PID advertised by MAINPID=, or 0 when absent.

fields.name: SenderPID
fields.doc:
SenderPID is the sending process's PID as verified by the kernel via
SO_PASSCRED, not a value the sender can forge; 0 when credentials were
unavailable.

symbols.doc:
NotificationValue is a parsed sd_notify(3) datagram received by a Listener: the
raw newline-separated state fields plus the kernel-verified sender PID. It
carries no policy — a supervisor decides what READY or WATCHDOG means for
ordering. The lifecycle flags are read through methods so State stays the
single source of truth.

symbols.name: Ready
symbols.doc: Ready reports whether the datagram carried READY=1.

symbols.name: Reloading
symbols.doc: Reloading reports whether the datagram carried RELOADING=1.

symbols.name: Stopping
symbols.doc: Stopping reports whether the datagram carried STOPPING=1.

symbols.name: Watchdog
symbols.doc: Watchdog reports whether the datagram carried WATCHDOG=1 (a keep-alive ping).

symbols.name: NotifyFailed

code.public: Could not send the sd_notify datagram

symbols.doc:
NotifyFailed is returned when an sd_notify datagram cannot be sent to
$NOTIFY_SOCKET — distinct from the no-op when the variable is unset.

symbols.name: Parse
symbols.doc:
Parse resolves a signal from its name or number into sig. It accepts the
canonical "SIGTERM", the bare "TERM", and the numeric "15" (all
case-insensitive), returning UnknownSignal for anything the platform table
does not define.

symbols.name: Process
symbols.spelled: interface{PID() int; Signal(sig Signal) error; SignalGroup(sig Signal) error; Stop(ctx context.Context, grace time.Duration, sig Signal) error; Wait() (ExitValue, error)}
symbols.canonical: interface{PID() int; Signal(sig github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc.Signal) error; SignalGroup(sig github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc.Signal) error; Stop(ctx context.Context, grace time.Duration, sig github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc.Signal) error; Wait() (github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc.ExitValue, error)}
symbols.doc:
Process is a handle to a spawned process. It exposes only lifetime control —
observe completion, deliver a signal to the leader or its whole group, and
stop it gracefully. Implementations live in internal/service/proc/*; the
pkg/v1/proc/process facade returns this interface.

symbols.name: PID
symbols.doc: PID reports the process identifier of the leader.

symbols.name: Signal
symbols.doc: Signal delivers sig to the leader process only.

symbols.name: SignalGroup
symbols.doc:
SignalGroup delivers sig to the leader's entire process group (kill(-pgid,
sig)), reaching forked grandchildren — the KillMode=control-group analogue.

symbols.name: Stop
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, grace time.Duration, sig Signal) error
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, grace time.Duration, sig github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc.Signal) error
symbols.doc:
Stop terminates the process group gracefully: it sends sig, waits up to
grace for exit, then escalates to SIGKILL. It returns when the process has
exited or ctx is cancelled.

symbols.name: Wait
symbols.doc:
Wait blocks until the process exits and returns its ExitValue — the real
one even when a running Reaper collected the child first. It is safe
to call once; concurrent or repeated calls observe the same outcome. Under
StdioCapture it returns only after every captured byte has reached the
caller's writers; if a writer itself failed, the ExitValue still reports the
real exit status and the error is StdioCaptureFailed.

symbols.name: ReapFailed

code.public: Could not reap child processes

symbols.doc:
ReapFailed is returned when a reap sweep hits a wait4 error other than the
benign "no children" condition.

symbols.name: Reaper
symbols.doc:
Reaper collects terminated child processes so they do not linger as zombies —
the core duty of any PID1 or subreaper. Implementations live in
internal/service/proc/*; non-supporting platforms return a no-op reaper.

A sweep collects every exited child, including one a Process handle is
waiting for; an implementation must hand such a child's exit status to that
Process rather than discard it, so its Wait still reports the real exit.

symbols.name: ReapOnce
symbols.doc:
ReapOnce performs a single non-blocking sweep and reports how many
children were reaped. It is safe to call concurrently with the loop.

symbols.name: Start
symbols.doc:
Start begins a background SIGCHLD-driven loop that reaps children as they
exit. It is idempotent: a second Start while running is a no-op.

symbols.name: Stop
symbols.doc:
Stop ends the background loop after a final draining sweep, so shutdown
leaves no un-reaped zombies. It is safe to call without a prior Start.

symbols.name: RelayFailed

code.public: Could not relay the signal to the target

symbols.doc:
RelayFailed is returned by Relay when a received signal cannot be forwarded
to its target process or group.

symbols.name: Resource
symbols.doc:
Resource identifies a per-process resource governed by setrlimit(2). It is an
abstract, platform-portable enum; the service layer maps each value to the
platform's RLIMIT_* constant. The zero value ResourceUnknown is the reserved
invalid sentinel.

symbols.name: Known
symbols.doc: Known reports whether r is a defined resource other than the zero value.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc:
String reports the canonical lowercase name of r (e.g. "nofile"), or
"unknown" for an unrecognised value. The names match the suffix of the
systemd Limit* directives.

symbols.name: ResourceAS
symbols.doc:
ResourceAS limits the process virtual address-space size (RLIMIT_AS),
mapping systemd's LimitAS=.

symbols.name: ResourceCPU
symbols.doc:
ResourceCPU limits CPU time in seconds (RLIMIT_CPU), mapping systemd's
LimitCPU=.

symbols.name: ResourceCore
symbols.doc:
ResourceCore limits the size of a core dump in bytes (RLIMIT_CORE),
mapping systemd's LimitCORE=.

symbols.name: ResourceData
symbols.doc:
ResourceData limits the process data-segment size (RLIMIT_DATA), mapping
systemd's LimitDATA=.

symbols.name: ResourceFSize
symbols.doc:
ResourceFSize limits the largest file the process may create in bytes
(RLIMIT_FSIZE), mapping systemd's LimitFSIZE=.

symbols.name: ResourceMemLock
symbols.doc:
ResourceMemLock limits bytes that may be locked into RAM (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK),
mapping systemd's LimitMEMLOCK=.

symbols.name: ResourceNProc
symbols.doc:
ResourceNProc limits the number of processes for the real user id
(RLIMIT_NPROC), mapping systemd's LimitNPROC=.

symbols.name: ResourceNoFile
symbols.doc:
ResourceNoFile limits the highest open file descriptor (RLIMIT_NOFILE),
mapping systemd's LimitNOFILE=.

symbols.name: ResourceStack
symbols.doc:
ResourceStack limits the process stack size (RLIMIT_STACK), mapping
systemd's LimitSTACK=.

symbols.name: ResourceUnknown
symbols.doc: ResourceUnknown is the reserved zero value: no resource selected.

symbols.name: RlimitFailed

code.public: Could not apply the resource limit

symbols.doc:
RlimitFailed is returned when setrlimit(2) fails applying a per-process
resource limit.

symbols.name: Signal
symbols.doc:
Signal is a typed, platform-portable OS signal. Its underlying value is the
platform signal number, so Signal(syscall.SIGTERM) and a Signal parsed from
"SIGTERM" compare equal. The zero value is the reserved invalid signal.

symbols.name: Int
symbols.doc: Int reports the raw platform signal number underlying s.

symbols.name: Known
symbols.doc: Known reports whether s names a signal in the platform table.

symbols.name: OS
symbols.doc:
OS bridges s to the os.Signal expected by os/signal and Process.Signal. It is
a zero-cost conversion to syscall.Signal — the canonical os.Signal carrier.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc:
String reports the canonical upper-case name of s (e.g. "SIGTERM"). An
unrecognised signal renders as "signal <n>" so logs stay unambiguous.

symbols.name: SignalFailed

code.public: Could not deliver the signal

symbols.doc:
SignalFailed is returned when kill(2) fails delivering a signal to a
process or process group.

symbols.name: SpawnFailed

code.public: Could not start the process

symbols.doc:
SpawnFailed is returned when fork/exec fails — a missing binary, a
permission denial, or a kernel resource fault.

symbols.name: Spec
symbols.spelled: struct{Path string; Args []string; Dir string; Env []string; User string; Group string; Groups []string; Setpgid bool; Setsid bool; Umask *int; Nice *int; OOMScoreAdj *int; Rlimits map[Resource]LimitValue; CgroupPath string; Stdio StdioMode; Stdout io.Writer; Stderr io.Writer; Stdin io.Reader; ExtraFiles []*os.File}
symbols.canonical: struct{Path string; Args []string; Dir string; Env []string; User string; Group string; Groups []string; Setpgid bool; Setsid bool; Umask *int; Nice *int; OOMScoreAdj *int; Rlimits map[github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc.Resource]github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc.LimitValue; CgroupPath string; Stdio github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc.StdioMode; Stdout io.Writer; Stderr io.Writer; Stdin io.Reader; ExtraFiles []*os.File}

fields.name: Path
fields.doc:
Path is the executable to run. Required. A value containing a path
separator is a file path, taken as written (a relative one is resolved
against Dir). A bare name — "go", "sh" — is searched in the PATH the
CHILD will see: the PATH entry of Env whenever Env names one (an
explicitly empty PATH= searches nothing), the parent's only when Env
names none (including when Env is nil). os/exec's rules apply: the first
executable in PATH order wins, and a match found only through a relative
entry ("." or an empty one) is refused with exec.ErrDot.

fields.name: Args
fields.doc:
Args is the full argv including argv[0]; when empty the service uses
[Spec.Path] — the name as written, not the resolved file — as the sole
argument.

fields.name: Dir
fields.doc: Dir is the working directory; empty means inherit the parent's.

fields.name: Env
fields.doc:
Env is the explicit environment; nil yields an empty environment, never
implicit inheritance, so a spawned service starts from a known state.

fields.name: User
fields.doc: User is the name or numeric uid to setuid to; empty leaves the parent's.

fields.name: Group
fields.doc: Group is the name or numeric gid to setgid to; empty leaves the parent's.

fields.name: Groups
fields.doc: Groups are supplementary group names or gids (systemd SupplementaryGroups=).

fields.name: Setpgid
fields.doc:
Setpgid places the child in its own process group, enabling group-kill of
the whole tree (systemd KillMode=control-group without cgroups).

fields.name: Setsid
fields.doc: Setsid starts the child in a new session detached from the controlling tty.

fields.name: Umask
fields.doc:
Umask, when non-nil, is the file-creation mask applied to the child
(systemd UMask=).

fields.name: Nice
fields.doc:
Nice, when non-nil, is the scheduling-priority adjustment applied to the
child (systemd Nice=).

fields.name: OOMScoreAdj
fields.doc:
OOMScoreAdj, when non-nil, is the /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj value applied
to the child (systemd OOMScoreAdjust=).

fields.name: Rlimits
fields.doc:
Rlimits are per-resource soft/hard limits applied post-fork, pre-exec
(systemd Limit*=); resources unsupported on the platform surface a typed
error rather than silently no-op.

fields.name: CgroupPath
fields.doc:
CgroupPath, when non-empty, is an already-created cgroup v2 directory the
child is placed into BEFORE exec, so controller limits (MemoryMax/TasksMax/
…) apply from its first instruction — closing the unconfined window that a
post-spawn Group.Add(pid) leaves open (systemd places the unit's payload in
its cgroup the same way). The service writes the child's pid to
<CgroupPath>/cgroup.procs in the pre-exec trampoline. Linux-only: a non-empty
value on any other GOOS surfaces UnsupportedPlatform; a path that is missing,
not a cgroup v2 directory, or not delegated surfaces a typed cgroup error
rather than spawning unconfined.

fields.name: Stdio
fields.doc:
Stdio selects how the child's standard streams are wired: StdioInherit
(default — share the parent's), StdioNull (discard to the null device), or
StdioCapture (use the Stdout/Stderr/Stdin members below). systemd
StandardOutput=/StandardError=/StandardInput= is the analogue.

fields.name: Stdout
fields.doc:
Stdout, when Stdio is StdioCapture, receives the child's standard output;
a nil writer discards that stream to the null device.

fields.name: Stderr
fields.doc:
Stderr, when Stdio is StdioCapture, receives the child's standard error;
a nil writer discards that stream to the null device.

fields.name: Stdin
fields.doc:
Stdin, when Stdio is StdioCapture, is copied to the child's standard input;
a nil reader gives the child an immediate-EOF stdin. The reader should be
EOF-terminating (a buffer, file, or strings.Reader); the copier closes the
child's stdin at EOF and never blocks Wait.

fields.name: ExtraFiles
fields.doc:
ExtraFiles are additional open files inherited by the child, in order,
starting at file descriptor 3 (after stdin/stdout/stderr). This is the
mechanism behind socket activation (sd_listen_fds): an activator binds
listening sockets and passes them here, then sets LISTEN_FDS/LISTEN_PID in
Env so the child finds them at fd 3..3+len-1. nil means no extra fds.

symbols.doc:
Spec is the immutable description of a process to spawn: the executable and
its environment, the credentials and isolation topology to apply, and the
resource/scheduling attributes to set between fork and exec. It carries no
policy — restart, health, and dependency concerns belong to the caller.

Pointer fields (Umask, Nice, OOMScoreAdj) distinguish "leave at the inherited
default" (nil) from "set explicitly to zero". Maps and slices are read by the
service layer and never mutated.

symbols.name: StdioCapture
symbols.doc:
StdioCapture connects the child to the Spec's Stdout/Stderr writers and
Stdin reader; a nil writer or reader for a given stream falls back to the
null device for that one stream.

symbols.name: StdioCaptureFailed

code.public: Could not deliver the captured output to the writer

symbols.doc:
StdioCaptureFailed is returned from Wait when a StdioCapture copier could
not deliver the child's stdout/stderr to the caller's writer (the writer
itself errored), even though the process exited cleanly.

symbols.name: StdioInherit
symbols.doc:
StdioInherit shares the parent's stdin/stdout/stderr with the child — the
default, and the only behaviour that existed before per-process wiring.

symbols.name: StdioMode
symbols.doc:
StdioMode selects how a spawned child's standard streams are wired. The zero
value is StdioInherit, preserving the historical behaviour where the child
shares the parent's stdin/stdout/stderr (systemd StandardOutput=/StandardInput=
is the analogue, but the choice is generic to anything that spawns processes).

symbols.name: Known
symbols.doc:
Known reports whether m is one of the defined StdioInherit/StdioNull/StdioCapture
modes (i.e. m <= StdioCapture).

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc:
String returns the lowercase mode name ("inherit", "null", "capture"), or
"stdiomode(N)" for an out-of-range value.

symbols.name: StdioNull
symbols.doc:
StdioNull connects every stream to the platform null device: the child's
output is discarded and its stdin returns EOF immediately.

symbols.name: StopFailed

code.public: Could not stop the process

symbols.doc:
StopFailed is returned when a graceful stop cannot terminate the process
group even after escalating to SIGKILL.

symbols.name: SubreaperFailed

code.public: Could not enable child-subreaper mode

symbols.doc:
SubreaperFailed is returned when prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER) fails arming
subreaper semantics for a non-PID1 supervisor.

symbols.name: UnknownGroup

code.public: The requested group does not exist

symbols.doc:
UnknownGroup is returned when a Spec names a Group or supplementary group
that does not resolve to a gid on the host.

symbols.name: UnknownResource

code.public: Unknown or unsupported resource limit

symbols.doc:
UnknownResource is returned by Apply when a Resource has no RLIMIT_*
mapping on the platform.

symbols.name: UnknownSignal

code.public: Unknown signal name or number

symbols.doc:
UnknownSignal is returned by Parse when the name or number is not in the
platform signal table.

symbols.name: UnknownUser

code.public: The requested user does not exist

symbols.doc:
UnknownUser is returned when a Spec names a User that does not resolve to a
uid on the host.

symbols.name: UnsupportedPlatform

code.public: This operation is not supported on this platform

symbols.doc:
UnsupportedPlatform is returned by a primitive invoked on an operating
system that cannot provide it; the no-op stub returns it, never a panic.

symbols.name: WaitFailed

code.public: Could not wait for the process to exit

symbols.doc:
WaitFailed is returned when wait4 fails reaping the leader — a host fault,
not a normal non-zero exit (reported via ExitValue instead).

symbols.name: Closed

code.public: The private socket is closed

symbols.doc: Closed reports an Accept on a closed listener.

symbols.name: CodeClosed
symbols.doc: CodeClosed identifies an Accept on a listener that was closed.

symbols.name: CodeDialFailed
symbols.doc: CodeDialFailed identifies a dial that did not reach a listener.

symbols.name: CodeDirectoryUnsafe
symbols.doc:
CodeDirectoryUnsafe identifies a socket directory another account could
plant an entry in or read through: not a directory, a link, not owned by
this process's user, or writable by its group or by anyone.

symbols.name: CodeEndpointForeign
symbols.doc:
CodeEndpointForeign identifies a socket file owned by another account: a
client refuses to talk to what may be an impostor.

symbols.name: CodeInUse
symbols.doc: CodeInUse identifies a socket path a live process already answers on.

symbols.name: CodeListenFailed
symbols.doc: CodeListenFailed identifies a listen the kernel refused.

symbols.name: CodeMisconfigured
symbols.doc:
CodeMisconfigured identifies a configuration no endpoint can be built from:
an empty or relative path, one longer than the kernel's sun_path, a UID or
GID list holding a negative value.

symbols.name: CodePathUnsafe
symbols.doc:
CodePathUnsafe identifies a socket path another account could steer: a
component ABOVE the socket's directory, or the directory holding it, lets
another account decide where the path leads — a link planted where anybody
can write, a directory another account created there, or an entry anybody
can replace. The socket directory's own entry stays [CodeDirectoryUnsafe]'s.

It is its own code, as LOCK_PATH_REDIRECTED is lock's (ADR 0083), because
the remedy differs: DIRECTORY_UNSAFE asks for a chmod or a chown, this asks
a human to look at a component that may be an attack in progress — or to
move the socket under the directory the engine's RuntimeDir names.

symbols.name: CodePeerRefused
symbols.doc:
CodePeerRefused identifies a peer whose kernel-reported identity is not
this process's user nor in the allow-lists.

symbols.name: Conn

fields.name: Peer
fields.doc: Peer is who connected (for a listener) or who listens (for a dialer).

symbols.doc:
Conn is a connection with its peer's identity: what a Listener's Accept
returns to a listener and a Dialer's Dial to a client, Peer naming the
other end.

symbols.name: DialFailed

code.public: The private socket did not answer

symbols.doc: DialFailed reports a dial that reached no listener.

symbols.name: Dialer
symbols.doc:
Dialer is the connecting end of a private socket: it reaches the listener
its configuration names and refuses — before a byte is sent — an endpoint
it cannot trust. It is frozen at one method (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: Dial
symbols.doc:
Dial connects within ctx. Peer names the listener where the kernel
does; a listener of an account that is not admitted is refused.

symbols.name: DirectoryUnsafe

code.public: The private socket's directory is not private

symbols.doc: DirectoryUnsafe refuses a socket directory another account could reach.

symbols.name: EndpointForeign

code.public: The private socket belongs to another account

symbols.doc: EndpointForeign refuses a socket file another account owns.

symbols.name: InUse

code.public: Another process already listens on this private socket

symbols.doc: InUse refuses to listen where a live process already answers.

symbols.name: ListenFailed

code.public: The private socket could not be opened

symbols.doc: ListenFailed reports a listen the kernel refused.

symbols.name: Listener
symbols.spelled: interface{Accept() (*Conn, error); Addr() net.Addr; Close() error; Path() string; Refused() int64}
symbols.canonical: interface{Accept() (*github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/proc/ipc.Conn, error); Addr() net.Addr; Close() error; Path() string; Refused() int64}
symbols.doc:
Listener is the accepting end of a private socket: it hands out the
connections of admitted peers only, and closes and counts the others.

It is frozen at these five methods (ADR 0039): a method added to a
published interface breaks every double a caller wrote, so a capability
that comes later is a sibling interface a Listener may also implement.

symbols.name: Accept
symbols.doc:
Accept returns the next connection of an admitted peer. A peer the
kernel names and the configuration does not admit is closed at once,
counted by Refused, and never returned. After Close it returns the
CLOSED sentinel.

symbols.name: Addr
symbols.doc: Addr is the endpoint's address.

symbols.name: Close
symbols.doc: Close stops accepting and releases the endpoint.

symbols.name: Path
symbols.doc:
