pool into an allocator that never recycles.

symbols.name: NewPool
symbols.doc:
NewPool returns a [Pool] whose factory newFn builds a value whenever Get
finds the pool empty. A nil newFn panics here, rather than at the first
empty Get far from this call.

symbols.name: Pool
symbols.doc:
Pool is a typed object pool over sync.Pool. [Pool].Get borrows a value,
building one with the factory when the pool is empty, and [Pool].Put hands
one back; a caller must not touch a value after Put. It resets nothing — a
caller resets before Put, or uses [CappedPool].

Safe for concurrent use; always used behind the pointer [NewPool] returns.

symbols.name: Group
symbols.doc:
Group deduplicates concurrent calls that name the same key. The zero value is
ready to use; a Group must not be copied after first use, and is safe for
any number of goroutines.

[Group].Do runs fn for a key unless the same key is already in flight, in
which case it waits for that call instead; it returns the value, whether the
result came from a call this goroutine did not start (shared), and the
error. fn receives the shared call's context, not the caller's — see the
package documentation. A caller whose ctx ends while it waits returns
ctx.Err() and leaves the call running; a result already available is
delivered even if ctx is also done.

[Group].Forget retires a key so the NEXT Do starts a fresh call — for an
in-flight call known to answer a question that has since changed; callers
already waiting keep waiting and still receive its result.

[Group].InFlight reports how many keys a Do arriving now would join rather
than start — a point-in-time reading for a gauge or a test, never for a
decision, and not a count of running calls (a forgotten or abandoned call
may still run).

symbols.name: PanicValue
symbols.doc:
PanicValue carries a panic raised inside a deduplicated call to every caller
waiting on it: Raised is the value the panic carried, verbatim, and Stack the
stack of the goroutine that ran fn, captured at recovery. Its String method
renders both, so an uncaught re-raise prints fn's stack rather than only the
waiter's.

It is deliberately NOT an error, and carries no error code: a panic is a
programming fault, not a runtime condition.

symbols.name: NewValue
symbols.doc:
NewValue returns a [Value] holding initial — call-site sugar for a value
known up front. A nil initial leaves it empty, as the zero value is.

symbols.name: Value
symbols.doc:
Value is a copy-on-write container for a *T. The zero value is ready to use
and holds nil until the first Store.

[Value].Load returns the current pointer without a lock — one atomic load,
no allocation — and the pointer it returns must be treated as immutable.
[Value].Store replaces it, [Value].Swap replaces it and returns the previous
one, and [Value].Update runs a function from the current pointer to the
next under the writers' lock, so a concurrent writer can never interleave
with the read-modify-write. Writers serialise; readers never wait.

symbols.name: Every
symbols.doc:
Every starts a [LoopDaemon] whose loop calls tick on each interval until
Stop is called, or until the channel given by [WithDone] is closed. The
daemon owns the ticker — the wall clock unless [WithClock] names another —
and stops it when the loop ends, so Stop both ends the ticking and joins
the goroutine. A tick due while the previous one still runs is dropped.

A nil tick and a non-positive interval panic here, at the caller.

symbols.name: EveryOption
symbols.doc:
EveryOption tunes [Every]: [WithClock] and [WithDone]. Options apply in
order, so a later one wins, and a nil option is skipped.

symbols.name: Loop
symbols.doc:
Loop is the goroutine body a [LoopDaemon] runs. It receives a stop channel,
closed when Stop is called, and MUST return promptly once it is: Stop blocks
until the loop has returned. A Loop MUST NOT panic.

symbols.name: LoopDaemon
symbols.doc:
LoopDaemon is a running background goroutine with an idempotent Stop and a
join. [LoopDaemon].Stop signals the loop to exit and blocks until it has
returned — idempotent, and safe to call from several goroutines.
[LoopDaemon].Done returns the channel closed once the loop has returned, for
a caller that reacts to the end without joining.

Always used behind the pointer [Start], [NewLoopDaemon] or [Every] returns:
it must not be copied.

symbols.name: NewLoopDaemon
symbols.doc:
NewLoopDaemon is [Start] under the New-prefixed name: the same daemon, the
same panic on a nil loop.

symbols.name: Start
symbols.doc:
Start spawns loop in a new goroutine and returns the [LoopDaemon] that
controls it. A nil loop panics here rather than spawning a goroutine that
does nothing.

symbols.name: WithClock
symbols.doc:
WithClock makes [Every] tick on w instead of the wall clock — a
[clock.ManualClock] in a test, advanced past the interval once the ticker is
armed. A nil w is the wall clock.

symbols.name: WithDone
symbols.doc:
WithDone ends the loop of [Every] as soon as done is closed, without waiting
for Stop, which still joins — returning at once on a loop that has already
left. A nil done never fires.

symbols.name: AESGCM
symbols.doc: AESGCM is the default algorithm: AES-256-GCM. Active out of the box.

symbols.name: Algorithm
symbols.doc:
Algorithm is the stable identifier of an AEAD scheme. Use it with SealAs. It
is a defined type distinct from the other crypto-family Algorithm types (hash,
mac, sign, …), so the compiler rejects feeding a hash or signature constant
into an AEAD call (V104) — the seven registries are separate keyspaces, and
the type system now enforces that separation the way typed Format/Level
discipline does elsewhere.

symbols.name: Key
symbols.doc:
Key is an opaque, redacting 256-bit symmetric key. Build one with NewKey; its
String output is always "<redacted>".

symbols.name: KeyLen
symbols.doc: KeyLen is the required symmetric key length in bytes (256-bit).

symbols.name: NewKey
symbols.doc:
NewKey builds a Key from raw, which must be exactly KeyLen (32) bytes. A wrong
length returns InvalidKey; the bytes are copied defensively.

symbols.name: Open
symbols.spelled: func(k Key, box []byte, aad []byte) (plaintext []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
Open decrypts a box produced by Seal/SealAs under k, verifying aad, and
returns the plaintext. The algorithm is read from the box — the caller never
names it. Any failure returns the single non-oracle DecryptionFailed.

symbols.name: OpenStream
symbols.spelled: func(src io.Reader, k Key, aad []byte) (opened io.Reader, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(src io.Reader, k github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto.Key, aad []byte) (opened io.Reader, err error)
symbols.doc:
OpenStream wraps src so reads are opened under k with aad, decrypting the
chunked stream produced by SealStream. The returned io.Reader never surfaces a
chunk's plaintext before it authenticates, returns EOF only after the final
chunk verifies, and surfaces a truncated stream as StreamTruncated. Pass nil
aad when unused.

symbols.name: Seal
symbols.spelled: func(k Key, plaintext []byte, aad []byte) (box []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
Seal encrypts plaintext under k using the default algorithm (AES-256-GCM),
binding aad, and returns a self-describing box. The nonce is generated and
embedded for you. Pass nil aad when unused.

symbols.name: SealAs
symbols.spelled: func(a Algorithm, k Key, plaintext []byte, aad []byte) (box []byte, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(a github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto.Algorithm, k github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto.Key, plaintext []byte, aad []byte) (box []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
SealAs is Seal with an explicit algorithm — e.g. a scheme activated by its own
blank import. An unregistered algorithm returns UnknownAlgorithm.

symbols.name: SealStream
symbols.spelled: func(dst io.Writer, k Key, aad []byte) (sealed io.WriteCloser, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(dst io.Writer, k github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto.Key, aad []byte) (sealed io.WriteCloser, err error)
symbols.doc:
SealStream wraps dst so writes are sealed under k with aad in fixed 64 KiB
authenticated chunks. The returned io.WriteCloser buffers and seals chunks as
they fill; Close writes the final authenticated chunk and MUST be called to
produce a valid stream. Pass nil aad when unused.

symbols.name: UnwrapKey
symbols.spelled: func(passphrase []byte, envelope string) (dek Key, err error)
symbols.doc:
UnwrapKey recovers the data key sealed in envelope under passphrase. A
structurally invalid envelope returns InvalidKeyEnvelope; a wrong passphrase
returns the non-oracle DecryptionFailed.

symbols.name: WrapKey
symbols.spelled: func(passphrase []byte, dek Key) (envelope string, err error)
symbols.doc:
WrapKey seals the data key dek at rest under passphrase, returning the frozen
"$kenv$" envelope string. The KEK is stretched from passphrase with
PBKDF2-SHA256 and the dek is sealed under AES-256-GCM; the envelope header is
bound as AAD so tampering is detected on UnwrapKey.

symbols.name: XChaCha20Poly1305
symbols.doc:
XChaCha20Poly1305 is the 192-bit-nonce AEAD, preferred for high-volume
random-nonce workloads. Pass it to SealAs after a blank import of
third-party/x-crypto/xchacha (which alone pulls golang.org/x/crypto):

	import _ "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/third-party/x-crypto/xchacha"
	box, _ := crypto.SealAs(crypto.XChaCha20Poly1305, k, pt, aad)

symbols.name: Algorithm
symbols.doc:
Algorithm is the stable identifier of a key-agreement scheme. It is a defined
type distinct from the other crypto-family Algorithm types (hash, mac, sign,
…), so the compiler rejects feeding a hash or signature constant into an
agreement call (V104) — the seven registries are separate keyspaces, and the
type system now enforces that separation the way typed Format/Level discipline
does elsewhere.

symbols.name: GenerateKey
symbols.doc:
GenerateKey draws a fresh keypair for the named scheme, returning the raw
public and private key bytes. An unregistered algorithm returns
UnknownAgreementAlgorithm; treat priv as a secret and zero it when done.

symbols.name: Key
symbols.doc:
Key is an opaque, redacting 256-bit symmetric key — the same key type the AEAD
surface uses. SharedKey returns one; its String output is "<redacted>".

symbols.name: KeyLen
symbols.doc:
KeyLen is the required symmetric key length in bytes (256-bit) — the length of
the Key SharedKey returns and that [NewKey] enforces.

symbols.name: NewKey
symbols.doc:
NewKey builds a Key from raw, which must be exactly KeyLen (32) bytes. A wrong
length returns InvalidKey; the bytes are copied defensively. Use it to
round-trip a SharedKey-shaped value without importing an unrelated facade.

symbols.name: SharedKey
symbols.spelled: func(a Algorithm, priv []byte, peerPub []byte, info string) (key Key, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(a github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto/agree.Algorithm, priv []byte, peerPub []byte, info string) (key github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto/agree.Key, err error)
symbols.doc:
SharedKey derives a redacting 32-byte symmetric Key from priv and peerPub for
the named scheme, binding info as HKDF domain separation. The raw DH secret is
HKDF'd and never returned. An unregistered scheme returns
UnknownAgreementAlgorithm; a low-order/garbage peerPub returns AgreementFailed.

symbols.name: X25519
symbols.doc: X25519 is Diffie-Hellman over Curve25519 (RFC 7748) — the modern default.

symbols.name: Algorithm
symbols.doc:
Algorithm is the stable identifier of a hash scheme. It is a defined type
distinct from the other crypto-family Algorithm types (mac, sign, kdf, …), so
the compiler rejects feeding a MAC or signature constant into a hash call
(V104) — the seven registries are separate keyspaces, and the type system now
enforces that separation the way typed Format/Level discipline does elsewhere.

symbols.name: CRC32C
symbols.doc: CRC32C is CRC-32C (Castagnoli): a fast NON-cryptographic checksum.

symbols.name: DigestWriter
symbols.doc:
DigestWriter tees writes into both a destination io.Writer and a running hash,
exposing the digest of everything written so far. See [NewDigestWriter].

symbols.name: FNV1a64
symbols.doc: FNV1a64 is FNV-1a 64-bit: a fast NON-cryptographic fingerprint.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New returns a fresh streaming hash.Hash for the named algorithm, for io.Copy
over large inputs. An unregistered algorithm returns UnknownHashAlgorithm.

symbols.name: NewDigestWriter
symbols.spelled: func(a Algorithm, dst io.Writer) (writer *DigestWriter, err error)
symbols.doc:
NewDigestWriter returns a DigestWriter that tees writes into dst while hashing
them under the named algorithm, so the content-address digest of everything
written is available via Sum/SumHex. An unregistered algorithm returns
UnknownHashAlgorithm.

symbols.name: NewVerifyingReader
symbols.spelled: func(a Algorithm, src io.Reader, wantHex string) (reader *VerifyingReader, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(a github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto/hash.Algorithm, src io.Reader, wantHex string) (reader *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto/hash.VerifyingReader, err error)
symbols.doc:
NewVerifyingReader returns a VerifyingReader over src that hashes the stream
under the named algorithm and verifies it against wantHex on the final (EOF)
read — a public-digest, non-oracle, EOF-typed check that never fails
mid-stream. An unregistered algorithm returns UnknownHashAlgorithm; a digest
mismatch surfaces as DigestMismatch only at EOF.

symbols.name: SHA256
symbols.doc: SHA256 is SHA-256: a 256-bit cryptographic digest for content addressing.

symbols.name: SHA3256
symbols.doc: SHA3256 is SHA3-256: the Keccak-family 256-bit cryptographic digest.

symbols.name: SHA512
symbols.doc: SHA512 is SHA-512: a 512-bit cryptographic digest.

symbols.name: Sum

algorithm returns UnknownHashAlgorithm.

symbols.name: SumHex

SumHex returns Sum as canonical lowercase hex — the frozen string form for
content IDs and cache keys.

symbols.name: VerifyingReader
symbols.doc:
VerifyingReader wraps a source reader and verifies its digest against an
expected value on the final (EOF) read. See [NewVerifyingReader].

symbols.name: Algorithm
symbols.doc:
Algorithm is the stable identifier of a key-derivation scheme. It is a defined
type distinct from the other crypto-family Algorithm types (hash, mac, sign,
…), so the compiler rejects feeding a hash or MAC constant into a KDF call
(V104) — the seven registries are separate keyspaces, and the type system now
enforces that separation the way typed Format/Level discipline does elsewhere.

symbols.name: HKDFSHA256
symbols.doc:
HKDFSHA256 is HKDF (RFC 5869) over SHA-256 — extract-and-expand for key
separation from a strong secret.

symbols.name: Key
symbols.doc:
Key is an opaque, redacting 256-bit symmetric key — the master a KeyTree
derives from and the type DeriveKey returns. Build one with [NewKey].

symbols.name: KeyLen
symbols.doc:
KeyLen is the required symmetric key length in bytes (256-bit) — the length
[NewKey] enforces.

symbols.name: KeyTree
symbols.doc:
KeyTree is the path-addressed hierarchical key-derivation node, re-exported
from the service layer. Build one with NewKeyTree; Child descends a path and
DeriveKey yields a 32-byte key at the current node.

symbols.name: NewKey
symbols.doc:
NewKey builds a Key from raw, which must be exactly KeyLen (32) bytes. A wrong
length returns InvalidKey; the bytes are copied defensively. Use it to build
the master a KeyTree derives from without importing an unrelated facade.

symbols.name: NewKeyTree
symbols.doc:
NewKeyTree returns the root KeyTree for master, deriving children under algo.
The master Key is shared by reference across children — the root owns its
Zeroize lifetime, so zeroizing master invalidates every derived node.

symbols.name: Subkey
symbols.spelled: func(a Algorithm, secret []byte, salt []byte, info string, length int) (subkey []byte, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(a github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto/kdf.Algorithm, secret []byte, salt []byte, info string, length int) (subkey []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
Subkey derives a length-byte subkey from secret using the named scheme. salt
is optional domain randomness (nil is allowed); info is a context label that
binds the subkey to its purpose. An unregistered algorithm returns
UnknownKDFAlgorithm; an over-long length returns DerivationFailed.

symbols.name: Algorithm
symbols.doc:
Algorithm is the stable identifier of a MAC scheme. It is a defined type
distinct from the other crypto-family Algorithm types (hash, sign, kdf, …), so
the compiler rejects feeding a hash or signature constant into a MAC call
(V104) — the seven registries are separate keyspaces, and the type system now
enforces that separation the way typed Format/Level discipline does elsewhere.

symbols.name: HMACSHA256
symbols.doc: HMACSHA256 is HMAC (RFC 2104) over SHA-256 — the detached-MAC default.

symbols.name: Key
symbols.doc:
Key is an opaque, redacting 256-bit symmetric key — the same key type used by
the AEAD surface. Build one with [NewKey]; its String output is "<redacted>".

symbols.name: KeyLen
symbols.doc:
KeyLen is the required symmetric key length in bytes (256-bit) — the length
[NewKey] enforces.

symbols.name: NewKey
symbols.doc:
NewKey builds a Key from raw, which must be exactly KeyLen (32) bytes. A wrong
length returns InvalidKey; the bytes are copied defensively.

symbols.name: Tag
symbols.spelled: func(a Algorithm, key Key, message []byte) (tag []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
Tag returns the authentication tag over message under key for the named
scheme. An unregistered algorithm returns UnknownMACAlgorithm; a registered
scheme cannot fail (the redacting Key pins the length).

symbols.name: Verify
symbols.spelled: func(a Algorithm, key Key, message []byte, tag []byte) (ok bool, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(a github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto/mac.Algorithm, key github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto/mac.Key, message []byte, tag []byte) (ok bool, err error)
symbols.doc:
Verify reports whether tag authenticates message under key for the named
scheme, using a constant-time comparison. An unregistered algorithm returns
(false, UnknownMACAlgorithm); a bad tag is (false, nil).

symbols.name: Algorithm
symbols.doc:
Algorithm is the stable identifier of a password-hashing scheme; it is also
the PHC id segment of hashes that scheme produces. It is a defined type
distinct from the other crypto-family Algorithm types (hash, mac, kdf, …), so
the compiler rejects feeding a hash or KDF constant into a password call
(V104) — the seven registries are separate keyspaces, and the type system now
enforces that separation the way typed Format/Level discipline does elsewhere.

symbols.name: Hash
symbols.spelled: func(a Algorithm, password []byte) (phc string, err error)
symbols.doc:
Hash returns a PHC-string hash of password using the named scheme, with a
fresh random salt and the scheme's current cost parameters. An unregistered
algorithm returns UnknownPasswordAlgorithm. Store the returned string as-is.

symbols.name: IsCommon
symbols.doc:
IsCommon reports whether password is one of the ten thousand most common
passwords, compared case-insensitively — PASSWORD as password. The empty
password is not: refusing it is a length rule's job.

symbols.name: NeedsRehash
symbols.doc:
NeedsRehash reports whether the stored PHC hash was produced with cost
parameters weaker than its scheme's current policy — call it after a
successful Verify to transparently upgrade the stored hash.

symbols.name: PBKDF2SHA256
symbols.doc: PBKDF2SHA256 is PBKDF2-SHA256 — the stdlib password stretcher (RFC 8018).

symbols.name: Verify
symbols.spelled: func(password []byte, phc string) (ok bool, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(password []byte, phc string) (ok bool, err error)
symbols.doc:
Verify reports whether password matches the stored PHC hash, comparing in
constant time. The scheme is read from phc. A malformed phc or unregistered
scheme returns an error; a genuine mismatch is (false, nil).

symbols.name: Algorithm
symbols.doc:
Algorithm is the stable identifier of a signature scheme. It is a defined type
distinct from the other crypto-family Algorithm types (hash, mac, kdf, …), so
the compiler rejects feeding a hash or MAC constant into a signature call
(V104) — the seven registries are separate keyspaces, and the type system now
enforces that separation the way typed Format/Level discipline does elsewhere.

symbols.name: ECDSAP256
symbols.doc:
ECDSAP256 is ECDSA over NIST P-256 with SHA-256 and ASN.1/DER signatures — the
interoperable choice for JWT/X.509 ecosystems. Keys are DER-marshalled.

symbols.name: Ed25519
symbols.doc:
Ed25519 is the EdDSA signature scheme over Curve25519 (RFC 8032): a 256-bit
public key, fast constant-time verification, and no parameter choices.

symbols.name: GenerateKey
symbols.doc:
GenerateKey draws a fresh keypair for the named scheme, returning the public
and private key bytes. An unregistered algorithm returns
UnknownSignatureAlgorithm; treat priv as a secret.

symbols.name: Sign
symbols.spelled: func(a Algorithm, priv []byte, message []byte) (sig []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
Sign returns a detached signature over message using priv under the named
scheme. An unregistered algorithm returns UnknownSignatureAlgorithm; a
malformed priv returns SigningFailed.

symbols.name: Verify
symbols.spelled: func(a Algorithm, pub []byte, message []byte, sig []byte) (ok bool, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(a github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/crypto/sign.Algorithm, pub []byte, message []byte, sig []byte) (ok bool, err error)
symbols.doc:
Verify reports whether sig is a valid signature for message under pub for the
named scheme. An unregistered algorithm returns
(false, UnknownSignatureAlgorithm); an invalid signature is (false, nil).

symbols.name: BackendFailed

code.public: The cache backend could not serve the operation

symbols.doc:
BackendFailed is returned when a store could not serve an operation. A
MISS is not this: a miss is (zero, false, nil).

symbols.name: Cache
symbols.doc: Cache is the public alias for the generic LRU+TTL primitive.

symbols.name: ChainConfig
symbols.doc: ChainConfig parameterises [NewChain].

symbols.name: ChainMisconfigured

code.public: The cache chain cannot be built from the given tiers

symbols.doc:
ChainMisconfigured is returned by [NewChain] for a tier set it cannot
honour.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc: Config is the public alias for the primitive's constructor configuration.

symbols.name: Entry
symbols.doc:
Entry is what a caller stores: the value, its lifetime, and the tags by
which it can later be invalidated in bulk.

symbols.name: EntryFetcher
symbols.doc:
EntryFetcher is the sibling that returns the whole entry — value, REMAINING
TTL, tags — rather than only the value. Both stores built here implement it.

symbols.name: EntryRejected

code.public: The cache entry is not storable as given

symbols.doc:
EntryRejected is returned by Set for an entry no store can represent —
an empty key, an empty tag, or a negative TTL other than [NoExpiry].

symbols.name: Fill
symbols.doc:
Fill computes the entry for a key the cache does not hold: a query, a
request, a derivation. It is your code.

symbols.name: FillFailed

code.public: The cache fill function failed and nothing was stored

symbols.doc:
FillFailed is returned by Load when your fill fails and its error
carries no SDK code of its own. Nothing is stored: caching a failure
turns one bad minute at the origin into a full TTL of confident wrong
answers.

symbols.name: Loader
symbols.doc:
Loader is the sibling that fills a miss while collapsing concurrent misses
on one key into a single fill — within one process, and not across replicas.
See the package documentation before sizing an origin against it.

symbols.name: MemoryConfig
symbols.doc:
MemoryConfig parameterises [NewMemory]. Its zero value is NOT a working
cache — MaxEntries must be stated, and is refused rather than defaulted.

symbols.name: Misconfigured

code.public: The cache cannot be built from the given configuration

symbols.doc:
Misconfigured is returned by a store constructor whose configuration it
cannot honour — a non-positive capacity, a negative default TTL.

symbols.name: New
symbols.spelled: func[K comparable, V any](cfg Config[K, V]) *Cache[K, V]
symbols.canonical: func[K comparable, V any](cfg github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/cache.Config[K, V]) *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/cache.Cache[K, V]
symbols.doc: New builds a [Cache] from cfg. A nil cfg.Clock defaults to the system clock.

symbols.name: NewChain
symbols.spelled: func[V any](cfg ChainConfig, tiers ...Store[V]) (store Store[V], err error)
symbols.doc:
NewChain puts each store in front of the next: tiers[0] is consulted first,
the last is the authority. A hit in a far tier is promoted into every nearer
one, carrying its REMAINING TTL and its tags.

Every tier must implement [EntryFetcher] and [Tagger], checked here and
refused rather than discovered per call: a value promoted without its tags
is one [Tagger] can no longer reach, so an invalidation would report success
while a nearer tier kept serving the entry.

symbols.name: NewMemory
symbols.spelled: func[V any](cfg MemoryConfig) (store Store[V], err error)
symbols.doc:
NewMemory builds an in-process store: an LRU with TTL, a tag index, and
stampede protection on Load.

The returned [Store] also implements [EntryFetcher], [Tagger] and [Loader].

A non-positive MaxEntries is REFUSED, not defaulted. A capacity is the whole
statement of how much memory you are willing to spend, so any number chosen
for you would be arbitrary — and the value a zero would naturally mean,
unbounded, is the dangerous one.

symbols.name: NoExpiry
symbols.doc:
NoExpiry is the [Entry].TTL that stores an entry with no deadline.

It is deliberately distinct from the zero TTL, which means "use the store's
default". A store with a one-minute default holding one entry that must
never expire is a real combination, and reading both meanings out of 0 would
make the second one unsayable.

symbols.name: Stats
symbols.doc: Stats is the public alias for the primitive's counters snapshot.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.doc:
Store is the cache port: Fetch, Set, Delete.

The method set is FROZEN at three. New capabilities arrive as SIBLING
interfaces you reach by type assertion — [EntryFetcher], [Tagger] and
[Loader] — because this alias publishes the interface, Go interfaces are
structural, and a fourth method would break every downstream implementer at
compile time with no deprecation window.

symbols.name: Tagger
symbols.doc:
Tagger is the sibling for invalidating every entry carrying a tag.

The cost is proportional to the entries carrying the tag, not to the size of
the store — measured in internal/service/data/cache/BENCH.md at two store sizes.

symbols.name: TierFailed

code.public: A tier of the cache chain could not serve the operation

symbols.doc:
TierFailed is returned when a chained operation failed inside one tier.
Its fields name the position, because a chain's caller holds one Store
and would otherwise have no way to tell which backend broke.

symbols.name: ASCII85
symbols.doc: ASCII85 denotes the JSON-mediated Adobe Ascii85 text-safe wrap.

symbols.name: ASN1DER
symbols.doc: ASN1DER denotes the stdlib encoding/asn1 DER wire format.

symbols.name: Available
symbols.doc: Available returns the sorted list of registered formats.

symbols.name: BSON
symbols.doc:
BSON denotes the MongoDB binary document format (top-level must be a
document — struct or map — not a scalar). ADR 0021.

symbols.name: Base16
symbols.doc: Base16 denotes the JSON-mediated base16 (uppercase hex) wrap.

symbols.name: Base32
symbols.doc: Base32 denotes the JSON-mediated base32 (std) text-safe wrap.

symbols.name: Base45
symbols.doc: Base45 denotes the JSON-mediated RFC 9285 Base45 wrap (QR-code safe).

symbols.name: Base58
symbols.doc:
Base58 denotes the JSON-mediated Bitcoin Base58 wrap (short inputs;
base-conversion is O(n²) so a 4 KiB input cap applies).

symbols.name: Base62
symbols.doc:
Base62 denotes the JSON-mediated Base62 wrap (short inputs; same O(n²)
4 KiB input cap as Base58).

symbols.name: Base64
symbols.doc: Base64 denotes the JSON-mediated base64 (std) text-safe wrap.

symbols.name: Base64URL
symbols.doc: Base64URL denotes the JSON-mediated base64 (URL-safe alphabet) wrap.

symbols.name: CBOR
symbols.doc:
CBOR denotes the RFC 8949 wire format, encoded and decoded on the
standard library alone.

symbols.name: CSV
symbols.doc: CSV denotes the stdlib encoding/csv wire format.

symbols.name: CodeCodecUnavailable
symbols.doc:
CodeCodecUnavailable fires when a codec entry exists but is unusable
(e.g., blank import missing or build tag not active).

symbols.name: CodePromoteFailed
symbols.doc:
CodePromoteFailed fires when the facade's JSON-bridge promotion path
cannot serve the request (unknown Format with no promotion strategy,
or a malformed container after the codec populated it).

symbols.name: CodeStreamingUnsupported
symbols.doc:
CodeStreamingUnsupported fires when NewEncoder / NewDecoder is called on
a codec that does not implement StreamingCodec.

symbols.name: CodeUnknownFormat
symbols.doc: CodeUnknownFormat fires when a Format is not registered in the registry.

symbols.name: Codec
symbols.doc: Codec re-exports core/data/codec.Codec for consumers who want direct access.

symbols.name: CodecUnavailable

code.public: codec is registered but unavailable

symbols.doc:
CodecUnavailable is returned when the registry entry exists but the
codec itself cannot be used (reserved for future gating).

symbols.name: CompressAlgorithm
symbols.doc:
CompressAlgorithm is the transform package's Algorithm, so consumers name a
compressor without importing internal/*. Use the Gzip / Flate constants.

symbols.name: Decoder
symbols.doc: Decoder re-exports core/data/codec.Decoder for streaming callers.

symbols.name: Encoder
symbols.doc: Encoder re-exports core/data/codec.Encoder for streaming callers.

symbols.name: FlatBuffers
symbols.doc:
FlatBuffers denotes the passthrough codec for already-encoded
FlatBuffer payloads — schema-typed reads stay in the caller's
flatc-generated accessors.

symbols.name: Flate
symbols.doc: Flate selects the raw-DEFLATE compressor (frame algID 0x02).

symbols.name: Form
symbols.doc:
Form denotes application/x-www-form-urlencoded, the encoding every
HTML form POSTs. Its native Go shape is url.Values: a repeated key
carries multiple values, which is the only array syntax the format
has.

symbols.name: Format
symbols.doc: Format re-exports core/data/codec.Format so consumers only depend on pkg/v1.

symbols.name: FromExtension
symbols.doc: FromExtension resolves a file extension to its registered Format.

symbols.name: FromMIME
symbols.doc: FromMIME resolves a MIME string to its registered Format.

symbols.name: Gzip
symbols.doc: Gzip selects the gzip compressor (frame algID 0x01).

symbols.name: Hex
symbols.doc: Hex denotes the JSON-mediated lowercase-hex text-safe wrap.

symbols.name: JSON
symbols.doc: JSON denotes the stdlib encoding/json wire format.

symbols.name: Marshal
symbols.spelled: func(f Format, v any) (encoded []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
Marshal serialises v using the codec registered under f. The codec's
native input shape is tried first (fast path, zero overhead); if the
codec rejects v as the wrong shape (csv requires [][]string, pem
requires *pem.Block, etc.) the facade promotes v via json-encode +
codec-specific wrap so every Format accepts any Go value — see
promote.go for the per-format strategies and the uniform-contract
rationale.

symbols.name: MarshalCompressed
symbols.spelled: func(f Format, algo CompressAlgorithm, v any) (box []byte, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(f github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/codec.Format, algo github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/codec.CompressAlgorithm, v any) (box []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
MarshalCompressed serialises v with the codec registered under f, compresses
the result with the transform registered under algo, and wraps both in a
self-describing frame so UnmarshalCompressed needs no Format or Algorithm
argument. It returns UnknownCompressor when algo has no frame id or no
registered body, CompressedFrameInvalid when f exceeds the addressable length,
and forwards any codec / compressor error untouched (origin wins).

symbols.name: MarshalMany
symbols.spelled: func(v any, formats ...Format) (encodedByFormat map[Format][]byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
MarshalMany serialises v into every format in formats and returns a
map keyed by Format with the encoded bytes. The same logical value
goes out in N different wire encodings — handy for HTTP content
negotiation, multi-protocol message buses, archival doubling, or
cross-region replication where each region speaks a different
codec.

Per-format errors are joined under [errors.Join] and returned as a
single error; partial results stay in the returned map so callers
can decide whether to ship the formats that succeeded or fail the
whole batch. An unknown Format in the list surfaces
[UnknownFormat] / [CodeUnknownFormat] inside that joined error
(and leaves no entry in the map for that Format).

Calling with formats == nil (or empty) returns an empty map and no
error — the no-op semantics mirror calling Marshal zero times.

	out, err := codec.MarshalMany(payload, codec.JSON, codec.CBOR, codec.MsgPack)
	// out[codec.JSON], out[codec.CBOR], out[codec.MsgPack] all populated
	// when err == nil.

symbols.name: MsgPack
symbols.doc:
MsgPack denotes the MessagePack wire format (msgpack.org specification),
implemented natively on the standard library.

symbols.name: Multipart
symbols.doc:
Multipart denotes RFC 7578 multipart/form-data. Its native Go shape is
a [MultipartForm] of [MultipartPart] sections; any other value travels
as a single JSON-mediated part. The RFC 2046 boundary lives in the
Content-Type header, which the Codec contract cannot carry — the codec
re-emits it in the body, and [MultipartContentType] recovers the header
value from the bytes Marshal returned.

symbols.name: MultipartContentType
symbols.doc:
MultipartContentType returns the Content-Type header value —
"multipart/form-data; boundary=…", quoted when the boundary needs it — for a
body Marshal(Multipart, …) returned. Send it alongside the bytes: the
boundary is announced in that header, and since the Codec contract has
nowhere to hand one back, it is read off the body's first delimiter line. A
body with no recoverable delimiter is refused with the codec's
BOUNDARY_INVALID.

A caller streaming through NewEncoder(Multipart, w) must set the header
before the first byte instead: the Encoder returned has a Boundary() string
method, and mime.FormatMediaType builds the same value from it.

symbols.name: MultipartForm
symbols.doc:
MultipartForm is the native Go shape of the [Multipart] format: a whole
multipart/form-data body — its RFC 2046 boundary and its parts, in wire
order. Marshal one to build an upload; Unmarshal into a *MultipartForm to
read one. An empty Boundary asks Marshal to generate a delimiter; Unmarshal
always fills it with the one it recovered, so a decode → encode round trip
keeps the original delimiter — and reproduces the whole body byte for byte
only for a body this codec encoded, since a part header other than the name,
filename and media type is not carried through, and a filename is decoded to
its last path element.

symbols.name: MultipartPart
symbols.doc:
MultipartPart is one section of a [MultipartForm]: a named field, optionally
a filename and a media type, and the bytes themselves — a file upload is a
part with FileName and ContentType set. Marshal also accepts a single
MultipartPart or a []MultipartPart.

Name is required. Name, FileName and ContentType are written into the part's
header block, so a CR, an LF or a NUL in any of them is refused — never
escaped — with the codec's VALUE_INVALID naming the field. A UTF-8 filename
is written as-is (RFC 7578 §4.2).

Decoding keeps only a filename's last path element, reading both '/' and '\'
as separators on every operating system — RFC 7578 §4.2 has the receiver
drop the directory information a sender may include, and the sender writes
it with its own separator. `C:\Users\ada\cv.pdf` decodes to `cv.pdf` on
Linux exactly as on Windows. Nothing else is removed, so a caller turning
FileName into a path still validates it first.

symbols.name: NDJSON
symbols.doc: NDJSON denotes the newline-delimited JSON dialect.

symbols.name: Unmarshal
symbols.spelled: func(f Format, data []byte, v any) error
symbols.doc:
Unmarshal parses data into v using the codec registered under f. As
with Marshal, the codec's native target shape is tried first; on
shape mismatch the facade promotes via JSON-bridge so every Format
can decode into any Go target.

symbols.name: UnmarshalCompressed
symbols.doc:
UnmarshalCompressed parses a frame produced by MarshalCompressed, decompresses
the payload under a bomb guard, and decodes it into v using the inner Format
the frame records. A malformed frame, an unknown algorithm id, or a payload
that decompresses past the bomb guard returns CompressedFrameInvalid; codec
and compressor faults are forwarded untouched.

and Close are the engine's own.

declared as for [Open]. It sends no statement: its tables are

symbols.canonical: func(dialect github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/sql.Migration, error)

SQLMigration returns the migration that creates the two tables a SQL store

Filter, Entries, Count, Lookup and Find read; Put, Insert, Replace, Update
and Delete write, and their Stamped forms say what the version they make
records; Versions, Version and RewriteVersions as for [Store]; OnWrite and
OnDelete announce once the write's transaction commits; Reindex files the
stored documents again. Every call takes a context.

in it: run it to turn versions off for good.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.doc:
Store is the public alias for the document store: Get, List, Filter,
Entries, Lookup, Find and Stats read; Put, Insert, Replace, Update and
Delete write, and their Stamped forms say what the version they make
records; Versions and Version read a document's versions, RewriteVersions
rewrites its former ones; OnWrite and OnDelete announce; Fold and Close
bring it to rest.

symbols.name: Broker
symbols.doc:
Broker is the public alias for the queue contract. It is FROZEN at four
methods; capabilities arrive as siblings ([DeadLetterReader],
[LeaseExtender], [Waker], [Rejecter], [DeadLetterManager]) reached by type
assertion.

errors.Is(err, NotRetryable) sees only an origin.

symbols.name: Consume
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, broker Broker, cfg ConsumerConfig) error
symbols.doc:
Consume runs cfg.Handler against broker until ctx is done, on
cfg.Parallelism goroutines it owns.

It returns nil when ctx ends — a cancelled consumer is a stopped consumer,
not a failed one — and returns the broker's error when the STORAGE fails. A
handler's error is never returned: it is nacked, retried, and eventually
dead-lettered, which is the entire point of the domain.

cfg.HandlerIsIdempotent must be true; see the package documentation.

symbols.name: ConsumerConfig
symbols.doc: ConsumerConfig is the public alias for [Consume]'s configuration.

symbols.name: ConsumerMisconfigured

code.public: The consumer configuration is not runnable and was refused

symbols.doc:
ConsumerMisconfigured refuses a consumer with no Handler, or one whose
author has not asserted HandlerIsIdempotent.

symbols.doc: DeadLetter is the public alias for one abandoned message and its cause.

symbols.doc:
DeadLetterManager is the public alias for the capability of replaying a
dead letter into its queue, its count reset, or deleting it. Every broker
here implements it.

code.public: No dead letter has that identifier

symbols.doc:
DeadLetterNotFound refuses a replay or a deletion naming a dead letter
the store does not hold.

symbols.name: DeadLetterReader
symbols.doc:
DeadLetterReader is the public alias for the capability of reading the
dead-letter store back. Every broker here implements it.

symbols.name: DefaultMaxMessageBytes
symbols.doc:
DefaultMaxMessageBytes is the payload bound applied when
[Policy].MaxMessageBytes is left at zero: one mebibyte.

symbols.name: DefaultPollInterval
symbols.doc:
DefaultPollInterval is how long an idle worker waits before asking again
when [ConsumerConfig].PollInterval is left at zero. With a [Waker] broker it
bounds only how late another process's publication is noticed.

symbols.name: Delivery
symbols.doc:
Delivery is the public alias for one message handed to one consumer,
carrying the lease that proves the claim and the count that says whether
this is a retry.

symbols.name: DoNotRetry
symbols.doc:
DoNotRetry marks cause as a failure no retry can fix: returned from a
[Handler], it makes [Consume] dead-letter the message at once, with cause,
instead of handing it back for another attempt. An SDK error keeps its own
reason, code and public words in the dead letter; any other error, or none,
is recorded as [NotRetryable].

symbols.name: FileConfig
symbols.doc: FileConfig is the public alias for [NewFile]'s configuration.

symbols.name: Handler
symbols.doc: Handler is the public alias for the function that processes one delivery.

symbols.name: HandlerPanicked

code.public: The queue handler panicked and was recovered

symbols.doc:
HandlerPanicked reports a recovered handler panic. The message was
nacked and the consumer kept running.

There is deliberately no HandlerFailed beside it: a handler that
returns an error has its error recorded in the dead letter unmodified,
because a verdict wrapped around it would displace the reason whoever
reads that record actually needs.

symbols.name: InvalidBatchSize

code.public: A batch size must be positive

symbols.doc: InvalidBatchSize refuses a non-positive batch size.

symbols.name: Lease
symbols.doc: Lease is the public alias for a consumer's exclusive claim on one message.

symbols.name: LeaseExpired

code.public: The lease on that message has expired and the acknowledgement was ignored

symbols.doc:
LeaseExpired reports an acknowledgement whose lease had already lapsed.
Nothing happened, and the message is elsewhere.

symbols.name: LeaseExtender
symbols.doc:
LeaseExtender is the public alias for the capability of renewing a lease a
handler is still working under. Every broker here implements it.

symbols.name: MaxDeadlineOffset
symbols.doc:
MaxDeadlineOffset is the ceiling on [Policy].VisibilityTimeout and
[Policy].RetryDelay: a century, refused above it rather than clamped,
because a deadline past 2262 cannot be written into the durable broker's
file names and read back.

symbols.name: MaxSQLTableLen
symbols.doc:
MaxSQLTableLen is the longest table name [NewSQL] and [SQLMigration] accept,
in bytes: PostgreSQL's identifier limit.

symbols.name: MemoryConfig
symbols.doc: MemoryConfig is the public alias for [NewMemory]'s configuration.

symbols.name: Message
symbols.doc: Message is the public alias for one unit of work as the broker minted it.

symbols.name: MessageTooLarge

code.public: The message payload exceeds the queue's configured maximum size

symbols.doc:
MessageTooLarge refuses a payload above the policy's bound, at the
producer, where it can still be made smaller.

symbols.name: Nack
symbols.doc:
Nack is the public alias for what [Broker].Nack decided: retried, or
dead-lettered.

symbols.name: NewFile
symbols.doc:
NewFile returns the durable broker: its whole state is the directory in
cfg.Dir, so it survives the process that published into it and two brokers
over one directory are one queue.

It refuses at construction — never at first use — a policy it cannot
honour, a directory it cannot use safely, and a platform with no atomic
replace or no flushable directory handle. Windows is such a platform: after
the directory checks — which read its access control lists there — NewFile
returns the SDK's UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM, matched with
errors.Is(err, proc.UnsupportedPlatform).

The broker holds two directory descriptors and additionally implements
io.Closer, which releases them — reached by type assertion, as the session
file store's is, so Broker grows no method:

	if closer, ok := broker.(io.Closer); ok { defer closer.Close() }

The messages stay on disk; every call after Close fails.

symbols.name: NewMemory
symbols.doc:
NewMemory returns the in-process test double: the port's full semantics,
no directory, no flush, and nothing that survives the process.

It refuses the same policies [NewFile] refuses, through the same guard,
which is what makes it an honest double.

symbols.name: NewSQL
symbols.doc:
NewSQL returns a durable broker whose queue is one table of the caller's
database, created by [SQLMigration]. Every call runs on the transaction its
context carries for cfg.Transactor, so a message published inside that
transaction exists if and only if it commits. It sends no statement.

It refuses at construction — never at first use — a policy it cannot honour
and a transactor, dialect or table it cannot use ([SQLQueueMisconfigured]).
The transactor must be the SDK's, or another core/data/sql Joiner and Deferrer.

symbols.name: NotRetryable

code.public: The message cannot be processed and was dead-lettered without a retry

symbols.doc:
NotRetryable is the failure no retry can fix: what a dead letter
records when [DoNotRetry] marked an error with no public words of its
own, or none at all.

symbols.name: Policy
symbols.doc: Policy is the public alias for the delivery discipline a broker enforces.

symbols.name: QueueBackendFailed

code.public: The queue's storage refused an operation

symbols.doc:
QueueBackendFailed reports a refusal from a durable broker's storage:
the filesystem's, or a statement the SQL broker's database did not
complete.

symbols.name: QueueDirectoryUnusable

code.public: The queue directory cannot be used safely

symbols.doc:
QueueDirectoryUnusable refuses a queue directory that is missing, is
not a directory, or is writable by accounts that must not be able to
inject or drain messages.

symbols.name: QueueMisconfigured

code.public: The queue policy is not one this broker can honour

symbols.doc: QueueMisconfigured refuses a Policy field the broker cannot honour.

symbols.name: Receipt
symbols.doc:
Receipt is the public alias for the opaque handle to one lease. Do not
parse it and do not construct one.

symbols.name: Rejecter
symbols.doc:
Rejecter is the public alias for the capability of dead-lettering a leased
message at once, with the cause that condemned it. Every broker here
implements it, and Consume uses it for a [DoNotRetry] failure.

symbols.name: SQLConfig
symbols.doc:
SQLConfig is the public alias for [NewSQL]'s configuration: Transactor,
Dialect and Table (required), Policy, and Clock.

symbols.name: SQLMigration
symbols.spelled: func(dialect sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (sql.Migration, error)
symbols.canonical: func(dialect github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/sql.Migration, error)
symbols.doc:
SQLMigration returns the migration that creates the one table an SQL queue
named table keeps on dialect, numbered version for the caller's own version
table. Its Down drops the table, and every message in it. Its statement does
nothing when the table exists.

symbols.name: SQLQueueMisconfigured

code.public: The SQL queue's configuration cannot be used

symbols.doc:
SQLQueueMisconfigured refuses an SQLConfig no SQL broker could run: no
transactor, one it cannot join a transaction of, a dialect it cannot
spell, or a table name it cannot use.

symbols.name: UnknownReceipt

code.public: The receipt does not name a lease this queue issued

symbols.doc:
UnknownReceipt refuses an acknowledgement naming a lease this queue
never issued.

symbols.name: Wake
symbols.doc:
Wake is the public alias for what an idle consumer waits on: a signal the
next Publish or Nack in this process closes, and how long until something
the broker holds becomes receivable on its own.

symbols.name: Waker
symbols.doc:
Waker is the public alias for the capability of telling an idle consumer
when to look again. Every broker here implements it, and Consume uses it; a
broker of your own that omits it is simply polled.

symbols.name: Compare
symbols.doc:
Compare returns -1, 0 or +1 as v orders before, equal to or after w under
SemVer precedence. Build metadata is ignored, so v1.0.0+a and v1.0.0+b
compare equal. An invalid string orders below every version and equal to
every other invalid string.

symbols.name: IsPseudoVersion
symbols.doc:
IsPseudoVersion reports whether v is a Go pseudo-version, in any of its
three shapes, with or without build metadata. It recognises the shape: a
stamp whose digits are no real instant still makes one, and
[PseudoVersionTime] is what reports that the time does not read.

symbols.name: IsValid
symbols.doc:
IsValid reports whether v is a version: SemVer 2.0.0 with a leading "v",
or one of the shorthands "vMAJOR" and "vMAJOR.MINOR".

symbols.name: Prerelease
symbols.doc:
Prerelease returns the pre-release part of v with its leading hyphen —
"-rc.1" for "v1.0.0-rc.1+build" — or "" when v has none: a release, a
shorthand, or a string that is not a version, which [IsValid] tells apart.

symbols.name: PseudoVersionRev
symbols.doc:
PseudoVersionRev returns the revision a pseudo-version names — by the
toolchain's convention a commit's first twelve hexadecimal digits — and
reports whether v is a pseudo-version at all.

symbols.name: PseudoVersionTime
symbols.doc:
PseudoVersionTime returns the commit time a pseudo-version carries, in UTC
and to the second, and reports whether it could be read: false when v is
not a pseudo-version, or when its fourteen digits are no real instant.

symbols.name: BeginFailed

code.public: The database refused to open a transaction

symbols.doc: BeginFailed reports a transaction the driver would not open.

symbols.name: Checker
symbols.doc: Checker is the public alias for the bounded liveness probe.

symbols.name: CommitFailed

code.public: The transaction could not be committed and had no effect

symbols.doc: CommitFailed reports a transaction that had NO effect.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc: Config is the public alias for the parameters every port is built from.

symbols.name: ConfigInvalid

code.public: The SQL configuration is incomplete and was refused

symbols.doc:
ConfigInvalid is returned by every constructor for a Config that could
never produce a working port.

symbols.name: Deferrer
symbols.doc:
Deferrer is the public alias for the ADR 0039 sibling of [Transactor] that
holds a function until the transaction a context carries has committed, and
drops it with a rollback. Discover it by type assertion.

symbols.name: Dialect
symbols.doc:
Dialect is the public alias for the closed set of SQL engines this SDK can
spell. For SQL you write yourself, it spells the engine's vocabulary — the
tokens the SDK's own statements are spelled with, never a statement:
[Dialect].Placeholder renders a bind marker ($1 on PostgreSQL, ? on MySQL and
SQLite), [Dialect].QuoteIdent a delimited name, its delimiter doubled
inside, and [Dialect].ForUpdate and [Dialect].ForUpdateSkipLocked a row-lock
clause, which SQLite — whose exclusion is its one write lock — renders as
nothing. QuoteIdent validates nothing: check a name before you interpolate
it. An unset Dialect renders no marker and no name, so a statement built
from it fails rather than passing for another engine's.

symbols.name: DialectMySQL
symbols.doc: DialectMySQL is MySQL 5.7+ / MariaDB 10.x with InnoDB.

symbols.name: DialectPostgres
symbols.doc: DialectPostgres is PostgreSQL 9.1+.

symbols.name: DialectRefused

code.public: That SQL engine is recognised and deliberately not supported

symbols.doc:
DialectRefused is returned by ParseDialect for an engine this SDK
recognises and declines. The reason travels in a field.

symbols.name: DialectSQLite
symbols.doc:
DialectSQLite is SQLite 3.6.8+. It has no advisory lock, so [NewMigrator]
serialises a run on the database file's write lock instead (ADR 0140).

symbols.name: DuplicateMigration

code.public: Two migrations declare the same version

symbols.doc: DuplicateMigration refuses two migrations declaring the same version.

symbols.name: Executor
symbols.doc:
Executor is the public alias for the read/write surface a statement runs
against. *sql.DB, *sql.Tx and *sql.Conn all satisfy it with no adapter, and
it deliberately carries no Commit, Rollback or Begin.

symbols.name: HealthCheckFailed

code.public: The database is not reachable

symbols.doc:
HealthCheckFailed reports a database that answered the probe with an
error.

symbols.name: HealthCheckTimeout

code.public: The database did not answer the health check in time

symbols.doc: HealthCheckTimeout reports a database that did not answer in time.

symbols.name: InvalidMigration

code.public: The migration is not runnable and was refused

symbols.doc:
InvalidMigration is returned for a migration with version 0, an empty
name, a nil Up or a nil Down.

symbols.name: Irreversible
symbols.doc:
Irreversible is the [Step] a migration assigns to Down to declare, out loud,
that it cannot be reversed.

symbols.name: Joiner
symbols.doc:
Joiner is the public alias for the ADR 0039 sibling of [Transactor] that
says where a statement issued under a context runs: in the transaction the
context carries, or on the pool. Discover it by type assertion.

symbols.name: MigrateConfig
symbols.doc: MigrateConfig is the public alias for the migration runner's parameters.

symbols.name: Migration
symbols.doc:
Migration is the public alias for one versioned schema change and its
reversal.

symbols.name: MigrationFailed

code.public: A migration did not apply and was rolled back

symbols.doc:
MigrationFailed reports a migration that did not apply; it was rolled
back.

symbols.name: MigrationIrreversible

code.public: That migration was declared irreversible and cannot be rolled back

symbols.doc: MigrationIrreversible is what the Irreversible step returns.

symbols.name: MigrationLockTimeout

code.public: Another process is running migrations and did not finish in time

symbols.doc:
MigrationLockTimeout reports another process holding the migration lock
for the whole budget. Nothing was applied.

symbols.name: MigrationLockUnsupported

code.public: That dialect has no advisory lock, so migrations cannot be serialised

symbols.doc:
MigrationLockUnsupported refuses a Migrator on a dialect with no lock
that dies with its holder. No dialect this SDK speaks answers it since
SQLite's runner serialises on its file's write lock (ADR 0140).

symbols.name: MigrationOutOfOrder

code.public: A pending migration is older than one already applied

symbols.doc:
MigrationOutOfOrder refuses a pending migration older than one already
applied.

symbols.name: MigrationUnknownVersion

code.public: The database records a migration this build does not carry

symbols.doc:
MigrationUnknownVersion refuses a Down over a version this build does
not carry.

symbols.name: Migrator
symbols.doc: Migrator is the public alias for the schema-migration runner.

symbols.name: NestedIsolation

code.public: A nested transaction cannot change isolation or read-only mode

symbols.doc:
NestedIsolation is returned when a nested Transact asks for isolation
or read-only mode a savepoint cannot provide.

symbols.name: NewChecker
symbols.doc: NewChecker returns a liveness probe bounded by cfg.CheckTimeout.

symbols.name: NewMigrator
symbols.spelled: func(cfg Config, mig MigrateConfig) (runner Migrator, err error)
symbols.doc:
NewMigrator returns the migration runner. It refuses a dialect with no
session-scoped advisory lock, by name and at construction.

symbols.name: NewTransactor
symbols.doc:
NewTransactor returns the transaction manager for cfg.DB, applying
cfg.Pool to it.

symbols.name: ParseDialect
symbols.doc:
ParseDialect resolves a dialect name and never guesses. A recognised but
unsupported engine returns [DialectRefused] carrying why; an unrecognised
one returns [UnknownDialect].

symbols.name: PoolConfig
symbols.doc: PoolConfig is the public alias for the connection-pool policy.

symbols.name: PoolMisconfigured

code.public: The connection-pool policy is not one this SDK will apply

symbols.doc:
PoolMisconfigured refuses a pool policy whose zero value database/sql
would read as a decision nobody made — a non-positive MaxOpen.

symbols.name: Preparer
symbols.doc:
Preparer is the public alias for the ADR 0039 sibling of [Executor]: an
executor that can also prepare a statement. Discover it by type assertion.

symbols.name: RollbackFailed

code.public: Rolling the transaction back did not complete cleanly

symbols.doc: RollbackFailed travels alongside the error that triggered the rollback.

symbols.name: SavepointFailed

code.public: A savepoint statement was rejected by the database

symbols.doc:
SavepointFailed reports a rejected savepoint statement; the "statement"
field names which of the three.

symbols.name: Statements
symbols.doc:
Statements returns a [Step] that runs the given statements in order on the
transaction's executor.

It is the smallest useful helper and deliberately not a file loader: it
invents no directory layout, no naming convention and no parser. Where the
text comes from — a literal, an embed.FS, a generator — stays yours.

symbols.name: Step
symbols.doc: Step is the public alias for one direction of a migration.

symbols.name: Transact
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, tm Transactor, fn TxFunc) error
symbols.doc:
Transact runs fn inside a transaction with the driver's default isolation.

It is the ergonomic form of [Transactor].Transact for the common case. The
port itself keeps the options parameter so it never needs a second method
(ADR 0039); this helper keeps the call site short.

symbols.name: Transactor
symbols.doc: Transactor is the public alias for the transaction manager.

symbols.name: TxClosed

code.public: That transaction handle is no longer valid

symbols.doc:
TxClosed reports an Executor used after the scope that lent it
returned.

symbols.name: TxFunc
symbols.doc: TxFunc is the public alias for a unit of work run inside a transaction.

symbols.name: TxOptions
symbols.doc:
TxOptions is the public alias for one transaction's isolation and
read-only-ness. The zero value defers to the driver.

symbols.name: TxPoisoned

code.public: The transaction is no longer usable and will not be committed

symbols.doc:
TxPoisoned refuses every operation on a transaction whose savepoint
rollback failed. It is never committed.

symbols.name: UnknownDialect

code.public: The SQL dialect is not one this SDK supports

symbols.doc:
UnknownDialect is returned by ParseDialect for a name this SDK has
never heard of.

symbols.name: VersionTableInvalid

code.public: The version-table name is not a plain SQL identifier

symbols.doc:
VersionTableInvalid refuses a version-table name that is not a plain
SQL identifier.

symbols.name: Algorithm
symbols.doc:
Algorithm is the name a Compressor registers under. The zero value is
reserved as invalid.

symbols.name: Available
symbols.doc: Available returns the registered Algorithms, sorted.

symbols.name: BoundedDecompressor
symbols.doc:
BoundedDecompressor is the optional extension of a Compressor that can be
told how much plaintext it may produce; DecompressBounded uses it when the
scheme has it.

symbols.name: CodeCompressedFrameInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeCompressedFrameInvalid identifies a malformed compressed frame of the
codec package, or a frame its decompression-bomb guard refused (0.2.5.4).

symbols.name: CodeDecompressedTooLarge
symbols.doc:
CodeDecompressedTooLarge identifies a stream whose plaintext would exceed
the ceiling its caller gave (0.2.5.6).

symbols.name: CodeFlateFailed
symbols.doc: CodeFlateFailed identifies a stream compress/flate refused (0.3.26.2).

symbols.name: CodeGzipFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeGzipFailed identifies a stream compress/gzip refused, compressing or
decompressing (0.3.26.1).

symbols.name: CodeUnknownCompressor
symbols.doc:
CodeUnknownCompressor identifies an Algorithm no imported package has
registered (0.2.5.1).

symbols.name: CodeZlibFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeZlibFailed identifies a stream compress/zlib refused (0.3.26.3): the
RFC 1950 envelope, told apart from raw DEFLATE because a stream one of
them refuses is often valid under the other.

symbols.name: Compress
symbols.spelled: func(algo Algorithm, dst []byte, src []byte) (encoded []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
Compress compresses src with the scheme registered under algo and appends
the result to dst. An unregistered algo is refused with UnknownCompressor
and dst comes back as it was.

symbols.name: CompressedFrameInvalid

code.public: Compressed frame is malformed or exceeds the safety bound

symbols.doc: CompressedFrameInvalid is the sentinel of [CodeCompressedFrameInvalid].

symbols.name: Compressor
symbols.doc:
Compressor is one compression scheme: Compress and Decompress append to dst.
Implementations are safe for concurrent use.

symbols.name: Decompress
symbols.spelled: func(algo Algorithm, dst []byte, src []byte) (decoded []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
Decompress decompresses src with the scheme registered under algo and
appends the result to dst, bounded by the scheme's own backstop. To bound
it by a number of your own, call DecompressBounded. An unregistered algo is
refused with UnknownCompressor and dst comes back as it was.

symbols.name: DecompressBounded
symbols.spelled: func(algo Algorithm, dst []byte, src []byte, limit int64) (decoded []byte, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(algo github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/transform.Algorithm, dst []byte, src []byte, limit int64) (decoded []byte, err error)
symbols.doc:
DecompressBounded decompresses src with the scheme registered under algo
and appends the result to dst, producing at most limit bytes of plaintext:
a stream that would produce more is refused with DecompressedTooLarge and
dst comes back as it was. A limit of zero admits an empty stream and nothing
else, and a negative limit is read as zero rather than given a meaning of
its own.

A scheme implementing BoundedDecompressor stops at limit, so the work is
bounded too. A scheme that does not — a consumer's own, or one of the
third-party module's — is decompressed under its own backstop and judged
afterwards: declining to tighten the work can never change the verdict,
only the bytes touched reaching it.

symbols.name: DecompressedTooLarge

code.public: Decompressed payload exceeds the caller's ceiling

symbols.doc:
DecompressedTooLarge is the sentinel of [CodeDecompressedTooLarge],
returned as is.

symbols.name: Flate
symbols.doc: Flate is the raw DEFLATE stream of RFC 1951, with no envelope.

symbols.name: FlateFailed

code.public: flate transform failed

symbols.doc: FlateFailed is the sentinel of [CodeFlateFailed].

symbols.name: Gzip
symbols.doc: Gzip is RFC 1952: a DEFLATE stream in a gzip envelope with a CRC-32.

symbols.name: GzipFailed

code.public: gzip transform failed

symbols.doc:
GzipFailed is the sentinel of [CodeGzipFailed]; the stdlib's error is
kept beneath it.

symbols.name: Lookup
symbols.doc: Lookup returns the Compressor registered under algo.

symbols.name: UnknownCompressor

code.public: No compressor is registered under that algorithm

symbols.doc:
UnknownCompressor is the sentinel of [CodeUnknownCompressor], returned
as is.

symbols.name: Zlib
symbols.doc:
Zlib is the RFC 1950 envelope with an Adler-32 — what HTTP calls
"deflate".

symbols.name: ZlibFailed

code.public: zlib transform failed

symbols.doc: ZlibFailed is the sentinel of [CodeZlibFailed].

symbols.name: AtomicWriter
symbols.doc:
AtomicWriter is the public alias for the publication capability, reached by
type assertion on a filesystem this package did not build.

symbols.name: DirectoryNotEmpty

code.public: That directory still has entries in it

symbols.doc:
DirectoryNotEmpty is returned by Remove for a directory that still has
entries. RemoveAll is the recursive call.

symbols.name: DirectorySyncFailed

code.public: The file was published but the directory entry was not flushed

symbols.doc:
DirectorySyncFailed is returned when the rename succeeded and the
directory entry could not be flushed. The content IS published; only
its survival across a power loss is in doubt, and it is deliberately
not rolled back.

symbols.name: FS
symbols.doc:
FS is the public alias for the read half, which is io/fs.FS unchanged. It
exists so a signature can say "an SDK filesystem" without implying that
anything about reading is different here.

symbols.name: FullFS
symbols.doc:
FullFS is the public alias for the union both constructors return: a
[WritableFS] that is also an [AtomicWriter]. A parameter should still ask
for the narrowest thing it uses.

symbols.name: InvalidPath

code.public: That path is not usable on this filesystem

symbols.doc:
InvalidPath is returned for a name outside the fs.ValidPath grammar —
rooted, empty, or carrying a "." or ".." element — and for the root
itself on any call that writes or removes.

symbols.name: InvalidPermission

code.public: A file mode is required and must be a plain permission mode

symbols.doc:
InvalidPermission is returned for a zero file mode, which is never read
as "pick a default", and for any mode carrying setuid, setgid, sticky
or a type bit.

symbols.name: NewMem
symbols.doc:
NewMem returns an empty in-memory filesystem containing only its root.

It takes no arguments on purpose: every knob it could offer would be one a
consumer's test has to set before it can assert anything, and the value of
this type is that a filesystem double costs one line.

symbols.name: NewOS
symbols.doc:
NewOS opens root as a filesystem confined to that directory tree.

It returns proc.UnsupportedPlatform on a GOOS that lacks the mechanics this
filesystem's guarantees rest on, and [RootUnavailable] when the directory
cannot be opened. Both are construction-time refusals, so a misconfiguration
is reported where the program is wired rather than on the first write.

The filesystem holds the directory's descriptor and additionally implements
io.Closer, which releases it; every call after Close fails.

symbols.name: NotRegularFile

code.public: That path already holds something other than a file

symbols.doc:
NotRegularFile is returned when the name — or a component of it —
exists and is not the kind of thing the call needs it to be.

symbols.name: PathEscaped

code.public: That path leaves the filesystem it was resolved against

symbols.doc:
PathEscaped is returned when a name resolved outside the filesystem's
root, and when a write's final component is a symbolic link.

symbols.name: PublishFailed

code.public: The filesystem could not publish that file

symbols.doc:
PublishFailed is returned when an atomic publication did not complete.
The previous content is intact and no temporary survives, so the
operation is safe to retry and safe to abandon.

symbols.name: ReadFailed

code.public: The filesystem could not read that path

symbols.doc:
ReadFailed is returned when an open, stat or listing was refused. The
cause stays in the chain, so errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) still
answers.

symbols.name: RootUnavailable

code.public: The filesystem root could not be opened

symbols.doc:
RootUnavailable is returned by NewOS when the root cannot be opened:
absent, not a directory, or not searchable by this process.

symbols.name: WritableFS
symbols.doc:
WritableFS is the public alias for the write half: the four write verbs on
top of the embedded [FS]. It is frozen — a new capability arrives as a
sibling interface, never as a fifth method.

symbols.name: WriteFailed

code.public: The filesystem could not write that path

symbols.doc:
WriteFailed is returned when a create, write, mkdir or remove was
refused, and keeps its cause the same way.

symbols.name: Bool
symbols.doc: Bool builds a Field holding a boolean value.

symbols.name: Code
symbols.doc:
Code is the dotted-quad error identifier packed into uint32.
See ADR 0005 for the registry and layout.

symbols.name: CodeOf
symbols.doc:
CodeOf returns the deepest *errs.Error's typed Code in err's chain,
or (0, false) when no *errs.Error is present.

symbols.name: ExitCodeOf
symbols.doc:
ExitCodeOf returns the sysexits code mapped from the deepest *errs.Error,
defaulting to 70 (EX_SOFTWARE) when no *errs.Error is present.

symbols.name: Field
symbols.doc:
Field is a single typed key/value pair attached to an error. Build one with
String / Int / Int64 / Bool / Float (or NewFieldValue); the zero value is
invalid and must never be passed across the API.

A Field read back from an error — see [FieldsOf] — answers two methods:
Key(), the name the emitter chose, and StringValue(), the value as text (a
string verbatim, a number in decimal, a bool as true or false, "" for the
zero Field). The rendering is for reading, not for parsing back into a type.

symbols.name: FieldsOf
symbols.doc:
FieldsOf returns every Field attached along err's chain, oldest cause
first and newest wrapper last, as a copy the caller owns — nil when no
*errs.Error is present. Read each with Key and StringValue.

The values are clauses the emitters chose to attach — names, positions,
reasons — never secrets: no SDK emitter attaches a value it was given to
protect (mail.ParseURL never quotes the URL), which is what makes reading
them safe. They are diagnostics nonetheless, like PrivateOf — keep them
off the wire.

symbols.name: Float
symbols.doc: Float builds a Field holding a float64 value (shortest round-trip render).

symbols.name: HTTPStatusOf
symbols.doc:
HTTPStatusOf returns the HTTP status mapped from the deepest *errs.Error,
defaulting to 500 when no *errs.Error is present.

symbols.name: HasAnyCode
symbols.doc:
HasAnyCode walks err's chain and reports whether any *errs.Error
carries a Code matching ANY of the supplied codes. Convenience
equivalent of `HasCode(err, c1) || HasCode(err, c2) || …` — useful
when a retry policy / circuit-breaker / metric routes on a SET of
failure modes rather than a single code.

Returns false when codes is empty.

	retryable := errs.HasAnyCode(err,
	    codec.CodeStreamingUnsupported,
	    logger.CodeWriterRequired,
	    logger.CodeSinkConfigRequired,
	)

symbols.name: HasAnyReason
HasCode
symbols.doc:
HasCode walks the chain (including errors.Join subtrees) and reports
whether any *errs.Error carries code (origin or trail entry).

symbols.name: HasReason
symbols.doc: HasReason walks the chain and reports whether any *errs.Error carries reason.

symbols.name: Int
symbols.doc:
Int builds a Field from a plain int (widened to int64 internally),
matching the slog / zap Int(key, int) convention.

symbols.name: Int64
symbols.doc: Int64 builds a Field from a 64-bit integer (no upcast at the call site).

symbols.name: Layer
symbols.doc:
Layer is the second octet of Code — SDK layer (0 = meta, 1 = kernel,
2 = core, 3 = service,...). See ADR 0005.

symbols.name: Major
symbols.doc:
Major is the top octet of Code — SemVer major version (0 = internal,
1 = v1,...). See ADR 0005.

symbols.name: MaskByLayer
symbols.doc: MaskByLayer matches all codes sharing Major+Layer (/16 equivalent).

symbols.name: MaskByMajor
symbols.doc: MaskByMajor matches all codes sharing the Major octet (/8 equivalent).

symbols.name: MaskByPackage
symbols.doc: MaskByPackage matches all codes sharing Major+Layer+Package (/24 equivalent).

symbols.name: MaskExact
symbols.doc: MaskExact matches a single exact code (/32 equivalent).

symbols.name: MaxMajor
symbols.doc:
MaxMajor is the largest legal Major octet. Codes must round-trip through a
positive int32 (the kernel rule that keeps the deprecated int accessor from
wrapping negative), so the top uint32 bit stays clear and the Major octet
caps at 0x7F.

symbols.name: MinAppMajor
symbols.doc:
MinAppMajor is the lowest Major octet reserved for third-party / application
error codes. The SDK only ever allocates Major < MinAppMajor (0 = internal,
1.. = the public semver major). A consumer that builds every Code with a
Major in [MinAppMajor, MaxMajor] is guaranteed never to collide with an SDK
code, now or in any future SDK release. See ADR 0019.

symbols.name: New
symbols.spelled: func(code Code, reason string, public string, private string, fields ...Field) error
symbols.canonical: func(code github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/errs.Code, reason string, public string, private string, fields ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/errs.Field) error
symbols.doc:
New constructs a typed SDK error at runtime. On success the returned error
carries code / reason / public / private plus any fields. On a structural
failure it returns a typed validation error (CodeInvalidCode / Reason /
Public / Private) identifying the exact rule broken — the result is always a
non-nil, introspectable SDK error, never a panic.

Arguments mirror the kernel sentinel contract:
  - code: a dotted-quad Code; use a Major in [MinAppMajor, MaxMajor] to stay
    collision-free with the SDK (see the package doc and ADR 0019).
  - reason: a stable SCREAMING_SNAKE identifier (^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$).
  - public: the wire-safe message — non-empty, ≤120 runes, no newline.
    Validated here; an over-cap or multiline public yields a typed
    CodeInvalidPublic error rather than the error you intended.
  - private: the log-only diagnostic envelope — non-empty, never surfaced.
  - fields: optional structured metadata (defensively copied).

HTTP status defaults to 500 and exit code to 70 (EX_SOFTWARE); a per-error
exit override is available through Wrap's WrapParams.ExitCode.

symbols.name: NewFieldValue
symbols.doc:
NewFieldValue builds a string-typed Field. Provided for tooling that
expects a New-prefixed factory; prefer String for the common case.

symbols.name: NewPrefixMatcher
symbols.doc: NewPrefixMatcher builds an errors.Is target for CIDR-style Code matching.

symbols.name: Pack
symbols.spelled: func(major Major, layer Layer, pkg PkgCode, serial Serial) Code
symbols.doc:
Pack constructs a Code from its four octets. Runtime only — sentinel
constants in caller code MUST use hex literals to stay const-expressible.

symbols.name: ParseCode
symbols.doc: ParseCode parses the canonical "M.L.P.S" textual form.

symbols.name: PkgCode
symbols.doc: PkgCode is the third octet of Code — per-layer package slot. See ADR 0005 / 0006.

symbols.name: PrefixMatcher
symbols.doc:
PrefixMatcher is the errors.Is target for CIDR-style Code matching.
Construct via NewPrefixMatcher.

symbols.name: PrivateOf
symbols.doc: PrivateOf returns the deepest *errs.Error Private message. DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY.

symbols.name: PublicOf
symbols.doc:
PublicOf returns the deepest *errs.Error Public message, or "" when no
*errs.Error is in the chain.

symbols.name: ReasonOf
symbols.doc:
ReasonOf returns the deepest *errs.Error reason in err's chain, or ("", false).

It is a variable bound to the kernel accessor rather than a forwarder like
its siblings: the forwarder cannot inline — the accessor it would inline
already costs 75 of the inliner's 80 — and in two of four measured runs it
was slower than the indirect call through this variable by more than the
3 % a forwarder may cost (BENCH.md). Assigning to it would change it for
every caller in the process: never do.

symbols.name: Serial
symbols.doc: Serial is the low octet of Code — per-package serial. See ADR 0005.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc: String builds a Field holding a string value.

symbols.name: Wrap
symbols.spelled: func(cause error, params WrapParams, fields ...Field) error
symbols.doc:
Wrap attaches a cause to a new error with origin-wins semantics and preserves
the chain (errors.Is / errors.Unwrap walk through it). When the cause is
already an SDK error (directly or behind a fmt.Errorf("%w") wrap) the result
inherits its Code/Reason/Public/Private and appends params.Code to the trail;
otherwise params.Code becomes the origin. Bad params at runtime do not panic —
the returned error carries a typed validation code.

Declared as a function (not a var alias over the kernel Wrap) so the public
signature returns error: the concrete *errs.Error stays unexported, never
leaking through the facade.

symbols.name: WrapParams
symbols.doc:
WrapParams groups the metadata Wrap stamps onto the wrapping error when the
cause is NOT already an SDK error. When the cause IS an SDK error, origin
wins: Code/Reason/Public/Private are inherited from the cause and only
params.Code is appended to the wrap trail (ADR 0005).

symbols.name: AllowMethods
symbols.doc: AllowMethods admits only the named HTTP methods. Passing none admits none.

symbols.name: AllowPaths
symbols.doc:
AllowPaths admits only paths matching one of the patterns. The patterns are
supplied unanchored and anchored here, so no caller can forget to.

symbols.name: CallFailed

code.public: The outbound call failed

symbols.doc: CallFailed reports an unreachable upstream or a non-2xx status.

symbols.name: CallHook
symbols.doc: CallHook receives one CallInfo per outbound call. It must not block.

symbols.name: CallInfo
symbols.doc: CallInfo records one completed outbound call.

symbols.name: Client
symbols.doc: Client performs guarded outbound HTTP calls.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc:
Config describes an outbound client. Durations accept "5s" as well as a raw
nanosecond count, so a configuration file stays readable.

symbols.name: DenyPaths
symbols.doc:
DenyPaths refuses paths matching one of the patterns. A deny is final and is
not overridable by an allow pattern.

symbols.name: Duration
symbols.doc: Duration is a configuration-friendly time.Duration.

symbols.name: New
symbols.spelled: func(cfg Config, id tlsid.Identity, policy Policy, hook CallHook) (c *Client, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(cfg github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/client.Config, id github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/tlsid.Identity, policy github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/client.Policy, hook github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/client.CallHook) (c *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/client.Client, err error)
symbols.doc:
New builds a guarded client. A nil policy is refused rather than defaulted to
"allow everything": an unguarded egress path wearing the name of a guarded one
is worse than no client at all.

symbols.name: Policies
symbols.doc:
Policies requires every policy to allow the request. Composition is by
conjunction, so adding a policy can only ever narrow what is permitted.

symbols.name: Policy
symbols.doc:
Policy authorises an outbound request. Implementations run inside the
transport, so no call site can bypass them.

symbols.name: PolicyFunc
symbols.doc: PolicyFunc adapts a plain function to Policy.

symbols.name: RequestDenied

code.public: The request was refused by policy

symbols.doc:
RequestDenied reports a request refused by the policy. Its public message
never names the refused path, so a denial cannot leak the private API
surface into a log line.

symbols.name: RequestInfo
symbols.doc:
RequestInfo is the immutable request description a Policy judges. It carries
the ESCAPED path: url.URL.Path is already percent-decoded, so a policy that
judged it would accept "%2e%2e", which the upstream reinterprets as "..".

symbols.name: Response
symbols.doc: Response is a fully-read outbound response.

symbols.name: ResponseTooLarge

code.public: The response is larger than the accepted size

symbols.doc: ResponseTooLarge reports a body beyond the configured ceiling.

symbols.name: TooManyRedirects

code.public: The outbound call exceeded its redirect budget
