symbols.doc: TooManyRedirects reports a redirect chain beyond the configured cap.

symbols.name: UnsafePath

code.public: The request path is not in normalised form

symbols.doc:
UnsafePath reports a path carrying a dot segment, literal or
percent-encoded, or a path that is not absolute.

symbols.name: Adopt
symbols.doc:
Adopt takes over a socket inherited from a supervisor instead of binding one.

Socket activation is what makes a zero-downtime restart possible: the
supervisor holds the bound socket across the exec, so no connection is lost
and no bind races. The name is the one the unit file publishes in
LISTEN_FDNAMES. Repeat the option to adopt several sockets into one group.

A named socket the supervisor did not pass is SocketAdoptFailed, never a
silent fallback to binding: a service that quietly binds its own port has
lost exactly the property activation exists to provide. The same holds on
Windows, which has no socket activation at all: Start fails there with
SocketAdoptFailed, whose cause field names UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.

symbols.name: AlreadyStarted

code.public: The server is already started

symbols.doc: AlreadyStarted reports a second Start on a running server.

symbols.name: BatchSize
symbols.doc:
BatchSize sets how many datagrams one read attempts to collect. One disables
batching; zero selects the platform default. Where the platform cannot batch,
State reports the degradation rather than hiding it.

symbols.name: Chain
symbols.doc:
Chain applies middlewares to a handler, outermost first.

Chain(h, a, b, c) yields a(b(c(h))): the first middleware listed is the first
to see a connection, matching how the list reads at the call site.

symbols.name: ChainPacket
symbols.doc: ChainPacket applies middlewares to a datagram handler, outermost first.

symbols.name: Conn
symbols.doc: Conn is one accepted stream connection. It embeds net.Conn.

symbols.name: ConnLimitReached

code.public: The server is at its connection limit

symbols.doc: ConnLimitReached reports a connection turned away by the group ceiling.

symbols.name: DrainSignal
symbols.doc:
DrainSignal returns the channel closed when the server serving this request
begins draining, or nil when none is published.

It is how a handler that holds a connection open indefinitely — an event
stream, a long poll — learns that finishing now is the cooperative thing to
do. Without it such a handler holds the drain open until the budget expires
and its socket is severed under it, on every shutdown.

A nil channel blocks forever, so a select that watches it needs no nil check
and behaves correctly on a server that publishes nothing.

symbols.name: DrainTimeout

code.public: The server did not drain before its deadline

symbols.doc: DrainTimeout reports a shutdown whose budget expired with work in flight.

symbols.name: Group
symbols.doc:
Group is a set of listeners sharing one handler, middleware chain and policy.

Group.HandleHTTP mounts an http.Handler on the group's listeners: the group
keeps its own limits, TLS identity and drain, and net/http only does the
protocol.

symbols.name: GroupDuplicate

code.public: The listener group is already declared

symbols.doc: GroupDuplicate reports a second group declared under one name.

symbols.name: GroupOption
symbols.doc: GroupOption configures a Group.

symbols.name: Handler
symbols.doc: Handler serves one accepted stream connection.

symbols.name: HandlerFunc
symbols.doc: HandlerFunc adapts a plain function to Handler.

symbols.name: HandlerMissing

code.public: The listener group has no handler

symbols.doc: HandlerMissing reports a group declared without a handler.

symbols.name: HandshakeTimeout
symbols.doc:
HandshakeTimeout bounds the TLS negotiation on the group's listeners.

Unset does not mean unbounded, unlike the other three. The handshake runs on
the connection's own goroutine — the listener does not negotiate in Accept,
which is what keeps one slow peer from stalling the accept path for everyone
— so it is the one phase that can be stalled before any handler exists to
notice, and a peer that connects and says nothing would otherwise hold a
goroutine and a slot under MaxConns indefinitely. It falls back to a domain
default instead.

symbols.name: IdleTimeout
symbols.doc:
IdleTimeout bounds how long a connection may sit with no traffic at all.

It is enforced on the read side, where silence is observable: a read is
bounded by whichever of ReadTimeout and IdleTimeout is tighter. Setting both
therefore narrows the bound rather than replacing it, which is what the two
options together are asking for.

symbols.name: InvalidAddress

code.public: The network address is not valid

symbols.doc: InvalidAddress reports an unusable listen address.

symbols.name: Listen
symbols.doc:
Listen adds an address to a group. Repeat it to bind several addresses to one
handler — a TCP port and a Unix socket, for instance.

On Windows, whose AF_UNIX sockets are stream-only, a "unixgram" or
"unixpacket" address fails Start with the SDK's UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM, before
any socket is opened; "unix" is served there as everywhere else.

symbols.name: ListenFailed

code.public: The server could not bind its listening address

symbols.doc: ListenFailed reports a listener that could not be bound.

symbols.name: ListenerState
symbols.doc: ListenerState reports one bound listener, including any fallback.

symbols.name: MaxConns
symbols.doc:
MaxConns caps how many connections a group serves at once.

The budget is per group, not per socket: a group listening on a TCP port and
a Unix socket, or sharded across several listeners, shares one ceiling —
which is what an operator sizing a server actually means. Beyond it a
connection is accepted and closed immediately with ConnLimitReached, because
a refusal the peer can observe beats a timeout it cannot tell from a hang.
Zero means no ceiling.

symbols.name: MaxHeaderBytes
symbols.doc:
MaxHeaderBytes caps the bytes net/http reads for a request's line and header
fields; a request past the cap is answered 431 Request Header Fields Too
Large and never reaches the handler.

Unset (or non-positive) keeps net/http's default of 1 MiB, which applied
silently before this option existed. net/http reads a small fixed allowance
past the cap before refusing. No effect on a group that does not serve HTTP.

symbols.name: MaxPacketSize
symbols.doc:
MaxPacketSize caps the datagram size a group accepts.

A larger datagram is dropped and counted in [State].OversizedPackets, never
delivered. Truncating would hand the handler a prefix indistinguishable from
a complete message, which is a correctness problem rather than a capacity
one; a drop it can observe in State is the honest answer.

symbols.name: Middleware
symbols.doc: Middleware decorates a handler with another of the same type.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc: New builds a server.

symbols.name: Option
symbols.doc: Option configures a Server.

symbols.name: Packet
symbols.doc: Packet is one received datagram.

symbols.name: PacketGroup
symbols.doc: PacketGroup is a set of datagram sockets sharing one handler and chain.

symbols.name: PacketHandler
symbols.doc: PacketHandler serves one received datagram.

symbols.name: PacketHandlerFunc
symbols.doc: PacketHandlerFunc adapts a plain function to PacketHandler.

symbols.name: PacketMiddleware
symbols.doc: PacketMiddleware decorates a datagram handler.

symbols.name: Phase
symbols.doc: Phase is where a server sits in its lifecycle.

symbols.name: PhaseDraining
symbols.doc: PhaseDraining has stopped accepting and is waiting for in-flight work.

symbols.name: PhaseNew
symbols.doc:
The lifecycle phases, in the order a server passes through them. They are
re-exported so a caller can compare State().Phase without importing the
internal package, which Go's firewall forbids anyway.
PhaseNew is a constructed server that has not bound anything yet.

symbols.name: PhaseServing
symbols.doc: PhaseServing is bound and accepting.

symbols.name: PhaseStarting
symbols.doc: PhaseStarting is binding listeners; some may already be up.

symbols.name: PhaseStopped
symbols.doc: PhaseStopped has released every listener.

symbols.name: ReadBufferSize
symbols.doc:
ReadBufferSize sizes the per-connection scratch buffer handed to the handler
by Conn.Buffer. It is recycled with the connection, which is what lets a
handler read without allocating per connection.

symbols.name: ReadHeaderTimeout
symbols.doc:
ReadHeaderTimeout bounds the HEADER phase of an HTTP request on its own: the
request line and every header field must arrive within d, whatever the read
timeout allows a body.

The header phase is the one a slowloris stalls — a byte every few seconds,
never finishing a line — and the one an honest client finishes in
milliseconds, so it deserves a bound far shorter than a read timeout sized
for an upload. A client that stalls there is disconnected at d. Unset (or
non-positive) keeps the earlier behaviour: the header phase is bounded by
[ReadTimeout]. No effect on a group that does not serve HTTP.

symbols.name: ReadTimeout
symbols.doc:
ReadTimeout bounds one read from the peer.

It is refreshed per read, not installed once when the connection is accepted:
a deadline set at accept time would be a budget for the connection's whole
life, which a peer trickling one byte at a time stays comfortably inside. On
a group serving an http.Handler the same value becomes net/http's own
ReadTimeout — and its ReadHeaderTimeout too, unless [ReadHeaderTimeout] sets
the header phase apart — so it is refreshed per request there.

symbols.name: Server
symbols.doc: Server owns a set of listener groups and their lifecycle.

symbols.name: Shards
symbols.doc:
Shards sets how many listeners to open on each of the group's addresses.

Zero selects one per core; one disables sharding. Where the platform (Windows
has no SO_REUSEPORT) or the socket family (a Unix socket) cannot shard, the
count collapses to one. An explicit count that collapses is reported in State
with the reason; zero collapsing is not, since it asked for nothing a single
listener fails to give.

symbols.name: State
symbols.doc: State is a snapshot of the server's lifecycle and listeners.

symbols.name: TLS
symbols.doc:
TLS turns the group's listeners into TLS listeners, or mutual-TLS ones when
the identity requires a client certificate.

symbols.name: UnsupportedNetwork

code.public: The network type is not supported

symbols.doc: UnsupportedNetwork reports a socket family the domain does not serve.

symbols.name: WithDrainTimeout
symbols.doc:
WithDrainTimeout bounds how long Shutdown waits for in-flight connections
before severing them.

symbols.name: WriteTimeout
symbols.doc: WriteTimeout bounds one write to the peer, refreshed per write.

symbols.name: AppendEvent
symbols.doc:
AppendEvent appends ev's wire form to dst and returns the extended slice —
the bytes [Stream].Send writes, for a caller that frames events onto a
transport of its own.

It appends nothing when the frame is invalid: the whole frame is validated
first, so a partial frame never reaches dst. Appending rather than returning
a fresh slice is what lets a caller reuse one buffer for every frame.

symbols.name: ContentType
symbols.doc:
ContentType is the media type an event stream is served under. A client that
receives anything else does not open an EventSource at all.

symbols.name: DefaultKeepAlive
symbols.doc:
DefaultKeepAlive is the comment cadence a stream uses when the caller sets
none. It sits under the idle timeout of every proxy worth naming.

symbols.name: DefaultWriteTimeout
symbols.doc:
DefaultWriteTimeout bounds ONE frame's write. A stream has no total write
budget by nature; this is what stops a peer that has stopped reading from
pinning a goroutine forever.

symbols.name: DrainSignal
symbols.doc:
DrainSignal returns the channel closed when the server serving this request
begins draining, or nil when it publishes none.

It is what [Stream] watches, exposed because an event stream is not the only
handler that holds a connection open indefinitely — a long poll does too, and
so will anything built on a protocol upgrade. A nil channel blocks forever,
so a select that watches it needs no nil check.

symbols.name: Event
symbols.doc:
Event is one Server-Sent Events frame. [Event].Validate reports whether the
wire format can carry it; [AppendEvent] writes it.

symbols.name: FieldInvalid

code.public: The event cannot be represented in the event-stream format

symbols.doc:
FieldInvalid reports an event the wire format cannot carry: a line
terminator in an id, an event name or a comment; a negative or
sub-millisecond retry; an event name with no data, which every client
discards; or a frame with no field at all.

symbols.name: FlushUnsupported

code.public: The response cannot be streamed

symbols.doc:
FlushUnsupported reports a ResponseWriter that cannot be flushed, and so
cannot stream at all.

symbols.name: KeepAlive
symbols.doc:
KeepAlive sets the interval between keep-alive comments.

Zero does not mean "never": a stream with keep-alive silently disabled works
perfectly on a developer's loopback and dies at one minute behind a real
proxy, which is the worst possible place to learn it. Zero is clamped to
[DefaultKeepAlive]; a negative interval is refused. To disable it, say so
with [WithoutKeepAlive].

symbols.name: LastEventIDHeader
symbols.doc:
LastEventIDHeader is the request header a reconnecting client sends, carrying
the id of the last event it processed.

symbols.name: MinRetry
symbols.doc:
MinRetry is the shortest reconnection hint [Event].Retry can carry. The wire
field is an integer millisecond count, so anything shorter would round to
zero — which does not mean "very soon", it means "reconnect immediately".

symbols.name: New
symbols.spelled: func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, opts ...Option) (stream *Stream, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(w net/http.ResponseWriter, r *net/http.Request, opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/sse.Option) (stream *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/sse.Stream, err error)
symbols.doc:
New starts an event stream on w and returns it.

It writes the response headers and flushes them immediately, so the client
connects at once rather than at the first event. It fails when the response
cannot be flushed — checked before anything is written, so the handler is
free to answer some other way.

symbols.name: Option
symbols.doc: Option configures a Stream.

symbols.name: Retry
symbols.doc:
Retry sets the reconnection delay the stream advertises in its opening frame.

It is the server's one chance to control how hard clients come back: a fleet
that all reconnect on the browser default of about three seconds is a
thundering herd aimed at a server that has just restarted. Zero sends no
retry field.

symbols.name: Stream
symbols.doc:
Stream is one open event stream: an HTTP response held open, written one
frame at a time and flushed after each. It is safe for concurrent use.

symbols.name: StreamClosed

code.public: The event stream is closed

symbols.doc:
StreamClosed reports a send on a stream that has already ended — the
client disconnected, the server began draining, or the handler closed it.
It is the terminal outcome a streaming handler loops until.

symbols.name: StreamMisconfigured

code.public: The event stream options are not valid

symbols.doc:
StreamMisconfigured reports an option the domain refuses to interpret
rather than guess at, such as a negative keep-alive interval.

symbols.name: WithoutKeepAlive
symbols.doc:
WithoutKeepAlive disables the keep-alive comment entirely, so that "never" is
something a caller writes on purpose rather than something a zero does to
them.

symbols.name: WriteTimeout
symbols.doc:
WriteTimeout bounds how long one frame's write may take.

It is per-frame on purpose. A group's WriteTimeout is an absolute deadline
for the whole response, which on an endless stream means the stream is cut at
that instant; a stream replaces it with this bound, refreshed per frame. Zero
is clamped to [DefaultWriteTimeout], negative is refused.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc:
Config says how a tree is served; its zero value is a working, strict
configuration.

symbols.name: DefaultContentSecurityPolicy
symbols.doc:
DefaultContentSecurityPolicy is the policy sent when Config names none: the
page's own origin for everything it loads, no base URL or form target
elsewhere, and no framing by another page.

symbols.name: DefaultReferrerPolicy
symbols.doc:
DefaultReferrerPolicy is the Referrer-Policy sent when Config names none: a
full referrer to this origin, none at all to another.

symbols.name: Handler
symbols.doc:
Handler serves one file tree; it is an http.Handler, safe for concurrent
use. The zero Handler has no tree and answers every request 500.

symbols.name: ImmutableCacheControl
symbols.doc:
ImmutableCacheControl is the Cache-Control of a file Config.Immutable marks
content-hashed: a year, shared caches included, never revalidated.

symbols.name: Misconfigured

code.public: The static file handler configuration is not valid

symbols.doc:
Misconfigured is returned by New for a nil tree, a header value holding a
control character, or a Referrer-Policy that is not a list of known tokens.
The "option" field names which; the value is never repeated.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New returns a Handler serving fsys as cfg says, or Misconfigured. It reads
nothing from fsys. To serve a sub-directory, hand it the result of fs.Sub;
to keep a link inside the tree from leading out of it, hand it an os.Root's
FS rather than os.DirFS — the handler confines the names it is asked for,
not what the tree's own entries point at.

symbols.name: RevalidateCacheControl
symbols.doc:
RevalidateCacheControl is the Cache-Control of every other response:
stored, but revalidated before each use.

symbols.name: FileParams
symbols.doc: FileParams names TLS material to read from the filesystem.

symbols.name: HandshakeFailed

code.public: The TLS handshake failed

symbols.doc: HandshakeFailed reports a TLS or mutual-TLS handshake that did not complete.

symbols.name: Identity
symbols.doc:
Identity is an opaque TLS identity. Its String and GoString output is always
"<redacted>"; ClientConfig and ServerConfig are the only ways to reach the
material, and each returns a fresh *tls.Config.

symbols.name: Load
symbols.doc:
Load reads the named TLS material from disk and returns the opaque identity.
A configured-but-unreadable file is an error, never a silently skipped one.

symbols.name: MaterialInvalid

code.public: The TLS material is missing or invalid

symbols.doc:
MaterialInvalid reports TLS material that is missing, unreadable,
malformed, or that yields no usable certificate. It is never downgraded to
an empty trust store.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New validates TLS material held in memory and returns the opaque identity. It
applies exactly the same rules as Load; only the source of the bytes differs.

symbols.name: Params
symbols.doc: Params carries TLS material already held in memory.

symbols.name: AcceptKey
symbols.doc:
AcceptKey computes the Sec-WebSocket-Accept value for a client's
Sec-WebSocket-Key (RFC 6455 §4.2.2).

It is exported for tests and for anyone writing a client handshake by hand.
The digest is SHA-1 by the RFC's own instruction and is not a security
primitive: its job is to prove the server parsed the handshake rather than
replaying it, so a cached 101 cannot pass for a live upgrade.

symbols.name: AllowAnyOrigin
symbols.doc:
AllowAnyOrigin disables the origin check.

It has to be written out because the browser's same-origin policy does not
apply to WebSocket: any page may open a connection to this server and the
browser will attach the user's cookies to the handshake. Reach for it when
authentication does not ride on ambient credentials — a bearer token, a
signed ticket — which is exactly when the origin proves nothing anyway.

symbols.name: AllowOrigins
symbols.doc:
AllowOrigins replaces the default same-origin rule with an exact allowlist.

The comparison is on the whole Origin header — scheme, host and port —
case-insensitively. Matching the host alone would accept http:// for an https
server, which is the downgrade the check exists to notice. Behind a proxy
that terminates TLS this is the only way to have the scheme checked at all:
the request arrives in plaintext there, so the default rule cannot see which
scheme the browser used.

symbols.name: CloseAbnormal
symbols.doc: CloseAbnormal means the connection died without a Close frame.

symbols.name: CloseCode
symbols.doc: CloseCode is the status code a Close frame carries (RFC 6455 §7.4).

symbols.name: CloseExtensionRequired
symbols.doc: CloseExtensionRequired is a client giving up for want of an extension.

symbols.name: CloseGoingAway
symbols.doc: CloseGoingAway is a server shutting down; it is what a drain sends.

symbols.name: CloseInternalError
symbols.doc: CloseInternalError is an unexpected condition on this side.

symbols.name: CloseInvalidPayload
symbols.doc: CloseInvalidPayload is text that is not valid UTF-8.

symbols.name: CloseNoStatus
symbols.doc: CloseNoStatus means the peer's Close frame carried no code.

symbols.name: CloseNormal
symbols.doc: CloseNormal is a completed purpose, on either side.

symbols.name: ClosePolicyViolation
symbols.doc: ClosePolicyViolation is the generic refusal when no other code fits.

symbols.name: CloseProtocolError
symbols.doc: CloseProtocolError is a frame the RFC forbids.

symbols.name: CloseTLSHandshake
symbols.doc: CloseTLSHandshake means the TLS handshake failed.

symbols.name: CloseTooLarge
symbols.doc: CloseTooLarge is a message beyond what this endpoint accepts.

symbols.name: CloseUnsupportedData
symbols.doc:
CloseUnsupportedData is a well-formed frame carrying data this endpoint
cannot accept.

symbols.name: Conn
symbols.doc:
Conn is one upgraded WebSocket connection.

Exactly one goroutine loops on [Conn].Receive for the connection's whole
life. Never two: the protocol is a single ordered frame stream, so two
readers would each take half of a message. Never zero: that loop is also
where Pings are answered, where the peer's Close is replied to and where the
heartbeat sees the peer alive, so a connection nobody reads is ended within
two ping intervals — see the package documentation for the push-handler
shape. Writes are safe for concurrent use.

symbols.name: ConnClosed

code.public: The WebSocket connection is closed

symbols.doc:
ConnClosed reports an operation on a connection that has ended. It is the
terminal outcome a receive loop runs until, and it carries the peer's
close code when there was one.

symbols.name: ConnMisconfigured

code.public: The WebSocket options are not valid

symbols.doc:
ConnMisconfigured reports an option the domain refuses to interpret
rather than guess at, such as a negative ping interval.

symbols.name: DefaultMaxFrameSize
symbols.doc: DefaultMaxFrameSize is the ceiling on a single frame's announced payload.

symbols.name: DefaultMaxMessageSize
symbols.doc: DefaultMaxMessageSize is the ceiling on one reassembled message.

symbols.name: DefaultPingInterval
symbols.doc:
DefaultPingInterval is the heartbeat cadence a connection uses when the
caller sets none. It sits under the idle timeout of every proxy worth naming.

symbols.name: DefaultWriteTimeout
symbols.doc:
DefaultWriteTimeout bounds ONE frame's write. A connection has no total write
budget by nature; this is what stops a peer that has stopped reading from
pinning a goroutine forever.

symbols.name: DrainSignal
symbols.doc:
DrainSignal returns the channel closed when the server serving this request
begins draining, or nil when it publishes none.

[Conn] watches it for you. It is re-exported here because a handler often
wants to stop its own work at the same moment, and a nil channel blocks
forever, so a select that watches it needs no nil check.

symbols.name: GUID
symbols.doc:
GUID is the fixed string RFC 6455 §1.3 concatenates to the client's key
before hashing. It is a constant of the protocol, not a secret.

symbols.name: HandshakeFailed

code.public: The WebSocket handshake is not valid

symbols.doc:
HandshakeFailed reports a request that is not a valid RFC 6455 opening
handshake, or one whose origin the policy refused. [Upgrade] has already
written the HTTP response when it returns this.

symbols.name: InvalidPayload

code.public: The WebSocket payload is not valid

symbols.doc:
InvalidPayload reports text that is not UTF-8, a close code that must
never travel, or a close reason past the control-frame ceiling.

symbols.name: MaxControlPayload
symbols.doc:
MaxControlPayload is the ceiling RFC 6455 §5.5 puts on a control frame's
payload, and therefore on a [Conn].Ping payload or a close reason.

symbols.name: MaxFrameSize
symbols.doc:
MaxFrameSize bounds one frame's ANNOUNCED payload length.

It is separate from [MaxMessageSize] because it is enforced at a different
moment: against the header, before a byte is read or allocated. A ceiling
above the message ceiling can never be reached and is refused as a mistake.

symbols.name: MaxMessageSize
symbols.doc:
MaxMessageSize bounds one reassembled message.

Zero is clamped to [DefaultMaxMessageSize], negative is refused. There is
deliberately no "unbounded" setting: the length is announced by the peer in a
64-bit field, and fragmentation lets it keep announcing more, so an unbounded
ceiling is not a configuration choice — it is a remote memory allocator.

symbols.name: Message
symbols.doc: Message is one complete WebSocket application message.

symbols.name: MessageTooLarge

code.public: The WebSocket message is larger than the accepted size

symbols.doc:
MessageTooLarge reports a frame or a reassembled message beyond the
configured ceiling, refused before any buffer was sized from it.

symbols.name: Option
symbols.doc: Option configures a Conn.

symbols.name: PingInterval
symbols.doc:
PingInterval sets how often the connection pings an otherwise silent peer.

Zero does not mean "never": it is clamped to [DefaultPingInterval], because a
connection with the heartbeat silently disabled works perfectly on loopback
and then stops noticing peers that vanish — which is how a mobile client
normally leaves. A negative interval is refused; "never" is [WithoutPing].

The heartbeat counts frames the handler has READ, so it keeps a connection
open only while one goroutine loops on [Conn].Receive; a connection nobody
reads is ended within two intervals, however healthy the peer.

symbols.name: ProtocolViolation

code.public: The WebSocket frame is not valid

symbols.doc:
ProtocolViolation reports a frame RFC 6455 forbids. The connection has
already been failed when it surfaces.

symbols.name: Subprotocols
symbols.doc:
Subprotocols declares the subprotocols this server speaks, most preferred
first.

The SERVER's order decides. A client advertises what it can speak; choosing
among those is the server's call, or a client that listed a deprecated
dialect first could pin the server to it forever. No overlap is not a failure
— the upgrade succeeds with no subprotocol, which RFC 6455 §4.2.2 names as
the way to say "none agreed".

Each name must be an RFC 7230 token, since the chosen one is written into
the response verbatim; a name with a space, a comma or a quote is refused at
Upgrade. The list is copied, so reusing the slice changes nothing later.

symbols.name: Upgrade
symbols.spelled: func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, opts ...Option) (conn *Conn, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(w net/http.ResponseWriter, r *net/http.Request, opts ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/websocket.Option) (conn *github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/websocket.Conn, err error)
symbols.doc:
Upgrade completes the RFC 6455 opening handshake and returns the connection.

On failure it has ALREADY written the HTTP response — a 426 carrying the
version this server speaks, a 400, a 403 or a 405 as the fault requires — so
the handler should simply return.

The socket is taken over from net/http. It is no longer the HTTP server's to
close, nor this SDK's listener engine's: it is the handler's until
[Conn].Close.

symbols.name: UpgradeUnsupported

code.public: The connection cannot be upgraded

symbols.doc:
UpgradeUnsupported reports a response whose connection cannot be taken
over — HTTP/2, or a middleware that wraps the ResponseWriter without
forwarding Unwrap. The request was fine; this stack cannot serve it.

symbols.name: Version
symbols.doc:
Version is the only protocol version this server speaks. A request naming
another is refused WITH this value advertised back, so a client can
renegotiate instead of guessing.

symbols.name: WithoutPing
symbols.doc:
WithoutPing disables the heartbeat, and with it the connection's only
liveness check. Use it where the transport provides its own.

symbols.name: WriteTimeout
symbols.doc:
WriteTimeout bounds how long one frame's write may take.

It is per-frame on purpose: a group's WriteTimeout is an absolute deadline
for one HTTP response, and this connection outlives the response entirely.
Zero is clamped to [DefaultWriteTimeout], negative is refused.

symbols.name: Any
symbols.doc:
Any builds an Attr carrying an opaque payload. Use the typed helpers when
possible — Any disables type-aware rendering.

symbols.name: Attr
symbols.doc: Attr is the stable alias for the internal AttrValue key/value pair.

symbols.name: Bool
symbols.doc: Bool builds an Attr carrying a boolean value.

symbols.name: Build
symbols.doc:
Build returns a chainable Builder bound to lg at the supplied level.
Builders are recycled through a sync.Pool, so the steady-state per-call
cost is one heap allocation per emit — the handler clones the accumulated
attrs on Send, and that clone escapes. See BENCH.md.

symbols.name: Builder
symbols.doc:
Builder is the stable alias for the internal chainable Builder. Returned
by Build, every typed accessor (Str / Int / Bool / …) returns the receiver
so callers compose the chain in a single expression. Send terminates the
chain — callers MUST NOT use the builder after Send.

symbols.name: CloudWatchConfig
symbols.doc:
CloudWatchConfig configures the "cloudwatch" writer. Same import-gated
resolution as S3Config.

symbols.name: CodeSinkConfigRequired
symbols.doc:
CodeSinkConfigRequired identifies a NewWithSink call with
SinkConfig.Sink == nil; the v1 façade refuses to default silently to
a console sink so callers see the misconfiguration immediately. The
identifier is qualified with "Config" so the AST audit can distinguish
it from the service-layer sink/handler validation (0.3.1.4).

symbols.name: CodeTopologyInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeTopologyInvalid identifies a FromConfig call whose config blob is
malformed, names an unregistered writer, or whose Factory/DecodeConfig
rejected its options. The error path is redacted: it names only the writer
and the failure kind, never any decoded credential or option value (ADR 0014).

symbols.name: CodeWriterRequired
symbols.doc:
CodeWriterRequired identifies a NewText call with Config.Writer == nil;
the v1 façade refuses to default silently to stderr.

symbols.name: CodeWriterSpecInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeWriterSpecInvalid identifies a NewMulti call with no WriterSpec entries;
the façade refuses to build a logger that fans out to nothing (ADR 0012).

symbols.name: Config

fields.name: Writer
fields.doc:
Writer is the single-destination convenience field; nil triggers
WriterRequired unless Writers carries at least one entry.

fields.name: Writers
fields.doc:
Writers is the multi-destination fan-out field; non-empty wires
the records through logger.Multi over per-writer console sinks.
Nil/empty falls back to Writer.

fields.name: MinLevel
fields.doc: MinLevel is the minimum severity emitted; zero value is LevelInfo.

symbols.doc:
Config carries the construction parameters accepted by NewText.
Two destination forms are supported — pick the one that fits:

  - Writer single — Writer: w. Records go to that one writer.
  - Writers fan-out — Writers: []io.Writer{a, b, c}. Records broadcast
    to every writer in order; per-branch failures are joined under
    FANOUT_WRITE_FAILED. Use this when you want stderr AND a log file
    in one go (a common ops pattern) without dropping to NewWithSink.

When BOTH are set, Writers wins and Writer is ignored. Use whichever
reads more naturally at the call site. Construction returns
WriterRequired (1.1.0.1) when neither field carries any writer.

symbols.name: ConsoleConfig
symbols.doc:
ConsoleConfig configures the "console" writer (stream + optional MinLevel).
The zero value targets os.Stderr (ADR 0030).

symbols.name: ConsoleStderr
symbols.doc:
ConsoleStderr returns the stderr console Sink used by Default. Exposed
so callers building a Multi() topology can wire stderr alongside richer
transports without re-implementing the convenience constructor.

symbols.name: ConsoleStdout
symbols.doc:
ConsoleStdout returns the stdout console Sink. Same rationale as
ConsoleStderr — exposed for Multi() compositions.

symbols.name: ConsoleStream
symbols.doc:
ConsoleStream selects which standard stream the console writer targets. Its
zero value is StreamStderr (ADR 0030).

symbols.name: CredentialProvider
symbols.doc:
CredentialProvider yields short-lived credentials on demand for the network
writers; the SDK never logs or wraps the returned material.

symbols.name: CredentialValue
symbols.doc:
CredentialValue is the opaque, redacting credential set returned by a
CredentialProvider; its String output is always "<redacted>".

symbols.name: Debug
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, lg Logger, msg string, attrs ...Attr)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, lg github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Logger, msg string, attrs ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Attr)
symbols.doc: Debug emits a RecordEvent at LevelDebug through lg.

symbols.name: Default
symbols.doc:
Default returns a Logger writing INFO-and-above records to os.Stderr.
The stderr Writer is supplied explicitly here; NewText itself no longer
silently defaults a nil Writer.

symbols.name: DefaultMulti
symbols.doc:
DefaultMulti returns a Logger that fans INFO-and-above records out to BOTH
the console (stderr, the ConsoleConfig zero value — ADR 0030) AND a plain
file at path.
It is the batteries-included "perfect default" the SDK recommends for a
service: two destinations from one call, with NO rotation surface — the
plain "file" writer never rotates, so rotation stays opt-in (a caller wanting
size/age rotation reaches for the rotating writer explicitly).

Unlike Default (stderr-only, no extra import), DefaultMulti resolves the
"console" and "file" writers through the registry, so the CALLER MUST
blank-import the writer package to activate them:

	import (
	    "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger"
	    _ "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger/writer" // console + file
	)

	lg, err := logger.DefaultMulti("/var/log/app.log")

Without that import the file/console Names do not resolve and DefaultMulti
returns the registry's WriterUnknownName, surfaced through NewMulti.

Like every Logger NewMulti returns, it owns the writers it opened and
implements io.Closer: Close releases the console writer and the file.

symbols.name: Duration
symbols.doc: Duration builds an Attr carrying a time.Duration value.

symbols.name: Encoder
symbols.doc:
Encoder is the stable alias for the internal service encoder interface.
The default text encoder is exposed via TextEncoder; structured output is
injected through NewWithSink via SinkConfig.Encoder (see NewJSONEncoder)
when callers need machine-readable output.

symbols.name: Error
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, lg Logger, msg string, attrs ...Attr)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, lg github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Logger, msg string, attrs ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Attr)
symbols.doc: Error emits a RecordEvent at LevelError through lg.

symbols.name: FileConfig
symbols.doc: FileConfig configures the "file" writer (path + optional MinLevel).

symbols.name: Float64
symbols.doc: Float64 builds an Attr carrying a float64 value.

symbols.name: Format
symbols.doc:
Format is the typed wire-format identifier accepted by FromConfig. It is a
stable alias onto the core codec dispatch surface, so a consumer names a
format with the same string values the codec facade exposes.

symbols.name: FrameworkVersion
symbols.doc: FrameworkVersion returns the linked-in SDK version, or "dev" if unset.

symbols.name: FromConfig
symbols.spelled: func(format Format, raw []byte) (lg Logger, err error)
symbols.doc:
FromConfig builds a Logger from raw, a config blob in the wire format named by
format, decoded by a codec the consumer has already registered (blank-import
github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/codec or a single service codec to activate
one). It unmarshals raw into a Topology, resolves each WriterEntry against the
writer registry — calling the Factory's ConfigDecoder when it implements one,
else a default mapping — composes the sinks via Multi, and returns a Logger
filtered at the topology's Level.

FromConfig returns TopologyInvalid (1.1.0.4) when format is unregistered, the
blob is undecodable, the topology has no writers, a writer Name is unknown, or
a writer rejects its options. The error is redacted: it names only the writer
and the failure kind, never a decoded credential or option value.

Like NewMulti's, the returned Logger owns the writers it opened — the caller
never held them — and implements io.Closer to release them, once.

symbols.name: Info
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, lg Logger, msg string, attrs ...Attr)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, lg github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Logger, msg string, attrs ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Attr)
symbols.doc: Info emits a RecordEvent at LevelInfo through lg.

symbols.name: Int
symbols.doc: Int builds an Attr carrying an int value.

symbols.name: Int64
symbols.doc: Int64 builds an Attr carrying an int64 value.

symbols.name: Kind
symbols.doc:
Kind is the stable alias for the internal payload discriminant carried by a
Value. Switch on it to select the matching typed accessor (String, Int64,
Float64, …) instead of paying for an `any` assertion at render time.

symbols.name: KindAny
symbols.doc:
KindAny tags a Value whose payload is an unconstrained interface. It is also
the zero value of Kind, so an unrecognised future variant degrades here
rather than panicking.

symbols.name: KindBool
symbols.doc: KindBool tags a Value carrying a boolean payload.

symbols.name: KindDuration
symbols.doc: KindDuration tags a Value carrying a time.Duration payload.

symbols.name: KindFloat64
symbols.doc: KindFloat64 tags a Value carrying a float64 payload.

symbols.name: KindGroup
symbols.doc:
KindGroup tags a Value whose payload is a nested []Attr. Producers that
target the bundled text and JSON encoders flatten groups into dotted keys
instead, since neither encoder renders a group payload directly.

symbols.name: KindInt64
symbols.doc:
KindInt64 tags a Value carrying an int64 payload (also covers int / int32,
which IntValue widens on the way in).

symbols.name: KindString
symbols.doc: KindString tags a Value carrying a string payload.

symbols.name: KindTime
symbols.doc: KindTime tags a Value carrying a time.Time payload.

symbols.name: KindUint64
symbols.doc: KindUint64 tags a Value carrying an unsigned 64-bit integer payload.

symbols.name: Level
symbols.doc: Level is the stable alias for the internal severity type.

symbols.name: LevelDebug
symbols.doc: LevelDebug selects records describing detailed tracing information.

symbols.name: LevelError
symbols.doc: LevelError selects records describing failures needing action.

symbols.name: LevelGate
symbols.doc:
LevelGate returns a Sink that passes to sink the records whose level is at
or above min and drops the others, delegating Flush and Close. It is how one
branch of a [Multi] fan-out sees less than another: the pipeline's
[SinkConfig].MinLevel is set to the lowest level any branch wants, and the
narrower branches are gated.

The floor is the one given, for every level — Info included. A dropped
record reports success (every byte accepted, no error), so a fan-out never
counts it as a failed write. The gate holds nothing of its own: Flush and
Close reach sink unchanged, and closing the gate closes sink.

A nil sink yields nil, which [Multi] skips and [NewWithSink] refuses with
[SinkConfigRequired].

symbols.name: LevelInfo
symbols.doc: LevelInfo selects records describing routine operational events.

symbols.name: LevelVar
symbols.doc:
LevelVar is the stable alias for the atomic Level holder. Its zero value
reports LevelInfo; Set and Level are safe for concurrent use, so one
goroutine can retune the floor while a sink reads it on the hot path.

symbols.name: LevelWarn
symbols.doc: LevelWarn selects records describing abnormal but recoverable conditions.

symbols.name: Leveler
symbols.doc:
Leveler is the stable alias for the internal one-method level port. A custom
Sink reads Level on each record so the threshold can change at runtime; both
LevelVar and any constant-returning type satisfy it.

symbols.name: LogAttrs
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, lg Logger, lv Level, msg string, attrs []Attr)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, lg github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Logger, lv github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Level, msg string, attrs []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Attr)
symbols.doc:
LogAttrs is the slice-overload of Logger.Log that avoids the variadic
slice allocation imposed by Logger.Log(... Attr). Pre-built attribute
slices flow through this entry point without per-call boxing.

symbols.name: Logger
symbols.doc: Logger is the stable alias for the internal core.Logger interface.

symbols.name: MemorySink
symbols.doc:
MemorySink is a Sink that buffers a defensive snapshot of every received
record in a mutex-guarded slice. It is intended for tests that assert on
what was logged. Pass it to NewWithSink (it satisfies Sink), retrieve the
buffered records with Records, and clear them with Reset.

symbols.name: Multi
symbols.doc:
Multi is a thin wrapper around the internal multi (fan-out) sink. It
broadcasts every record to each branch in order and aggregates per-sink
failures via errors.Join under the FANOUT_WRITE_FAILED sentinel.

symbols.name: NewCredentialValue
symbols.spelled: func(accessKeyID string, secretAccessKey string, sessionToken string) CredentialValue
symbols.canonical: func(accessKeyID string, secretAccessKey string, sessionToken string) github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.CredentialValue
symbols.doc:
NewCredentialValue builds a CredentialValue from AWS SigV4 material. An empty
sessionToken is valid for long-lived keys.

symbols.name: NewJSONEncoder
symbols.doc:
NewJSONEncoder returns a structured single-line JSON encoder, rendering each
record as one encoding/json-compatible object per line:
{"ts":…,"level":…,"msg":…,<flat attrs>}. Grouped attributes flatten to
dotted keys ("g1.g2.key") to match the text encoder's convention. Pass it to
NewWithSink via SinkConfig.Encoder for machine-readable output.

symbols.name: NewLevelVar
symbols.doc:
NewLevelVar returns a LevelVar seeded with initial. Hold the returned pointer
where a sink or gate can read its Level, then call Set to raise or lower the
live threshold. Pair it with ParseLevel to retune from an env or flag value.

symbols.name: NewMemorySink
symbols.doc: NewMemorySink returns an empty MemorySink ready to record received records.

symbols.name: NewMulti
symbols.spelled: func(min Level, specs ...WriterSpec) (lg Logger, err error)
symbols.doc:
NewMulti builds a Logger that fans every record out to all specs, each
resolved to a Sink by its registered factory and composed through Multi.
Records are filtered at min (the handler-global level); a spec's own MinLevel
can restrict an individual writer further.

Each writer's package MUST be imported for its Name to resolve: blank-import
pkg/v1/observe/logger/writer for console + file, and third-party/aws/writer/{s3,cloudwatch}
for the AWS writers. An unresolved Name returns the registry's
WriterUnknownName; an empty specs list returns WriterSpecInvalid.

The returned Logger OWNS the writers NewMulti opened — the caller never held
them — and implements io.Closer to release them: Close drains what an
asynchronous writer still holds and closes every writer, once, whatever the
number of calls. Loggers derived with With or WithGroup share the writers and
own none of them; closing one releases nothing. Until Close, the writers live
as long as the Logger does, and a file one opened cannot be deleted or
rotated by another program on Windows:

	lg, err := logger.NewMulti(logger.LevelInfo, specs...)
	if err != nil { … }
	defer lg.(io.Closer).Close()

	import (
	    "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger"
	    _ "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger/writer" // console + file
	)

	lg, err := logger.NewMulti(logger.LevelInfo,
	    logger.WriterSpec{Name: "console", Config: logger.ConsoleConfig{Stream: logger.StreamStderr}},
	    logger.WriterSpec{Name: "file",    Config: logger.FileConfig{Path: "/var/log/app.log"}},
	)

symbols.name: NewText
symbols.doc:
NewText builds a text-format Logger writing to cfg.Writer (single) OR
cfg.Writers (fan-out) filtered at cfg.MinLevel. NewText intentionally
does NOT default a nil destination: callers that want stderr use
Default(), which supplies it explicitly. Every record emitted through
the returned Logger carries a "framework_version" attr.

Multi-writer example — stream identical text records to stderr AND a
log file:

	f, _ := os.OpenFile("/var/log/myapp.log", os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)
	lg, err := logger.NewText(logger.Config{
	    Writers:  []io.Writer{os.Stderr, f},
	    MinLevel: logger.LevelInfo,
	})

symbols.name: NewTextEncoder
symbols.doc:
NewTextEncoder returns the default human-readable encoder, rendering each
record as "TIME LEVEL msg key=val …\n" with RFC3339-millisecond timestamps.
It is a named peer of TextEncoder bound to the real system clock.

symbols.name: NewWithSink
symbols.doc:
NewWithSink builds a Logger forwarding records through cfg.Sink and
formatting them with cfg.Encoder. It is the port-and-adapter entry point
for callers that want full control over both the format (Encoder) and
the transport (Sink); use NewText for the default text-on-stderr wiring.

symbols.name: NewWriterSink
symbols.doc:
NewWriterSink wraps an arbitrary [io.Writer] in a [Sink] so callers can
compose plain file / network / bytes.Buffer writers with [Multi] for
fan-out. The returned Sink serialises Write calls through an internal
mutex (identical contract to [ConsoleStderr] / [ConsoleStdout]).

Returns [WriterRequired] when w is nil.

	f, _ := os.OpenFile("/var/log/app.log", os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)
	fileSink, _ := logger.NewWriterSink(f)
	lg, _ := logger.NewWithSink(logger.SinkConfig{
	    Sink: logger.Multi(logger.ConsoleStderr(), fileSink),
	})

symbols.name: ParseLevel
symbols.doc:
ParseLevel maps a canonical lowercase level name (debug / info / warn /
error) to its Level, the strict inverse of a lowercased Level.String. Input
is trimmed and lowercased before matching. Unknown names return the zero
Level and a redacted LevelUnknown error — the offending input is never echoed.

Unlike the internal best-effort config path, this surface reports the miss so
a caller validating an env/flag value can reject it rather than silently
falling back to Info.

symbols.name: Record
symbols.doc:
Record is the stable alias for the internal RecordEvent value passed to
Sink.Write. Consumers implementing custom Sinks reach for this type
rather than reimporting the internal core.logger package.

symbols.name: RecordSnapshot
symbols.doc:
RecordSnapshot is a buffered copy of a single recorded log event. It is the
element type returned by MemorySink.Records, letting tests assert on a
record's Level, Message, and Attrs without parsing an encoder's byte output.
It is the same type as Record (an alias of the core RecordEvent).

symbols.name: RotFileConfig
symbols.doc:
RotFileConfig configures the "rotfile" writer — a size- and/or age-capped,
optionally gzip-compressed on-disk file that rotates Path -> Path.1 … up to
MaxBackups (Path / MaxBytes / MaxBackups / MaxAgeDays / Compress / RotateEvery
/ MinLevel). Usable as a value once
github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger/writer is blank-imported (it
self-registers the "rotfile" factory alongside console and file); pass it via
WriterSpec{Name: "rotfile", Config: cfg} to NewMulti.

symbols.name: S3Config
symbols.doc:
S3Config configures the "s3" writer. Usable as a value without the AWS SDK;
it resolves to a working sink only once third-party/aws/writer/s3 is imported.

symbols.name: Sink
symbols.doc:
Sink is the stable alias for the internal core.Sink port. Consumers
compose Sink instances (console / file / syslog / async / multi …) and
pass them to NewWithSink to wire a custom transport pipeline.

symbols.name: SinkConfig
symbols.spelled: struct{Sink Sink; Encoder Encoder; MinLevel Level}

fields.name: Sink
fields.doc: Sink is the destination transport; nil yields SinkConfigRequired.

fields.name: Encoder
fields.doc: Encoder formats records into bytes; nil falls back to the text encoder.

fields.name: MinLevel
fields.doc: MinLevel is the minimum severity emitted; zero value is LevelInfo.

symbols.doc:
SinkConfig carries the construction parameters accepted by NewWithSink.
A zero-valued SinkConfig{Sink: s} is enough to ship records through s at
LevelInfo using the default text encoder bound to the real wall clock.

symbols.name: SinkConfigRequired

code.public: Logger SinkConfig requires an explicit sink

symbols.doc:
SinkConfigRequired is returned when NewWithSink is called with
SinkConfig.Sink==nil. Callers that want a console sink use
logger.ConsoleStderr / ConsoleStdout or stick to logger.Default()
for the legacy text-on-stderr wiring.

symbols.name: StreamStderr
symbols.doc:
StreamStderr selects os.Stderr for the console writer (zero value, so a
ConsoleConfig{} written without an opinion lands here — ADR 0030).

symbols.name: StreamStdout
symbols.doc:
StreamStdout selects os.Stdout for the console writer. Because stdout is
a protocol channel for many processes, it is reachable only by name.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc: String builds an Attr carrying a string value.

symbols.name: TextEncoder
symbols.doc:
TextEncoder returns a fresh text Encoder bound to the real system clock.
Callers passing a custom Encoder to NewWithSink usually want this as a
starting point — it is the same encoder NewText / Default rely on.

symbols.name: Time
symbols.doc: Time builds an Attr carrying a time.Time value.

symbols.name: TopologyConfig
symbols.spelled: struct{Level string "json:\"level\" yaml:\"level\" toml:\"level\""; Writers []WriterEntryConfig "json:\"writers\" yaml:\"writers\" toml:\"writers\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{Level string "json:\"level\" yaml:\"level\" toml:\"level\""; Writers []github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.WriterEntryConfig "json:\"writers\" yaml:\"writers\" toml:\"writers\""}

fields.name: Level
fields.doc: Level is the minimum severity emitted, by name; empty defaults to info.

fields.name: Writers
fields.doc: Writers is the ordered set of named writer entries to fan records out to.

symbols.doc:
TopologyConfig is the decoded logger configuration: a global Level (parsed by
the same names the level package prints — "debug" / "info" / "warn" /
"error", case-insensitive, empty defaults to info) and the ordered Writers
fanned out to. FromConfig unmarshals a config blob into a TopologyConfig via a
consumer-registered codec, then resolves each entry against the writer
registry. The Config role suffix marks it a config DTO (KTN-STRUCT-ROLE).

symbols.name: TopologyInvalid

code.public: Logger topology config is invalid

symbols.doc:
TopologyInvalid is returned by FromConfig when the config blob cannot be
decoded, names a writer no imported package has registered, or a writer's
Factory/DecodeConfig rejected its options. The message is redacted: it
names only the writer and the failure kind, never a decoded credential or
option value (the SECRET GATE of ADR 0014 §D5).

symbols.name: TraceContext
symbols.doc:
TraceContext is the stable alias for the trace correlation a Record carries:
the trace and span identifiers of the span the record was emitted inside.
The zero value means "no trace here" and renders nothing.

symbols.name: TraceContextFromContext
symbols.doc:
TraceContextFromContext reads the span identity carried by ctx and returns
it in the shape a log record carries.

It is the adapter between [github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/trace]'s
SpanContext and the logger's TraceContext: the two identifiers, without the
flags and the tracestate, because a log line answers "which span produced
this?" and nothing else.

An absent, unsampled-and-absent or malformed span context yields the zero
value, and the encoders then emit no trace_id and no span_id at all — never
an empty string and never the all-zero identifier, both of which W3C Trace
Context §3.2.2.3/§3.2.2.4 declare invalid.

It allocates nothing: the context walk returns a value type, and the two
identifiers are fixed-size arrays copied by assignment.

symbols.name: TraceContextSource
symbols.doc:
TraceContextSource is the stable alias for the port that reads a
TraceContext off a context.Context. Every Logger built by this package is
wired to TraceContextFromContext.

symbols.name: Uint64
symbols.doc: Uint64 builds an Attr carrying a uint64 value.

symbols.name: Version
symbols.doc:
Version is overridden at build time via

	go build -ldflags "-X github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Version=v0.1.0"

Leave it as the zero value in local dev; FrameworkVersion returns "dev".

symbols.name: Warn
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, lg Logger, msg string, attrs ...Attr)
symbols.canonical: func(ctx context.Context, lg github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Logger, msg string, attrs ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/logger.Attr)
symbols.doc: Warn emits a RecordEvent at LevelWarn through lg.

symbols.name: WithCaller
symbols.doc:
WithCaller returns a derived Logger whose emitted records carry a "source"
attribute resolving the call site into file:line:function. The skip argument
is the extra stack-frame offset reserved for wrapper layers; pass 0 for
direct callers. The returned Logger shares the original's sink and encoder;
the only change is the added annotation, so the option is safe to layer onto
any Logger built by this package.

	lg, _ := logger.Default()
	lg = logger.WithCaller(lg, 0)
	lg.Info(ctx, "ready") // record now carries source=…/main.go:42:main.run

symbols.name: WithError
symbols.doc:
WithError decomposes err into structured log Attrs so the SDK's dotted-quad
typed errors become first-class structured data rather than a flat string.

For an SDK error it emits error.code, error.reason and error.public, then one
error.trail.<n> Attr per wrap-trail code (newest wrap last). Empty metadata
fields are skipped. For a plain stdlib error it falls back to a single
error.message Attr. A nil err yields no Attrs.

The result is meant to be spread into an emission call, e.g.
logger.Error(ctx, lg, "op failed", logger.WithError(err)...).

symbols.name: WriterEntryConfig
symbols.spelled: struct{Name string "json:\"name\" yaml:\"name\" toml:\"name\""; Options map[string]any "json:\"config\" yaml:\"config\" toml:\"config\""}
symbols.canonical: struct{Name string "json:\"name\" yaml:\"name\" toml:\"name\""; Options map[string]any "json:\"config\" yaml:\"config\" toml:\"config\""}

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the registered writer key ("console" / "file" / "s3" / …).

fields.name: Options
fields.doc: Options is the raw, codec-decoded per-writer option map.

symbols.doc:
WriterEntryConfig names one writer in a TopologyConfig and carries its raw
option map as decoded from the config blob. Name MUST match a writer
registered via a blank-import; Options is the per-writer option bag handed to
the writer's Decoder (when it implements one) or passed straight to the
factory's Open otherwise. Option values are never echoed into an error — the
SECRET GATE redacts them. The Config role suffix marks it a config DTO
(KTN-STRUCT-ROLE).

symbols.name: WriterName
symbols.doc:
WriterName is the stable alias for a registered writer key
("console" / "file" / "rotfile" / "s3" / "cloudwatch").

symbols.name: WriterRequired

code.public: Logger config requires an explicit writer

symbols.doc:
WriterRequired is returned when NewText is called with Config.Writer==nil.
Callers that want the "stderr convenience" use Default() instead.

symbols.name: WriterSpec
symbols.doc:
WriterSpec names a writer and carries its concrete config. Read at call sites
as logger.WriterSpec{Name: "file", Config: logger.FileConfig{Path: …}}. It is
a type alias onto internal/core/observe/logger/writer, so the public type is identity-equal
to the internal writer model (alias-based public surface, zero runtime cost).

symbols.name: WriterSpecInvalid

code.public: NewMulti requires at least one writer spec

symbols.doc:
WriterSpecInvalid is returned when NewMulti is called with zero
WriterSpec entries. Supply at least one named writer (and blank-import
its package) so the fan-out has a destination.

symbols.name: CodeLoggerRequired
symbols.doc:
CodeLoggerRequired identifies a NewHandler / New call with a nil Logger.
The bridge refuses to build a handler that discards silently: its whole
purpose is to guarantee a single pipeline, and a bridge to nowhere would
break that guarantee precisely where the caller believed it held.

symbols.name: LoggerRequired

code.public: slog bridge requires an explicit logger

symbols.doc:
LoggerRequired is returned when NewHandler or New is called with a nil
Logger. Build the destination first (logger.NewText / NewWithSink /
Default), then bridge it — there is no "default destination" here, by the
same reasoning that made NewText refuse to default to stderr (ADR 0002).

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New returns a *slog.Logger writing through lg — the one-liner a caller hands
to a library whose logging knob is typed as the concrete *slog.Logger.

A nil lg returns [LoggerRequired] (1.1.1.1).

symbols.name: NewHandler
symbols.doc:
NewHandler returns an slog.Handler that forwards every record to lg.

A nil lg returns [LoggerRequired] (1.1.1.1) rather than a handler that
silently discards: this package exists to guarantee one pipeline, and a
bridge to nowhere would defeat the guarantee at the exact moment a caller
believed it held.

symbols.name: AsyncMeter
symbols.doc:
AsyncMeter is the public alias for the sibling port that registers
observable (asynchronous) instruments.

symbols.name: Attr
symbols.doc: Attr is the public alias for one typed dimension of a series.

symbols.name: AttrKind
symbols.doc: AttrKind is the public alias for an attribute value's type tag.

symbols.name: AttrKindBool
symbols.doc: AttrKindBool marks a bool-valued attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindFloat64
symbols.doc: AttrKindFloat64 marks an IEEE-754 double attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindInt64
symbols.doc: AttrKindInt64 marks a signed 64-bit integer attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindInvalid
symbols.doc: AttrKindInvalid marks an attribute whose value no constructor ever set.

symbols.name: AttrKindString
symbols.doc: AttrKindString marks a string-valued attribute.

symbols.name: AvailableExporters
symbols.doc: AvailableExporters returns the sorted list of registered exporter names.

symbols.name: Bool
symbols.doc: Bool returns a bool-valued attribute.

symbols.name: Counter
symbols.doc: Counter is the public alias for a monotonic sum instrument.

symbols.name: DefaultMaxSeriesPerInstrument
symbols.doc:
DefaultMaxSeriesPerInstrument is the cardinality bound NewMeter applies,
and the value a non-positive MeterConfig knob clamps to.

symbols.name: DefaultOTLPMaxResponseBytes
symbols.doc:
DefaultOTLPMaxResponseBytes caps how much of a collector's response is
read. The body is the one length a remote party controls in this
exchange, and a conforming response is a few hundred bytes.

symbols.name: DefaultOTLPTimeout
symbols.doc:
DefaultOTLPTimeout bounds one OTLP/HTTP export round trip when
OTLPHTTPConfig leaves Timeout unset. It is the OpenTelemetry protocol
exporter specification's own default, not a figure this SDK invented.

symbols.name: DefaultScopeName
symbols.doc:
DefaultScopeName names this SDK as the instrumenting library when a
caller declares no scope of their own.

symbols.name: Describer
symbols.doc:
Describer is the public alias for the sibling port that documents an
instrument NAME. It is deliberately NOT part of FullMeter — reach it by type
assertion, and read the false case as "this meter records no description".

symbols.name: DescriptionConflict

code.public: That instrument name already carries a different description

symbols.doc:
DescriptionConflict is raised when a second, DIFFERENT description is
bound to an instrument name that already has one.

symbols.name: EncodeOTLPJSON
symbols.doc:
EncodeOTLPJSON renders snap as ONE OTLP/JSON ExportMetricsServiceRequest:
exactly the bytes that go in the body of a POST to /v1/metrics under
Content-Type: application/json.

It does no I/O, so it is the half of OTLP support that is testable on its
own — and the half NewOTLPHTTPExporter calls before it touches a socket.

symbols.name: Export
symbols.doc: Export ships snap through the exporter registered as name.

symbols.name: ExportFailed

code.public: The metrics exporter failed to ship the snapshot

symbols.doc: ExportFailed wraps an exporter's shipping failure.

symbols.name: Exporter
symbols.doc: Exporter is the public alias for a snapshot shipper.

symbols.name: ExporterName
symbols.doc: ExporterName is the public alias for an exporter's registry key.

symbols.name: Float64
symbols.doc:
Float64 returns a double attribute. A float is a measurement rather than a
dimension, and it is keyed on its bit pattern — see the core documentation.

symbols.name: Float64Callback
symbols.doc: Float64Callback is the public alias for a double observable's callback.

symbols.name: FullMeter
symbols.doc:
FullMeter is the public alias for the union of all three — what NewMeter
returns.

symbols.name: Gauge
symbols.doc: Gauge is the public alias for a sampled-reading instrument.

symbols.name: GaugeMetric
symbols.doc: GaugeMetric is the public alias for every series of one gauge instrument name.

symbols.name: GaugePoint
symbols.doc: GaugePoint is the public alias for one gauge series.

symbols.name: Histogram
symbols.doc: Histogram is the public alias for a bucketed distribution instrument.

symbols.name: HistogramMetric
symbols.doc:
HistogramMetric is the public alias for every series of one histogram
instrument name, plus its temporality.

symbols.name: HistogramPoint
symbols.doc: HistogramPoint is the public alias for one histogram series.

symbols.name: InstrumentKindConflict

code.public: That instrument name is already registered with a different kind

symbols.doc: InstrumentKindConflict is raised when a name is reused across kinds.

symbols.name: Int64
symbols.doc: Int64 returns a signed-integer attribute.

symbols.name: Int64Callback
symbols.doc: Int64Callback is the public alias for an integer observable's callback.

symbols.name: InvalidAttribute

code.public: An attribute key is empty or repeated, or its value was never set

symbols.doc:
InvalidAttribute is raised when an attribute set has an empty or
repeated key, or a value no constructor ever set.

symbols.name: InvalidDescription

code.public: An instrument description must not be empty

symbols.doc:
InvalidDescription is raised when Describe is handed an empty
description, which would document nothing.

symbols.name: InvalidLabelName

code.public: An attribute key is not a valid Prometheus label name

symbols.doc:
InvalidLabelName is returned by the Prometheus connector when an
attribute key is not a valid Prometheus label name.

symbols.name: InvalidMetricName

code.public: An instrument name is not a valid Prometheus metric name

symbols.doc:
InvalidMetricName is returned by the Prometheus connector when an
instrument name is not a valid Prometheus metric name.

symbols.name: InvalidTemporality

code.public: That aggregation temporality is not one this SDK declares

symbols.doc:
InvalidTemporality is raised when a MeterConfig carries a Temporality
that is none of the three constants.

symbols.name: Meter
symbols.doc:
Meter is the public alias for the frozen instrument factory: Counter, Gauge,
Histogram and Collect.

symbols.name: MeterConfig
symbols.doc: MeterConfig is the public alias for a Meter's configuration.

symbols.name: NewMeter
symbols.doc:
NewMeter returns a fresh in-memory Meter with every MeterConfig knob at its
resolved default: bounded at DefaultMaxSeriesPerInstrument, cumulative,
service.name=unknown_service, this SDK as the scope, and the system clock.

symbols.name: NewMeterWithConfig
symbols.doc:
NewMeterWithConfig returns a fresh in-memory Meter honouring cfg. Every unset
field resolves to a working value and none of them to an inert one.

symbols.name: NewOTLPHTTPExporter
symbols.spelled: func(name ExporterName, cfg OTLPHTTPConfig) (exporter Exporter, err error)
symbols.doc:
NewOTLPHTTPExporter returns an Exporter that encodes each snapshot as
OTLP/JSON and POSTs it to cfg.Endpoint, which is a full URL used as-is.

It is never registered, and it never retries — compose resilience.NewRetry
with OTLPRetryable instead. A refused endpoint fails here, at wiring, rather
than at the first scrape.

symbols.name: NewOTLPJSONExporter
symbols.doc:
NewOTLPJSONExporter returns an Exporter writing each snapshot to dst as one
newline-terminated OTLP/JSON document, so a stream of exports is NDJSON. It
is not auto-registered; the registered "otlpjson" exporter is this, on
stderr.

symbols.name: NewPrometheusExporter
symbols.doc:
NewPrometheusExporter returns an Exporter rendering the Prometheus text
exposition format to dst under name (not auto-registered). Hand it the
http.ResponseWriter of a /metrics handler; the registered "prometheus"
exporter targets stderr and is a diagnostic, not a scrape endpoint.

symbols.name: NewTextExporter
symbols.doc:
NewTextExporter returns a text Exporter writing to dst under name (not
auto-registered).

symbols.name: OTLPEndpointInvalid

code.public: The OTLP endpoint is not an absolute http or https URL with a path

symbols.doc:
OTLPEndpointInvalid is returned by NewOTLPHTTPExporter when the endpoint
is not an absolute http(s) URL carrying the signal path.

symbols.name: OTLPExportRejected

code.public: The OTLP collector rejected the metrics payload

symbols.doc:
OTLPExportRejected is returned when a collector refuses the payload with
a status the specification marks non-retryable.

symbols.name: OTLPExportUnavailable

code.public: The OTLP collector is unreachable or overloaded

symbols.doc:
OTLPExportUnavailable is returned when an OTLP/HTTP export fails
transiently — a transport fault, or HTTP 429/502/503/504. It is the one
OTLPRetryable reports true for.

symbols.name: OTLPHTTPConfig
symbols.doc: OTLPHTTPConfig is the public alias for an OTLP/HTTP exporter's configuration.

symbols.name: OTLPInvalidBucketLayout

code.public: That histogram's buckets have no OTLP representation

symbols.doc:
OTLPInvalidBucketLayout is returned by the OTLP/JSON encoder when a
histogram's buckets are not one count more than strictly-increasing
finite bounds.

symbols.name: OTLPMetricsPath
symbols.doc:
OTLPMetricsPath is the URL path OTLP/HTTP reserves for the metrics
signal. An OTLP endpoint is a full URL used as-is, so append this to a
collector's base address rather than hoping the SDK guesses it.

symbols.name: OTLPPartialSuccess

code.public: The OTLP collector accepted the request but rejected some data points

symbols.doc:
OTLPPartialSuccess is returned when a collector accepts the request but
rejects some of its data points. The specification forbids retrying it.

symbols.name: OTLPRetryable
symbols.doc:
OTLPRetryable reports whether err is an OTLP/HTTP failure the specification
says may be replayed: a transport fault, or HTTP 429 / 502 / 503 / 504.
Its signature is resilience.RetryConfig.Retryable's, so it drops in without
an adapter.

symbols.name: OTLPUnresolvedTemporality

code.public: That aggregation temporality has no OTLP representation

symbols.doc:
OTLPUnresolvedTemporality is returned by the OTLP/JSON encoder when a
metric's temporality is neither delta nor cumulative. The schema's
UNSPECIFIED value is documented as one that MUST NOT be used.

symbols.name: ObserveFloat64
symbols.doc:
ObserveFloat64 is the public alias for the reporting function a double
observable callback is handed.

symbols.name: ObserveInt64
symbols.doc:
ObserveInt64 is the public alias for the reporting function an integer
observable callback is handed.

symbols.name: OverflowAttrKey
symbols.doc:
OverflowAttrKey is the reserved attribute naming a meter's aggregated
overflow series. It appears in a snapshot only once an instrument has
exceeded its cardinality bound, and its value is the boolean true.

symbols.name: RegisterExporter
symbols.doc: RegisterExporter adds e to the process-wide exporter registry.

symbols.name: ReservedLabelName

code.public: An attribute key is reserved by the Prometheus exposition format

symbols.doc:
ReservedLabelName is returned by the Prometheus connector when an
attribute key is legal but reserved — a "__" prefix, or "le" on a
histogram.

symbols.name: Resource
symbols.doc:
Resource is the public alias for the producer's identity, carried once per
snapshot.

symbols.name: Scope
symbols.doc:
Scope is the public alias for the instrumentation's identity, carried once
per snapshot.

symbols.name: ServiceNameKey
symbols.doc:
ServiceNameKey is the attribute key the OTel resource semantic
conventions reserve for the logical name of the service.

symbols.name: Snapshot
symbols.doc: Snapshot is the public alias for a whole-meter point-in-time copy.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc:
String returns a string-valued attribute. It is the shortest of the four
constructors to write because a string dimension is the common one.

symbols.name: SumMetric
symbols.doc:
SumMetric is the public alias for every series of one sum instrument name,
plus its temporality and monotonicity.

symbols.name: SumPoint
symbols.doc: SumPoint is the public alias for one sum series.

symbols.name: Temporality
symbols.doc: Temporality is the public alias for a metric's aggregation temporality.

symbols.name: TemporalityCumulative
symbols.doc: TemporalityCumulative reports the window since the series started.

symbols.name: TemporalityDelta
symbols.doc: TemporalityDelta reports the window since the previous collection.

symbols.name: TemporalityUnspecified
symbols.doc:
TemporalityUnspecified is the unset zero value; it resolves to
TemporalityCumulative and never reaches a Snapshot.

symbols.name: UnknownExporter

code.public: No metrics exporter is registered under that name

symbols.doc: UnknownExporter is returned by Export when no exporter matches the name.

symbols.name: UnknownService
symbols.doc:
UnknownService is the service.name the specification mandates when a
producer supplies none.

symbols.name: UnsupportedTemporality

code.public: The Prometheus exposition format carries cumulative metrics only

symbols.doc:
UnsupportedTemporality is returned by the Prometheus connector when the
snapshot is not cumulative — a delta one, which the exposition format
cannot express, or a hand-built one whose temporality is unresolved.

symbols.name: UpDownCounter
symbols.doc: UpDownCounter is the public alias for a non-monotonic sum instrument.

symbols.name: UpDownMeter
symbols.doc:
UpDownMeter is the public alias for the sibling port that mints the
non-monotonic sum Meter cannot.

symbols.name: CanonicalName
symbols.doc: CanonicalName spells a function the same way whoever named it.

symbols.name: CaptureCPU
symbols.doc: CaptureCPU samples the process's CPU for window and returns the profile.

symbols.name: CaptureCanceled

code.public: The profile was abandoned before its window ended

symbols.doc:
CaptureCanceled is a CPU capture whose context ended before the window
(503); errors.Is still finds the context's error.

symbols.name: CaptureFailed

code.public: The profile could not be written

symbols.doc:
CaptureFailed wraps an error runtime/pprof returned while writing a
profile.

symbols.name: CaptureHeap
symbols.doc: CaptureHeap returns the live heap, after a garbage collection.

symbols.name: CodeCaptureCanceled
symbols.doc:
CodeCaptureCanceled identifies a CPU capture whose context ended before its
window (0.3.89.3).

symbols.name: CodeCaptureFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeCaptureFailed identifies a profile runtime/pprof could not write
(0.3.89.4).

symbols.name: CodeProfileMalformed
symbols.doc:
CodeProfileMalformed identifies bytes that are not a well-formed pprof
profile, or a hand-built profile Fold cannot read (0.3.89.5).

symbols.name: CodeProfileTooLarge
symbols.doc:
CodeProfileTooLarge identifies a profile over MaxProfileBytes, or whose
stacks exceed MaxFrames (0.3.89.6).

symbols.name: CodeProfilerBusy
symbols.doc:
CodeProfilerBusy identifies a CPU capture refused because the process's one
CPU profiler is running (0.3.89.2).

symbols.name: CodeSampleTypeMissing
symbols.doc:
CodeSampleTypeMissing identifies a fold asked for a sample type the profile
does not measure (0.3.89.7).

symbols.name: CodeWindowInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeWindowInvalid identifies a CPU window not positive or over MaxCPUWindow
(0.3.89.1).

symbols.name: DefaultFlameMaxDepth
symbols.doc:
DefaultFlameMaxDepth is how deep the flame graph goes when
FoldConfig.FlameMaxDepth is not positive.

symbols.name: DefaultFlameMinShare
symbols.doc:
DefaultFlameMinShare prunes a flame frame costing less than this share of
the total when FoldConfig.FlameMinShare is outside (0, 1): half a percent.

symbols.name: DefaultTopFunctions
symbols.doc:
DefaultTopFunctions is how many functions Folded.Top lists when
FoldConfig.TopFunctions is not positive.

symbols.name: DefaultTopPerOwner
symbols.doc:
DefaultTopPerOwner is how many functions each owner's Top lists when
FoldConfig.TopPerOwner is not positive.

symbols.name: FlameNode
symbols.doc: FlameNode is one frame of a flame graph.

symbols.name: FlameRoot
symbols.doc: FlameRoot is the name of a flame graph's root frame.

symbols.name: Fold
symbols.doc: Fold charges every sample of p to an owner and adds it all up.

symbols.name: FoldConfig
symbols.doc: FoldConfig says how Fold reads a profile; every zero field has a default.

symbols.name: Folded
symbols.doc: Folded is a profile folded, in the sample type's own unit.

symbols.name: Frame
symbols.doc: Frame is one frame of a stack.

symbols.name: FunctionCost
symbols.doc: FunctionCost is what one function cost.

symbols.name: Goroutine
symbols.doc: Goroutine is one goroutine, as the runtime's dump describes it.

symbols.name: GoroutineGroup
symbols.doc: GoroutineGroup is goroutines sharing their labels, state and top frame.

symbols.name: Goroutines
symbols.doc: Goroutines returns every goroutine of the process.

symbols.name: GroupConfig
symbols.doc: GroupConfig says how GroupGoroutines groups.

symbols.name: GroupGoroutines
symbols.doc:
GroupGoroutines groups goroutines by labels, state and top frame, largest
first.

symbols.name: MaxCPUWindow
symbols.doc: MaxCPUWindow is the longest window CaptureCPU samples.

symbols.name: MaxFrames
symbols.doc:
MaxFrames bounds the frames Parse builds: each location's once, and every
copy a sample's stack makes of them.

symbols.name: MaxProfileBytes
symbols.doc: MaxProfileBytes bounds what Parse reads, compressed and inflated alike.

symbols.name: OwnerCost
symbols.doc: OwnerCost is what one owner cost.

symbols.name: Parse
symbols.doc: Parse decodes a pprof profile, gzipped or not.

symbols.name: ParseGoroutines
symbols.doc: ParseGoroutines reads a goroutine dump; it never fails.

symbols.name: Profile
symbols.doc: Profile is a decoded pprof profile.

symbols.name: ProfileMalformed

code.public: That is not a well-formed pprof profile

symbols.doc:
ProfileMalformed refuses bytes that are not a well-formed pprof profile —
the field names the part, the input is never quoted — and a nil profile or
a sample short of values handed to Fold.

symbols.name: ProfileTooLarge

code.public: The profile is too large to read

symbols.doc:
ProfileTooLarge refuses a profile over MaxProfileBytes, compressed or
inflated, or whose stacks would take more than MaxFrames frames.

symbols.name: ProfilerBusy

code.public: A CPU profile is already being recorded

symbols.doc:
ProfilerBusy refuses a CPU capture while the process's one CPU profiler is
running, whoever started it (409).

symbols.name: Sample
symbols.doc: Sample is one sample: a stack, a value per sample type, and labels.

symbols.name: SampleType
symbols.doc: SampleType names what a value measures and its unit.

symbols.name: SampleTypeMissing

code.public: The profile does not measure that

symbols.doc:
SampleTypeMissing refuses a fold asked for a sample type the profile does
not measure.

symbols.name: WindowInvalid

code.public: A CPU profile needs a window longer than zero and at most five minutes

symbols.doc: WindowInvalid refuses a CPU window not positive or over MaxCPUWindow (400).

symbols.name: AlwaysSample
symbols.doc: AlwaysSample keeps every root trace.

symbols.name: Attr
symbols.doc:
Attr is one typed dimension. It is the SAME type as
[github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/observe/metrics.Attr], deliberately: an attribute is
OTel's common.proto, shared by every signal, so a value built for a metric is
accepted by a span and the reverse.

symbols.name: AttrKind
symbols.doc: AttrKind discriminates an Attr's value type.

symbols.name: AttrKindBool
symbols.doc: AttrKindBool marks a bool-valued attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindFloat64
symbols.doc: AttrKindFloat64 marks an IEEE-754 double attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindInt64
symbols.doc: AttrKindInt64 marks a signed 64-bit integer attribute.

symbols.name: AttrKindInvalid
symbols.doc: AttrKindInvalid is the zero value and names no type.

symbols.name: AttrKindString
symbols.doc: AttrKindString marks a string-valued attribute.

symbols.name: AvailableExporters
symbols.doc:
AvailableExporters returns the sorted list of registered names. The OTLP/HTTP
emitter never appears in it.

symbols.name: Bool
symbols.doc: Bool returns a bool-valued attribute.

symbols.name: Carrier
symbols.doc:
Carrier is the two-method surface a header set presents for propagation. It is
exactly http.Header's Get/Set pair, so http.Header satisfies it with no
adapter.

symbols.name: ClientMiddleware
symbols.doc:
ClientMiddleware returns a middleware tracing every outbound request and
INJECTING the traceparent into it. It decorates the RoundTripper, so no call
site can skip it, and it clones the request rather than mutating one the caller
still holds.

symbols.name: ContextWithSpanContext
symbols.doc:
ContextWithSpanContext returns a copy of parent carrying spanContext. An
invalid context is still stored: it is how "this scope deliberately has no
trace" is expressed, and it shadows any outer one.

symbols.name: DefaultMaxSpans
symbols.doc:
DefaultMaxSpans is a Recorder's default bound. There is no "unbounded"
