setting, because a buffer nobody drains is how a tracing integration takes a
process down.

symbols.name: DefaultOTLPMaxResponseBytes
symbols.doc: DefaultOTLPMaxResponseBytes caps the response body read: 1 MiB.

symbols.name: DefaultOTLPTimeout
symbols.doc:
DefaultOTLPTimeout bounds one export round trip: 10s, the OpenTelemetry
specification's own default for OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT.

symbols.name: DefaultScopeName
symbols.doc:
DefaultScopeName names this package as the instrumenting library when a caller
declares no scope. It is deliberately NOT the metrics one: a scope names the
library that produced THIS signal.

symbols.name: DuplicateRegistration

code.public: A trace exporter is already registered under that name

symbols.doc: DuplicateRegistration is the boot-time registry panic sentinel.

symbols.name: EncodeOTLPJSON
symbols.doc:
EncodeOTLPJSON renders spans as ONE OTLP/JSON ExportTraceServiceRequest —
exactly the bytes that go in the body of a POST to /v1/traces. It does no I/O,
so an encoding question never becomes a network question.

symbols.name: EntropyFailed

code.public: Trace identifier generation failed to read secure random bytes

symbols.doc:
EntropyFailed is kept for code that matches it: nothing returns it since
Go 1.24, whose crypto/rand.Read never fails, so minting an identifier
cannot fail.

symbols.name: Event
symbols.doc: Event is a timestamped point inside a span.

symbols.name: ExceptionEventName
symbols.doc: ExceptionEventName is the reserved event name RecordError writes.

symbols.name: ExceptionMessageKey
symbols.doc: ExceptionMessageKey names a recorded error's message.

symbols.name: ExceptionTypeKey
symbols.doc: ExceptionTypeKey names a recorded error's stable identity.

symbols.name: Export
symbols.doc: Export ships spans through the SpanExporter registered as name.

symbols.name: ExportFailed

code.public: The trace exporter failed to ship the spans

symbols.doc: ExportFailed wraps an exporter's failure.

symbols.name: ExporterName
symbols.doc: ExporterName is the typed key a SpanExporter registers under.

symbols.name: Extract
symbols.doc:
Extract reads a span context out of carrier, returning the invalid zero value
when there is nothing usable. It returns no error on purpose — see the package
documentation.

symbols.name: FlagSampled
symbols.doc:
FlagSampled is the traceparent sampled bit — the one flag version 00 defines,
and the one the whole sampling design travels in.

symbols.name: Float64
symbols.doc: Float64 returns a double attribute.

symbols.name: FormatTraceParent
symbols.doc:
FormatTraceParent renders a span context as a version-00 traceparent,
reporting ok=false when the context names no joinable span — an all-zero
identifier is a header every conforming receiver must ignore, so there is
nothing to write. Undefined flag bits are masked here, which is where this SDK
acts as a producer.

symbols.name: HTTPRequestMethodKey
symbols.doc: HTTPRequestMethodKey is the request method attribute the middlewares record.

symbols.name: HTTPResponseStatusCodeKey
symbols.doc: HTTPResponseStatusCodeKey is the response status attribute.

symbols.name: Inject
symbols.doc:
Inject writes context into carrier as a traceparent, plus a tracestate when the
vendor list is non-empty. An invalid context writes NOTHING — not an empty
header, not a zero-filled one.

symbols.name: Int64
symbols.doc: Int64 returns a signed-integer attribute.

symbols.name: InvalidAttribute

code.public: An attribute key is empty or repeated, or its value was never set

symbols.doc:
InvalidAttribute is the panic sentinel for an unusable attribute set —
an empty or repeated key, or a value no constructor set — on a span, an
event, a link or a Resource. It is this package's own code; the metrics
one is a different sentinel for the same defect in that signal.

symbols.name: InvalidSampleRatio

code.public: A sampling ratio must be greater than 0 and at most 1

symbols.doc:
InvalidSampleRatio reports a fraction Ratio will not accept — including
exactly 0, which also spells "unconfigured".

symbols.name: InvalidSpanName

code.public: A span name must not be empty

symbols.doc: InvalidSpanName is the panic sentinel for a Start with no name.

symbols.name: InvalidTraceParent

code.public: The traceparent header is not a valid W3C trace context

symbols.doc: InvalidTraceParent reports a traceparent header that cannot be read.

symbols.name: InvalidTraceState

code.public: The tracestate header is not a valid W3C trace state list

symbols.doc: InvalidTraceState reports a tracestate header that cannot be read.

symbols.name: Kind
symbols.doc: Kind says how a span relates to its neighbours.

symbols.name: KindClient
symbols.doc: KindClient is making an outbound synchronous request.

symbols.name: KindConsumer
symbols.doc: KindConsumer is handling a message enqueued earlier.

symbols.name: KindInternal
symbols.doc: KindInternal is work inside one process.

symbols.name: KindProducer
symbols.doc: KindProducer is enqueuing a message handled later, elsewhere.

symbols.name: KindServer
symbols.doc: KindServer is handling an inbound synchronous request.

symbols.name: KindUnspecified
symbols.doc: KindUnspecified is SPAN_KIND_UNSPECIFIED; it resolves to KindInternal.

symbols.name: Link
symbols.doc: Link points at a causally related span in another trace.

symbols.name: LookupExporter
symbols.doc: LookupExporter returns the SpanExporter registered under name.

symbols.name: MaxTraceStateMembers
symbols.doc:
MaxTraceStateMembers is the W3C list cap: 32 members, from the grammar itself
rather than from a ceiling this SDK invented.

symbols.name: NeverSample
symbols.doc:
NeverSample drops every root trace. It exists so "off" has a NAME a reviewer
can grep for, rather than a rate of zero that is indistinguishable from a field
nobody set.

symbols.name: NewOTLPHTTPExporter
symbols.spelled: func(name ExporterName, cfg OTLPHTTPConfig) (exporter SpanExporter, err error)
symbols.doc:
NewOTLPHTTPExporter builds a SpanExporter that POSTs each batch to an OTLP
collector. It is deliberately NOT in the registry: arming a network client from
an import is worse than arming a writer, and no endpoint could be a correct
default. It does not retry either — use OTLPRetryable with
[github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/resilience].

symbols.name: NewOTLPJSONExporter
symbols.doc:
NewOTLPJSONExporter returns a SpanExporter writing each batch to dst as one
newline-terminated OTLP/JSON document. It is not registered — bind it yourself.

symbols.name: NewRecorder
symbols.doc:
NewRecorder builds the in-memory span destination. Its Sink is what a
TracerConfig takes, and its Collect DRAINS — a Recorder has exactly one reader.

symbols.name: NewSpanID
symbols.doc: NewSpanID draws a fresh random span identifier.

symbols.name: NewTraceID
symbols.doc: NewTraceID draws a fresh random trace identifier.

symbols.name: NewTracer
symbols.doc:
NewTracer builds a Tracer from cfg, applying every clamp once. It cannot fail:
every field of TracerConfig has a resolved meaning, and the inputs that CAN be
refused — a sampling ratio, an OTLP endpoint — are refused by their own
constructors before they reach here.

It returns the concrete [SDKTracer] rather than the [Tracer] port, so a caller
keeps Resource and Scope, and anything the concrete type grows later, without
the port having to grow (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: OTLPEndpointInvalid

code.public: The OTLP endpoint must be an absolute http(s) URL with a path

symbols.doc: OTLPEndpointInvalid reports an endpoint that cannot address a collector.

symbols.name: OTLPExportRejected

code.public: The trace collector rejected the export

symbols.doc: OTLPExportRejected reports a permanent refusal by the collector.

symbols.name: OTLPExportUnavailable

code.public: The trace collector is unavailable

symbols.doc: OTLPExportUnavailable reports a transient failure worth retrying.

symbols.name: OTLPHTTPConfig
symbols.doc: OTLPHTTPConfig configures the OTLP/HTTP exporter.

symbols.name: OTLPInvalidSpanContext

code.public: A span carries an all-zero trace or span identifier

symbols.doc: OTLPInvalidSpanContext reports a span with an all-zero identifier.

symbols.name: OTLPPartialSuccess

code.public: The trace collector accepted the request but rejected some spans

symbols.doc: OTLPPartialSuccess reports an accepted request with rejected spans.

symbols.name: OTLPRetryable
symbols.doc:
OTLPRetryable reports whether err is an OTLP/HTTP failure the specification
says may be replayed. Its signature is exactly resilience.RetryConfig.Retryable's.

symbols.name: OTLPSpanNotEnded

code.public: A span reached the exporter without an end time

symbols.doc: OTLPSpanNotEnded reports a span that reached the encoder unended.

symbols.name: OTLPTracesPath
symbols.doc:
OTLPTracesPath is the OTLP/HTTP path for the trace signal. Append it to a
collector's base URL yourself, so the whole address is one readable string.

symbols.name: ParentBased
symbols.doc:
ParentBased returns a Sampler that honours a valid parent's decision and
consults root only at the start of a trace. It is what almost every deployment
wants — see the package documentation on why re-deciding produces a trace with
holes in it. A nil root clamps to AlwaysSample.

symbols.name: ParseSpanID
symbols.doc: ParseSpanID reads 16 lowercase hex digits, refusing an all-zero result.

symbols.name: ParseTraceID
symbols.doc: ParseTraceID reads 32 lowercase hex digits, refusing an all-zero result.

symbols.name: ParseTraceParent
symbols.doc:
ParseTraceParent reads a traceparent header value, with a typed error. It is
the diagnostic form of Extract: use it when you are debugging a header, not
when you are serving a request.

symbols.name: ParseTraceState
symbols.doc:
ParseTraceState reads a tracestate header value. It refuses the whole header
rather than salvaging the members it understood: a half-parsed list forwarded
to the next hop is a list this process invented.

symbols.name: Ratio
symbols.doc:
Ratio returns a Sampler keeping a deterministic fraction of root traces,
decided on the trace id so two services reach the same verdict for the same id.

It REFUSES exactly 0, and that refusal is the point. A float64 left unset, a
JSON document missing the key and a YAML `rate:` with nothing after it all
produce 0.0 — so a rate of zero means both "sample nothing" and "nobody
configured this", and nothing in the type can tell them apart. The failure is
silent: no error, no log, and no telemetry, where the absence of telemetry IS
the symptom. Say NeverSample for none and AlwaysSample (or Ratio(1)) for all.

symbols.name: RecordError
symbols.doc:
RecordError records err on span as the conventional `exception` event and marks
the span ERROR.

It is a helper rather than a Span method because what an error's type is, and
whether recording one should also set the status, are judgements about the
caller's error model — and a port method would freeze this SDK's answer into
every downstream implementation (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: Recorder
symbols.doc:
Recorder accumulates finished spans in memory and hands them out in
batches. It is the in-tree SpanSink.

symbols.name: RecorderConfig
symbols.doc: RecorderConfig configures a Recorder.

symbols.name: RegisterExporter
symbols.doc:
RegisterExporter inserts e under e.Name(). It panics on a nil exporter or a
distinct exporter claiming a taken name.

symbols.name: Resource
symbols.doc:
Resource identifies the producer of the telemetry. The same type a MeterConfig
takes, so a process cannot carry two Resources that disagree about
service.name — which is the key a backend correlates a trace with a metric on.

symbols.name: SDKTracer
symbols.doc:
SDKTracer is the concrete [Tracer] that [NewTracer] returns: the port's
Start, plus Resource and Scope, which read back what it stamps on every
span it starts. The port keeps the name Tracer; this is the SDK's
implementation of it, in OpenTelemetry's sense of API and SDK. Name it
to keep a tracer in a field, or to pass one to a function of your own.

symbols.name: Sampler
symbols.doc:
Sampler decides whether a ROOT trace is recorded. A func port, so it cannot
grow a method at all.

symbols.name: SamplingParams
symbols.doc: SamplingParams is everything a Sampler sees.

symbols.name: Scope
symbols.doc: Scope identifies the instrumentation that started the spans.

symbols.name: ServerAddressKey
symbols.doc: ServerAddressKey is the host attribute.

symbols.name: ServerMiddleware
symbols.doc:
ServerMiddleware returns a middleware tracing every inbound request: it
extracts the parent context from the headers, starts a SERVER span named by the
request method, and records the status. A malformed traceparent starts a new
trace and never fails the request.

symbols.name: ServiceNameKey
symbols.doc:
ServiceNameKey is the resource attribute a backend joins a trace to a metric
on. It is the same constant pkg/v1/observe/metrics exports, so the two signals cannot
disagree about the spelling.

symbols.name: Span
symbols.doc: Span is one live, recording span. FROZEN at five methods (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: SpanContext
symbols.doc:
SpanContext is the immutable identity of a span — what travels in a
traceparent and what a child inherits.

symbols.name: SpanContextFromContext
symbols.doc:
SpanContextFromContext returns the span context carried by ctx, or the invalid
zero value when there is none.

symbols.name: SpanData
symbols.doc:
SpanData is one FINISHED span — what a SpanSink receives and an exporter
ships. The live one is [Span].

symbols.name: SpanExporter
symbols.doc: SpanExporter ships a batch of finished spans to a backend.

symbols.name: SpanID
symbols.doc:
SpanID identifies one span: eight octets, rendered as 16 lowercase hex
digits. The all-zero value is invalid, and is also how "no parent" is spelled.

symbols.name: SpanParams
symbols.doc:
SpanParams are the facts a span is born with. The zero value is an INTERNAL
span starting now.

symbols.name: SpanSink
symbols.doc: SpanSink receives every sampled span at End. A func port, for the same reason.

symbols.name: Spans
symbols.doc:
Spans is a batch of finished spans plus the Resource and Scope that describe
all of them.

symbols.name: Status
symbols.doc: Status is a span's recorded outcome.

symbols.name: StatusCode
symbols.doc: StatusCode is a span's verdict: unset, ok or error.

symbols.name: StatusError
symbols.doc: StatusError is a failure.

symbols.name: StatusOK
symbols.doc: StatusOK is an explicit success assertion by the developer.

symbols.name: StatusUnset
symbols.doc:
StatusUnset is the default: no explicit judgement. It does NOT mean "it
worked" — a backend applies its own heuristics, and claiming OK on the
caller's behalf would suppress them.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc: String returns a string-valued attribute.

symbols.name: TraceFlags
symbols.doc: TraceFlags is the traceparent flag byte. Only bit 0, sampled, is defined.

symbols.name: TraceID
symbols.doc:
TraceID identifies one trace: sixteen octets, rendered as 32 lowercase hex
digits. The all-zero value is invalid.

symbols.name: TraceParentHeader
symbols.doc: TraceParentHeader is the W3C header carrying the span context.

symbols.name: TraceParentLen
symbols.doc: TraceParentLen is the length of a version-00 traceparent: 55 characters.

symbols.name: TraceState
symbols.doc:
TraceState is the parsed tracestate header: an ordered vendor list, leftmost
first. Immutable.

symbols.name: TraceStateHeader
symbols.doc: TraceStateHeader is the W3C header carrying the vendor list.

symbols.name: Tracer
symbols.doc: Tracer starts spans. FROZEN at one method (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: TracerConfig
symbols.doc:
TracerConfig configures a Tracer. Every field has a resolved meaning
when left unset.

symbols.name: URLFullKey
symbols.doc: URLFullKey is the outbound URL attribute, recorded on CLIENT spans.

symbols.name: URLPathKey
symbols.doc: URLPathKey is the inbound request path attribute, in its ESCAPED form.

symbols.name: URLSchemeKey
symbols.doc: URLSchemeKey is the request scheme attribute.

symbols.name: UnknownExporter

code.public: No trace exporter is registered under that name

symbols.doc: UnknownExporter reports a name no imported package registered.

symbols.name: VersionSupported
symbols.doc: VersionSupported is the traceparent version this SDK emits: "00".

symbols.name: CapCgroup
symbols.doc: CapCgroup is a kernel-enforced resource container (cgroup.Create).

symbols.name: CapProcessSpawn
symbols.doc: CapProcessSpawn is spawning + supervising a child process (process.Start).

symbols.name: CapReaper
symbols.doc: CapReaper is zombie reaping / subreaping (reaper.New).

symbols.name: CapRlimit
symbols.doc: CapRlimit is applying per-process setrlimit-style limits (rlimit.Apply).

symbols.name: CapSdNotify
symbols.doc: CapSdNotify is the service-manager readiness/watchdog protocol (systemd/notify).

symbols.name: CapSignalRelay
symbols.doc: CapSignalRelay is forwarding signals to a pid / process group (signal.Relay).

symbols.name: CapSocketActivation
symbols.doc: CapSocketActivation is inheriting a pre-opened listening socket (systemd/listen).

symbols.name: CapUmaskNiceOOM
symbols.doc: CapUmaskNiceOOM is the spawn-time umask / nice / oom_score_adj knobs.

symbols.name: Capability
symbols.doc:
Capability identifies one process-supervision capability whose native backend
is present on some platforms and absent on others.

symbols.name: String
symbols.doc:
String returns the capability's stable name, or its integer form when the
value is out of range.

symbols.name: MissingCapabilities
symbols.doc:
MissingCapabilities returns the subset of caps with no native backend on the
current platform; an empty (nil) result means every capability is present.

symbols.name: MustSupport
symbols.doc:
MustSupport panics when any requested capability is missing on the current
platform, and is a no-op otherwise. It is the consumer's OPT-IN fail-fast: the
SDK never calls it. The panic value is the typed [errs] UnsupportedPlatform
error (code 0.2.6.1), so a top-level recover() can classify it via
errs.CodeOf / HasCode rather than a bare string.

symbols.name: Supported
symbols.doc:
Supported reports whether cap has a native backend on the current GOOS. It is
pure, allocation-free and race-clean: it consults runtime.GOOS only, never a
runtime delegation probe (see the package doc on cgroup.Available()).

symbols.name: UnsupportedPlatform

code.public: This operation is not supported on this platform

symbols.doc:
UnsupportedPlatform is the central sentinel a missing capability surfaces. A
recover() of a [MustSupport] panic yields an error carrying this error's code.

symbols.name: Available
symbols.doc:
Available reports whether a kernel-enforced control-group backend is usable: on
Linux, that the unified cgroup v2 hierarchy is mounted AND a sub-group can be
created under it by the caller; on Windows, that Job Objects are available
(always true); on FreeBSD, that the kernel carries RACCT. It returns false on
platforms with no backend (darwin, OpenBSD, NetBSD, DragonFly, illumos, Solaris), on cgroup v1,
and on a Linux host where the hierarchy is read-only.

symbols.name: Create
symbols.spelled: func(name string, opts ...Option) (g Group, err error)
symbols.doc:
Create makes a new control group named name and returns a Group bound to it —
a cgroup v2 sub-group under the delegated root on Linux, a Job Object on
Windows, a tracked rctl group on FreeBSD. It returns CgroupUnavailable when the
Linux hierarchy is absent or not delegated, CgroupCreateFailed when creation
fails, and UnsupportedPlatform on a platform with no control-group backend
(darwin, OpenBSD, NetBSD, DragonFly, illumos, Solaris).

symbols.name: Group
symbols.doc:
Group is a handle to a cgroup v2 control group: set controller ceilings,
attach processes, and remove the group. It aliases the core proc.Group port.

symbols.name: MustCreate
symbols.doc:
MustCreate is like [Create] but panics with the typed error when creation
fails — UnsupportedPlatform on a platform with no control-group backend
(darwin, OpenBSD, NetBSD, DragonFly, illumos, Solaris), or CgroupUnavailable when the Linux hierarchy is not
delegated. It is the idiomatic Go MustX opt-in (like
[regexp.MustCompile]) for a consumer that chooses crash-on-unsupported at its
own startup; the SDK itself never panics, and [Create] is the non-panicking
form for normal use. The panic value is the typed error, so a top-level
recover() can classify it via errs.CodeOf / HasCode.

symbols.name: Option
symbols.doc:
Option customises a Create call (functional-option pattern). It aliases the
service Option type; construct options with WithRoot.

symbols.name: WithRoot
symbols.doc:
WithRoot overrides the parent directory under which Create makes the new
control group, targeting a delegated sub-tree instead of the top-level mount.
It is a cgroup v2 path: on Windows and FreeBSD, whose backends have no
hierarchy, it is accepted and ignored.

symbols.name: CodeClosed
symbols.doc:
The codes, for errs.HasCode: a caller must tell "another daemon runs"
(IN_USE: talk to it) from "the directory or the path to it is not private"
(fix the deployment, or look for whoever planted a component) from "nobody
answers" (start one).

symbols.name: CodeDialFailed
symbols.doc:
The codes, for errs.HasCode: a caller must tell "another daemon runs"
(IN_USE: talk to it) from "the directory or the path to it is not private"
(fix the deployment, or look for whoever planted a component) from "nobody
answers" (start one).

symbols.name: CodeDirectoryUnsafe
symbols.doc:
The codes, for errs.HasCode: a caller must tell "another daemon runs"
(IN_USE: talk to it) from "the directory or the path to it is not private"
(fix the deployment, or look for whoever planted a component) from "nobody
answers" (start one).

symbols.name: CodeEndpointForeign
symbols.doc:
The codes, for errs.HasCode: a caller must tell "another daemon runs"
(IN_USE: talk to it) from "the directory or the path to it is not private"
(fix the deployment, or look for whoever planted a component) from "nobody
answers" (start one).

symbols.name: CodeInUse
symbols.doc:
The codes, for errs.HasCode: a caller must tell "another daemon runs"
(IN_USE: talk to it) from "the directory or the path to it is not private"
(fix the deployment, or look for whoever planted a component) from "nobody
answers" (start one).

symbols.name: CodeListenFailed
symbols.doc:
The codes, for errs.HasCode: a caller must tell "another daemon runs"
(IN_USE: talk to it) from "the directory or the path to it is not private"
(fix the deployment, or look for whoever planted a component) from "nobody
answers" (start one).

symbols.name: CodeMisconfigured
symbols.doc:
The codes, for errs.HasCode: a caller must tell "another daemon runs"
(IN_USE: talk to it) from "the directory or the path to it is not private"
(fix the deployment, or look for whoever planted a component) from "nobody
answers" (start one).

symbols.name: CodePathUnsafe
symbols.doc:
The codes, for errs.HasCode: a caller must tell "another daemon runs"
(IN_USE: talk to it) from "the directory or the path to it is not private"
(fix the deployment, or look for whoever planted a component) from "nobody
answers" (start one).

symbols.name: CodePeerRefused
symbols.doc:
The codes, for errs.HasCode: a caller must tell "another daemon runs"
(IN_USE: talk to it) from "the directory or the path to it is not private"
(fix the deployment, or look for whoever planted a component) from "nobody
answers" (start one).

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc:
Config is where a private socket lives and who, besides its own
account, may use it — the engine's configuration, shared by both ends.

symbols.name: Conn
symbols.doc: Conn is a connection with its peer's identity.

symbols.name: Dial
symbols.doc: Dial connects to the private socket at cfg.Path, within ctx and one second.

symbols.name: Dialer
symbols.doc:
Dialer is the connecting end of a private socket: it reaches the
listener its configuration names, and refuses one it cannot trust
before a byte is sent.

symbols.name: Listen
symbols.doc:
Listen opens the private socket at cfg.Path and returns the engine behind
the Listener port.

symbols.name: Listener
symbols.doc:
Listener is the accepting end of a private socket: it hands out the
connections of admitted peers only, and closes and counts the others.

symbols.name: NewDialer
symbols.doc:
NewDialer returns the engine behind the Dialer port for the private socket
at cfg.Path. The configuration is checked here, before anything is touched,
and copied: editing cfg's slices afterwards changes nothing.

symbols.name: Peer
symbols.doc: Peer is who is at the other end of a connection, as the kernel says.

symbols.name: RuntimeDir
symbols.doc:
RuntimeDir is where an application's private sockets belong on this
machine. It creates nothing.

symbols.name: Apply
symbols.doc:
Apply derives the Go soft memory limit from the tightest control-group cap
governing this process and installs it, returning what it read, what it
derived, and what decided the outcome.

It stands aside — leaving the runtime default in place — when GOMEMLIMIT is
already set, when no cgroup declares a cap, and when the derived limit is too
small to be useful. Those three are told apart by Limit.Source.

symbols.name: Limit
symbols.doc:
Limit is an immutable record of one derivation: the allowance read, the limit
derived, and the source that decided it. It aliases the core proc type.

symbols.name: MemorySourceBelowFloor
symbols.doc:
MemorySourceBelowFloor reports that a cap was found but the limit derived from
it fell under the usable floor and was discarded.

symbols.name: MemorySourceCgroup
symbols.doc:
MemorySourceCgroup reports the one outcome that yields a limit: a real cap was
read from the control-group hierarchy and the derived value was applied.

symbols.name: MemorySourceOperator
symbols.doc:
MemorySourceOperator reports that GOMEMLIMIT carried a non-empty value, which
the runtime has already applied. It re-exports the core enum value so consumers
qualify it as memlimit.MemorySourceOperator.

symbols.name: MemorySourceUnconstrained
symbols.doc:
MemorySourceUnconstrained reports that no control group governing this process
declares a memory cap.

symbols.name: Source
symbols.doc: Source names what decided the soft memory limit. It aliases the core proc type.

symbols.name: Build
symbols.doc:
Build describes what the running binary was built from, and reports false
when the binary carries no build information.

symbols.name: BuildInfo
symbols.doc:
BuildInfo is what the running binary was built from: the toolchain, the
main package, the main module with its version-control stamp, and every
dependency followed through its replacement. It is an alias of the service
value.

symbols.name: Distribution
symbols.doc:
Distribution is one of the Go runtime's cumulative histograms, read as
durations: Count, and Quantile(q) as the upper bound of the bucket that
reaches q. It is an alias of the service value.

symbols.name: ExitResult
symbols.doc:
ExitResult is the outcome of a finished process — exit code, terminating
signal, and resource usage. It is an alias of the core port's ExitValue.

symbols.name: Limit
symbols.doc:
Limit is a soft/hard resource-limit pair for setrlimit(2). It is an alias of
the core port's LimitValue.

symbols.name: Module
symbols.doc:
Module is one module of the running binary, with its release, its commit
and its local directory told apart. It is an alias of the service value.

symbols.name: MustStart
symbols.doc:
MustStart is like [Start] but panics with the typed error when the spawn fails
— UnsupportedPlatform off Unix/Windows, InvalidSpec, RlimitFailed, … It is the
idiomatic Go MustX opt-in (like [regexp.MustCompile]) for a consumer that
chooses crash-on-failure at its own startup; the SDK itself never panics, and
[Start] is the non-panicking form for normal use. The panic value is the typed
error, so a top-level recover() can classify it via errs.CodeOf / HasCode.

symbols.name: ParseBuild
symbols.doc:
ParseBuild describes a BuildInfo from elsewhere — one a test builds by
hand, or debug.ParseBuildInfo's reading of another binary — exactly as
Build describes the running one.

symbols.name: Process
symbols.doc:
Process is the handle to a spawned process: PID, Wait, Signal, SignalGroup,
and a group-aware Stop. It is an alias of the core port interface.

symbols.name: Resource
symbols.doc:
Resource identifies a per-process resource governed by setrlimit(2). It is an
alias of the core port type.

symbols.name: ResourceAS
symbols.doc: ResourceAS limits the process virtual address-space size (RLIMIT_AS).

symbols.name: ResourceCPU
symbols.doc: ResourceCPU limits CPU time in seconds (RLIMIT_CPU).

symbols.name: ResourceCore
symbols.doc: ResourceCore limits the size of a core dump in bytes (RLIMIT_CORE).

symbols.name: ResourceNoFile
symbols.doc: ResourceNoFile limits the highest open file descriptor (RLIMIT_NOFILE).

symbols.name: SIGHUP
symbols.doc: SIGHUP is the hang-up / reload signal many daemons treat as "reconfigure".

symbols.name: SIGINT
symbols.doc: SIGINT is the interrupt signal (Ctrl-C analogue).

symbols.name: SIGKILL
symbols.doc: SIGKILL is the unignorable kill Stop escalates to after the grace window.

symbols.name: SIGQUIT
symbols.doc: SIGQUIT is the quit-with-core signal.

symbols.name: SIGTERM
symbols.doc: SIGTERM is the polite termination request — the default Stop signal.

symbols.name: Self
symbols.doc:
Self takes a snapshot of the running process. It never fails: a figure the
platform cannot give is zero, and Stats.CPUEstimated says when CPUTime is
the runtime's estimate rather than the kernel's count.

symbols.name: Signal
symbols.doc:
Signal is a typed, platform-portable OS signal. It is an alias of the core
port type, so process.SIGTERM and a signal parsed elsewhere compare equal.

symbols.name: Spec
symbols.doc:
Spec is the immutable description of a process to spawn — executable,
environment, credentials, isolation topology, and scheduling attributes. It is
an alias of the core port type.

symbols.name: Start
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, spec Spec) (proc Process, err error)
symbols.doc:
Start spawns the process described by spec and returns a live Process handle.
It delegates to internal/service/proc/exec; ctx is honoured up to the
fork/exec boundary. A bare Spec.Path is searched in the child's PATH (see
the package documentation). On Windows the Unix-only Spec fields are refused
with UnsupportedPlatform; on platforms that are neither Unix nor Windows,
Start itself returns UnsupportedPlatform.

symbols.name: Stats
symbols.doc:
Stats is the running process at one instant: identity, scheduler settings,
goroutines, heap, collections with their pause distribution, scheduling
latency, and CPU time. Every count is cumulative since the process started.
It is an alias of the service value.

symbols.name: StdioCapture
symbols.doc:
StdioCapture connects the child to Spec.Stdout/Stderr (io.Writer) and
Spec.Stdin (io.Reader); a nil stream falls back to the null device for that
one stream. The systemd analogue is StandardOutput=/StandardError=/StandardInput=.

symbols.name: StdioInherit
symbols.doc:
StdioInherit shares the parent's stdin/stdout/stderr with the child — the
default and the only behaviour before per-process wiring existed.

symbols.name: StdioMode
symbols.doc:
StdioMode selects how a spawned child's standard streams (stdin, stdout,
stderr) are wired. It is an alias of the core port type; set it on Spec.Stdio.
The zero value is StdioInherit.

symbols.name: StdioNull
symbols.doc:
StdioNull connects every stream to the null device: output is discarded and
the child's stdin returns EOF immediately.

symbols.name: IsPID1
symbols.doc:
IsPID1 reports whether the current process is the init process (pid 1). It is
false on platforms where the convention does not apply.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc:
New returns a [Reaper] configured by opts. On Unix it is a SIGCHLD-driven
waitpid loop; elsewhere it is a no-op. The reaper starts idle — call Start.

symbols.name: Option
symbols.doc:
Option configures a [Reaper] returned by [New]. It is an alias of the service
option type so callers compose options without importing internal packages.

symbols.name: ReapFailed

code.public: Could not reap child processes

symbols.doc:
ReapFailed is returned by a sweep when wait4 fails with an error other
than the benign ECHILD ("no children") condition.

symbols.name: Reaper
symbols.doc:
Reaper collects terminated child processes so they do not linger as zombies —
the core duty of any PID1 or subreaper. It is an alias of the core port; the
concrete value is platform-selected by [New].

symbols.name: SetChildSubreaper
symbols.doc:
SetChildSubreaper marks the calling process as a child subreaper so orphaned
descendants reparent to it rather than to PID1. It returns [SubreaperFailed]
on a prctl error and [UnsupportedPlatform] off Unix.

symbols.name: SubreaperFailed

code.public: Could not enable child-subreaper mode

symbols.doc:
SubreaperFailed is returned by [SetChildSubreaper] when
prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER) fails to arm subreaper mode.

symbols.name: UnsupportedPlatform

code.public: This operation is not supported on this platform

symbols.doc:
UnsupportedPlatform is returned by [SetChildSubreaper] on platforms
without a prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER) equivalent (e.g. Windows).

symbols.name: WithOnReap
symbols.doc:
WithOnReap registers fn as a post-sweep observer receiving the number of
children reaped in each sweep (including zero). fn must not block. On illumos
and Solaris the loop also sweeps once a second, so there an idle reaper calls
fn with zero once a second.

symbols.name: Apply
symbols.doc:
Apply sets the soft/hard ceilings in limits on the process identified by pid.
A pid of 0 targets the calling process; any other pid targets that process via
prlimit64(2) and needs CAP_SYS_RESOURCE. It returns UnknownResource for an
unmapped resource, RlimitFailed on a syscall failure, and UnsupportedPlatform
off Linux.

symbols.name: Limit
symbols.doc:
Limit is an immutable soft/hard setrlimit(2) pair. It aliases the core proc
LimitValue type.

symbols.name: LimitInfinity
symbols.doc: LimitInfinity is the soft/hard value meaning "no limit" (RLIM_INFINITY).

symbols.name: PrepareSysProcAttr
symbols.doc:
PrepareSysProcAttr validates limits without issuing any syscall and reports
whether they can be applied on this platform, returning the same typed errors
Apply would (UnknownResource / UnsupportedPlatform). Use it to fail fast at
Spec-construction time; Go's SysProcAttr has no rlimit field, so the actual
application happens post-fork via Apply.

symbols.name: Resource
symbols.doc:
Resource is the abstract, platform-portable resource enum mapped to a
RLIMIT_* constant by the service layer. It aliases the core proc type.

symbols.name: ResourceAS
symbols.doc: ResourceAS limits the process virtual address-space size (RLIMIT_AS).

symbols.name: ResourceCPU
symbols.doc: ResourceCPU limits CPU time in seconds (RLIMIT_CPU).

symbols.name: ResourceCore
symbols.doc: ResourceCore limits the core-dump size in bytes (RLIMIT_CORE).

symbols.name: ResourceData
symbols.doc: ResourceData limits the process data-segment size (RLIMIT_DATA).

symbols.name: ResourceFSize
symbols.doc: ResourceFSize limits the largest file the process may create (RLIMIT_FSIZE).

symbols.name: ResourceMemLock
symbols.doc: ResourceMemLock limits bytes that may be locked into RAM (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK).

symbols.name: ResourceNProc
symbols.doc: ResourceNProc limits the number of processes for the real uid (RLIMIT_NPROC).

symbols.name: ResourceNoFile
symbols.doc:
ResourceNoFile limits the highest open file descriptor (RLIMIT_NOFILE). It
re-exports the core enum value so consumers qualify it as rlimit.ResourceNoFile.

symbols.name: ResourceStack
symbols.doc: ResourceStack limits the process stack size (RLIMIT_STACK).

symbols.name: Notify
symbols.doc:
Notify subscribes to sigs and returns a receive-only channel of typed Signals
plus an idempotent, leak-free stop function. Each delivery is translated to a
typed Signal; the channel is buffered so a burst is not dropped, and stop
detaches the subscription and closes the channel.

symbols.name: Parse
symbols.doc:
Parse resolves a signal from its name or number — the canonical "SIGTERM", the
bare "TERM", or the numeric "15", all case-insensitive — returning a typed
UNKNOWN_SIGNAL error for anything the platform table does not define.

symbols.name: Relay
symbols.doc:
Relay reads signals from src and forwards each to target until src closes —
via kill(2) on Unix, via TerminateProcess or a console control event on
Windows. A positive target is a pid; a target below -1 addresses the process
group whose id is -target. It returns nil on a clean drain and a typed
RELAY_FAILED error on the first delivery failure (UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM on a
platform that is neither Unix nor Windows).

symbols.name: Signal
symbols.doc:
Signal is a typed, platform-portable OS signal. It aliases the domain type, so
a value parsed here interoperates with the rest of the SDK process domain.

symbols.name: Target
symbols.doc:
Target names the recipient of a relayed signal: a positive value is a pid; a
value below -1 addresses the process group whose id is its absolute value.

symbols.name: Files
symbols.doc:
Files returns the inherited listening sockets (fd 3..3+LISTEN_FDS) as *os.File,
honouring LISTEN_PID. When unsetEnv is true the activation environment is
cleared so a grandchild does not re-inherit it. An empty or foreign activation
set yields nil with no error; off Unix it returns UnsupportedPlatform.

symbols.name: Listeners
symbols.doc:
Listeners returns the inherited stream sockets wrapped as net.Listener (the
underlying *os.File is closed after the dup). Same gating and platform
behaviour as Files.

symbols.name: Prepare
symbols.doc:
Prepare (activator side) appends each named listener's socket to child as an
inherited fd and sets LISTEN_FDS / LISTEN_FDNAMES in child.Env so the spawned
process recovers them via Files/Listeners. Off Unix it returns
UnsupportedPlatform.

symbols.name: Spec
symbols.doc:
Spec is the process spawn specification an activator augments via Prepare. It
aliases the core port type, so the same value drives process.Start.

symbols.name: WithNames
symbols.doc:
WithNames returns the inherited sockets grouped by their LISTEN_FDNAMES name;
duplicate names group several fds under one key.

symbols.name: Listen
symbols.spelled: func() (l Listener, socketPath string, err error)
symbols.doc:
Listen creates a supervisor-side sd_notify socket and returns the Listener plus
the socketPath a child should be given via NOTIFY_SOCKET. On non-Linux
platforms it returns the UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM error.

symbols.name: Listener
symbols.doc:
Listener is the supervisor side of the protocol: it owns the datagram socket a
supervised child writes readiness to and yields one parsed, credential-verified
Notification per Recv.

symbols.name: MainPID
symbols.doc: MainPID advertises the main process PID to the supervisor (MAINPID=pid).

symbols.name: Notification
symbols.doc:
Notification is a parsed sd_notify datagram: the raw State field set plus the
typed Status, MainPID, and kernel-verified SenderPID, with Ready/Reloading/
Stopping/Watchdog lifecycle accessors.

symbols.name: Notify
symbols.doc:
Notify sends an sd_notify datagram carrying the given NAME=value state to
$NOTIFY_SOCKET, or is a no-op returning nil when $NOTIFY_SOCKET is unset.

symbols.name: Ready
symbols.doc: Ready notifies the supervisor that startup is complete (READY=1).

symbols.name: Reloading
symbols.doc:
Reloading notifies the supervisor that a configuration reload has begun
(RELOADING=1).

symbols.name: Status
symbols.doc: Status publishes a single-line free-text status (STATUS=msg).

symbols.name: Stopping
symbols.doc: Stopping notifies the supervisor that shutdown has begun (STOPPING=1).

symbols.name: Watchdog
symbols.doc: Watchdog sends a watchdog keep-alive ping (WATCHDOG=1).

symbols.name: WatchdogInterval
symbols.doc:
WatchdogInterval reports the watchdog ping interval the supervisor configured
via $WATCHDOG_USEC; ok is false when the variable is unset or malformed.

symbols.name: Abstain
symbols.doc:
Abstain means a policy has no opinion about this request. It is the
ZERO Decision, it grants nothing, and [Check] refuses it.

symbols.name: AllOf
symbols.doc:
AllOf holds when every condition holds. Every branch is evaluated, so the
answer is order-independent and a failure anywhere is reported.

symbols.name: Allow
symbols.doc:
Allow means a policy permits the request. It is the only granting state,
and any [Deny] in the composition still outranks it.

symbols.name: AnyOf
symbols.doc:
AnyOf holds when at least one condition holds — but an unevaluable branch is
still absorbing, so a request cannot satisfy the rule by omitting the
attribute one of its branches names.

symbols.name: Attr
symbols.doc: Attr is the public alias for one typed, named fact attached to a [Request].

symbols.name: AttrAtLeast
symbols.spelled: func(key string, lo int64) (condition Condition, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(key string, lo int64) (condition github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/security/authz.Condition, err error)
symbols.doc: AttrAtLeast holds when the request carries key as a number at least lo.

symbols.name: AttrBool
symbols.doc:
AttrBool builds a flag attribute. Present-and-false is a different fact from
absent, and this is how the first one is stated.

symbols.name: AttrContains
symbols.spelled: func(key string, want string) (condition Condition, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(key string, want string) (condition github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/security/authz.Condition, err error)
symbols.doc: AttrContains holds when the request carries key as a set containing want.

symbols.name: AttrEquals
symbols.spelled: func(key string, want string) (condition Condition, err error)
symbols.canonical: func(key string, want string) (condition github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/security/authz.Condition, err error)
symbols.doc:
AttrEquals holds when the request carries key as text equal to want, and
FAILS when the attribute is absent or is not text.

symbols.name: AttrInt64
symbols.doc: AttrInt64 builds a whole-number attribute. Times travel as Unix seconds.

symbols.name: AttrIsTrue
symbols.doc:
AttrIsTrue holds when the request carries key as a flag that is set. Present
and false does not hold; absent fails.

symbols.name: AttrKind
symbols.doc:
AttrKind is the public alias for the type an [Attr] carries. The kind is
part of the attribute's identity: a text rule against a number MISMATCHES,
it does not compare false.

symbols.name: AttrMatchesSubject
symbols.doc:
AttrMatchesSubject holds when the request carries key as text equal to the
subject — the ownership rule. An anonymous request owns nothing, so an empty
subject never matches, not even an empty owner.

symbols.name: AttrString
symbols.doc: AttrString builds a text attribute.

symbols.name: AttrStrings
symbols.doc:
AttrStrings builds a set attribute — roles, groups, scopes. Passing no
values states that the subject holds none, which is NOT the same as omitting
the attribute: the first abstains, the second refuses.

symbols.name: AttributeKindMismatch

code.public: Access to the requested resource is denied

symbols.doc:
AttributeKindMismatch is reported by a condition whose attribute is
present under another kind.

symbols.name: AttributeMissing

code.public: Access to the requested resource is denied

symbols.doc:
AttributeMissing is reported by a condition whose rule named an
attribute the request does not carry.

symbols.name: Check
symbols.spelled: func(ctx context.Context, policy Policy, request Request) error
symbols.doc:
Check evaluates policy and reports the verdict as an error: nil when
permitted, [PermissionDenied] otherwise. It is the closure — the one place
where "nobody said Allow" becomes a refusal — and a nil policy refuses.

symbols.name: CodeAttributeKindMismatch
symbols.doc:
CodeAttributeKindMismatch identifies an attribute present under another
kind than the rule compares.

symbols.name: CodeAttributeMissing
symbols.doc:
CodeAttributeMissing identifies a rule that named an attribute the
request does not carry. It is a failure, never a false comparison.

symbols.name: CodeConditionInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeConditionInvalid identifies a condition constructor refused at
construction.

symbols.name: CodeGrantInvalid
symbols.doc: CodeGrantInvalid identifies an RBAC grant table refused at construction.

symbols.name: CodePermissionDenied
symbols.doc:
CodePermissionDenied identifies every refusal this domain produces —
explicit, by abstention, or by an evaluation that could not complete.

symbols.name: CodePolicyMisconfigured
symbols.doc:
CodePolicyMisconfigured identifies a nil policy in a composition, or one
that returned a decision outside allow/deny/abstain.

symbols.name: CodeRuleInvalid
symbols.doc: CodeRuleInvalid identifies an ABAC rule set refused at construction.

symbols.name: Condition
symbols.doc:
Condition is the public alias for an attribute predicate. Returning an error
means "could not be evaluated", which is absorbing everywhere.

symbols.name: ConditionInvalid

code.public: The condition cannot be built from the given arguments

symbols.doc:
ConditionInvalid is returned by a condition constructor for arguments it
cannot honour.

symbols.name: Decision
symbols.doc:
Decision is the public alias for the three-valued verdict: [Allow], [Deny]
or [Abstain]. Its zero value is [Abstain].

symbols.name: Deny
symbols.doc: Deny means a policy refuses the request. It is absorbing.

symbols.name: DenyOverrides
symbols.doc:
DenyOverrides composes policies: a [Deny] from any member wins, an [Allow]
requires at least one grant and no refusal, and everything else abstains.
Every member is evaluated — only a refusal short-circuits — so the result
does not depend on the order the policies were listed in.

symbols.name: Grant
symbols.doc: Grant is the public alias for one role and the permissions it confers.

symbols.name: GrantInvalid

code.public: The role grant table is not usable and was refused

symbols.doc: GrantInvalid is returned by [NewRBAC] for a grant table it cannot honour.

symbols.name: KindBool
symbols.doc: KindBool is a flag, which can be present and false.

symbols.name: KindInt64
symbols.doc: KindInt64 is a whole number — including a Unix timestamp.

symbols.name: KindInvalid
symbols.doc:
KindInvalid is the zero AttrKind. [NewRequest] drops an attribute
carrying it, so such an attribute is absent rather than unusable.

symbols.name: KindString
symbols.doc: KindString is a single text value.

symbols.name: KindStrings
symbols.doc: KindStrings is an unordered set of text values — roles, groups, scopes.

symbols.name: Must
symbols.doc:
Must unwraps a policy constructor for a package-level var, panicking on
error. Use it on wiring written in code, never on data read at run time.

symbols.name: MustCondition
symbols.doc:
MustCondition unwraps a condition constructor for a package-level var,
panicking on error. Same contract as [Must].

symbols.name: NewABAC
symbols.doc:
NewABAC builds an attribute-based policy over a fixed rule set, folded by
the same deny-overrides algorithm the policy set is.

symbols.name: NewRBAC
symbols.doc:
NewRBAC builds a role-based policy over a fixed grant table. It answers
[Allow] or [Abstain] and never [Deny] for an ungranted request — see the
package docs for why that is what makes it composable.

symbols.name: NewRequest
symbols.spelled: func(subject string, action string, resource string, attrs ...Attr) Request
symbols.canonical: func(subject string, action string, resource string, attrs ...github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/security/authz.Attr) github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/security/authz.Request
symbols.doc:
NewRequest builds the immutable question. Attributes are indexed by key,
last one wins, and one with an empty key or the zero kind is dropped — so
every attribute a rule can find is one it can use.

symbols.name: Not
symbols.doc:
Not inverts a condition's answer and PROPAGATES its failure unchanged. An
attribute the request does not carry therefore stays unevaluable instead of
becoming "true", which is the single sharpest form of the absent-attribute
trap.

symbols.name: Permission
symbols.doc:
Permission is the public alias for one (action, resource) pair a role
confers. Resource is the KIND of thing; instance facts belong in attributes.

symbols.name: PermissionDenied

code.public: Access to the requested resource is denied

symbols.doc:
PermissionDenied is the one refusal. Every non-granting outcome converts
to it, with the same code, status and sentence.

symbols.name: Policy
symbols.doc:
Policy is the public alias for the authorization port. It is a func type, so
it can never grow a method and break a downstream implementer (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: PolicyMisconfigured

code.public: Access to the requested resource is denied

symbols.doc:
PolicyMisconfigured is reported for a nil policy in a composition, or a
decision outside allow/deny/abstain.

symbols.name: RBACConfig
symbols.doc: RBACConfig is the public alias for [NewRBAC]'s parameters.

symbols.name: Request
symbols.doc: Request is the public alias for the immutable question a policy answers.

symbols.name: Rule
symbols.doc:
Rule is the public alias for one attribute rule: what it is about, what it
decides, and when it fires.

symbols.name: RuleInvalid

code.public: The attribute rule set is not usable and was refused

symbols.doc: RuleInvalid is returned by [NewABAC] for a rule set it cannot honour.

symbols.name: CodeDocumentInvalid
symbols.doc: CodeDocumentInvalid identifies a document that is not one JSON value.

symbols.name: CodeValueUnencodable
symbols.doc: CodeValueUnencodable identifies a value encoding/json refuses to encode.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc:
Config says what a Redactor treats as secret: the name Words, the struct
Tag, an extra Field rule, and how an Error in a log attribute is shown. Its
zero value is usable.

symbols.name: DefaultWords
symbols.doc:
DefaultWords returns the name fragments a Redactor treats as secret when its
Config gives none, as a fresh slice a caller may extend.

symbols.name: Document
symbols.doc:
Document is a JSON document with its secrets replaced — never longer than
its bound, always well-formed — and whether it had to be cut.

symbols.name: DocumentInvalid

code.public: The document is not valid JSON and was not redacted

symbols.doc: DocumentInvalid refuses a document that is not one JSON value.

symbols.name: Ellipsis
symbols.doc: Ellipsis ends whatever was cut to fit a bound, and is counted in it.

symbols.name: MinBytes
symbols.doc: MinBytes is the smallest bound honoured; a smaller one is raised to it.

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc: New returns a Redactor applying cfg.

symbols.name: Placeholder
symbols.doc: Placeholder replaces every secret.

symbols.name: Redactor
symbols.doc:
Redactor is the redaction port: Name, Text, JSON, Value and Attrs. [New]
returns the SDK's implementation, which caches what it learns about each Go
type, so build one per configuration and keep it; it is safe for concurrent
use. The port is frozen at those five methods (ADR 0039), so a consumer can
accept a Redactor and hand a test double in its place.

symbols.name: Unencodable
symbols.doc: Unencodable is the text a log attribute encoding/json refuses is shown as.

symbols.name: ValueUnencodable

code.public: The value cannot be encoded as JSON and was not redacted

symbols.doc: ValueUnencodable refuses a value encoding/json will not encode.

symbols.name: EmptyValue

code.public: An empty secret cannot be stored

symbols.doc: EmptyValue is returned by a Put of an empty secret.

symbols.name: EnvConfig
symbols.doc: EnvConfig parameterises [NewEnv].

symbols.name: EnvRefused

code.public: The environment does not supply a usable value for that secret

symbols.doc:
EnvRefused is returned when the environment names a secret without a
usable value: both forms set, or an empty or oversized file.

symbols.name: FileConfig
symbols.doc: FileConfig parameterises [NewFile].

symbols.name: FromString
symbols.doc: FromString returns a Value holding text.

symbols.name: GenerateFailed

code.public: A new secret could not be generated

symbols.doc: GenerateFailed is returned when a rotation's generator failed.

symbols.name: InvalidConfig

code.public: The secret store configuration is not usable

symbols.doc:
InvalidConfig is returned by a constructor given a configuration it
cannot honour.

symbols.name: InvalidKeep

code.public: A prune must keep at least one version

symbols.doc: InvalidKeep is returned by a Prune asked to keep fewer than one version.

symbols.name: InvalidName

code.public: That is not a valid secret name

symbols.doc: InvalidName is returned for a name outside the grammar.

symbols.name: InvalidSubject

code.public: That is not a valid subject reference

symbols.doc:
InvalidSubject is returned for a subject outside the grammar; the
rejected string is never repeated.

symbols.name: KeyDestroyed

code.public: That value was erased

symbols.doc:
KeyDestroyed is returned by SubjectKeys.Open for a box whose data key is
not held: the value was erased.

symbols.name: KeyFile
symbols.doc:
KeyFile returns the crypto.Key held in the file at path — exactly
crypto.KeyLen raw bytes — creating the file with a fresh random key on first
use: 0600, its directory 0700 when it has to be made, published atomically so
that concurrent first uses all return the same key.

It refuses content that is not exactly one key with [KeyFileInvalid], an
existing file other accounts can read with [InvalidConfig], and — where the
file store refuses, every platform outside the Unix family, because a mode
is not an access list there — proc.UnsupportedPlatform. No error carries the
key or a refused file's content.

symbols.name: KeyFileInvalid

code.public: The key file does not hold a key

symbols.doc:
KeyFileInvalid is returned by KeyFile for a file that exists and does not
hold exactly one key of raw bytes.

symbols.name: KeyMaterialInvalid

code.public: That secret cannot be used as a key

symbols.doc:
KeyMaterialInvalid is returned when a keyring version is not exactly 32
bytes.

symbols.name: Keyring
symbols.doc:
Keyring sees the versions of one secret as keys: the newest seals and signs,
every kept version opens and verifies.

symbols.name: MaxNameLen
symbols.doc: MaxNameLen is the longest secret name, in bytes.

symbols.name: MaxSubjectLen
symbols.doc: MaxSubjectLen is the longest subject reference, in bytes.

symbols.name: MemoryConfig
symbols.doc: MemoryConfig parameterises [NewMemory].

symbols.name: New
symbols.doc: New returns a Value holding a copy of raw.

symbols.name: NewEnv
symbols.doc:
NewEnv returns a read-only Store over the process environment, honouring the
NAME_FILE convention. It refuses a prefix no shell could export.

symbols.name: NewFile
symbols.doc:
NewFile returns a Store that keeps its versions in a directory it owns,
sealed at rest when cfg.Key is set. It refuses a directory other accounts
can read, and returns proc.UnsupportedPlatform where atomic publication or
the file lock is unavailable. The store also implements io.Closer.

symbols.name: NewKeyring
symbols.spelled: func(store Store, name string) (keyring *Keyring, err error)
symbols.doc: NewKeyring returns the keyring over the versions of name in store.

symbols.name: NewMemory
symbols.doc: NewMemory returns a Store that keeps its versions in this process's memory.

symbols.name: NewMemorySubjectKeyStore
symbols.doc:
NewMemorySubjectKeyStore returns a [SubjectKeyStore] that keeps the wrapped
keys in this process's memory — for tests and development, where the data
they protect dies with the process too.

symbols.name: NewRotator
symbols.doc: NewRotator returns a rotator for cfg.Name in cfg.Store. It starts nothing.

symbols.name: NewSubjectKeys
symbols.doc:
NewSubjectKeys returns the engine that keeps one data key per subject under
cfg.Root, filed in cfg.Store. It refuses a nil root or store, a negative
cache, and a cache without a TTL — the TTL bounds how long a key another
process destroyed keeps opening here — with [InvalidConfig].

symbols.name: NotFound

code.public: No secret has that name

symbols.doc: NotFound is returned for a name that holds no version.

symbols.name: Policy
symbols.doc:
Policy says how often a secret rotates, how many versions a rotation keeps,
and how a new one is made.

symbols.name: Random
symbols.doc:
Random returns a generator of n bytes from crypto/rand; a keyring's versions
need n = 32. Below 16 bytes the generator refuses every call.

symbols.name: ReadOnly

code.public: This secret store cannot be written

symbols.doc: ReadOnly is returned by a write to a store that only reads.

symbols.name: RecordUnreadable

code.public: A stored secret could not be read back

symbols.doc:
RecordUnreadable is returned by the file store for a record it found
and could not read back — most often, one written under another key.

symbols.name: Redacted
symbols.doc: Redacted is the placeholder every rendering of a [Value] writes.

symbols.name: RewrapReport
symbols.doc: RewrapReport says what one [SubjectKeys].Rewrap pass did, key by key.

symbols.name: Rotator
symbols.doc: Rotator mints new versions of one secret according to a [Policy].

symbols.name: RotatorConfig
symbols.doc: RotatorConfig parameterises [NewRotator].

symbols.name: SealInvalid

code.public: That sealed value could not be opened

symbols.doc: SealInvalid is returned by Keyring.Open for every box it cannot open.

symbols.name: SignatureInvalid

code.public: That signature is not valid

symbols.doc:
SignatureInvalid is returned by Keyring.Verify for every signature it
cannot verify.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.doc:
Store keeps named secrets as numbered versions. It is frozen at five
methods; a new capability arrives as a sibling interface.

symbols.name: StoreUnavailable

code.public: The secret store is unavailable

symbols.doc:
StoreUnavailable is returned when the backend could not be read or
written; a retry is meaningful.

symbols.name: SubjectKeyStore
symbols.doc:
SubjectKeyStore keeps one wrapped data key per subject. The caller
implements it over its own storage — Insert and Replace atomic across every
process — or uses [NewMemorySubjectKeyStore]. It is frozen at five methods;
a new capability arrives as a sibling interface.

symbols.name: SubjectKeyUnreadable

code.public: A data key could not be unwrapped

symbols.doc:
SubjectKeyUnreadable is returned when a subject's data key is held and
does not unwrap under the root: a fault, never an erasure.

symbols.name: SubjectKeys
symbols.doc:
SubjectKeys keeps one data key per subject, wrapped by a root [Keyring]:
Seal and Open under a subject's key, Destroy to erase everything it sealed,
Rewrap after the root rotates.

symbols.name: SubjectKeysConfig
symbols.doc: SubjectKeysConfig parameterises [NewSubjectKeys].

symbols.name: SubjectOf
symbols.doc:
SubjectOf returns the subject a box sealed by [SubjectKeys].Seal names,
without opening it, or [SealInvalid] for anything that is not such a box.

symbols.name: ValidateName
symbols.doc:
ValidateName reports whether name is a secret name, returning [InvalidName]
when it is not. Every store calls it; a caller may too, to refuse a name at
the edge of its own input.

symbols.name: ValidateSubject
symbols.doc:
ValidateSubject reports whether subject is a subject reference, returning
[InvalidSubject] when it is not: 1 to [MaxSubjectLen] bytes of a-z, 0-9,
'-', '_', '.' and ':', starting with a letter or a digit. A subject is kept
in clear, so it is a reference derived from an identity, never the identity.

symbols.name: Value
symbols.doc:
Value is an immutable secret that renders as [Redacted] in every rendering;
only Reveal and RevealString hand its bytes back.

symbols.name: ValueRefused

code.public: A secret can only be decoded from a string, and never from its own placeholder

symbols.doc:
ValueRefused is returned by a decode given anything but a string, or
the placeholder itself.

symbols.name: Versioned
symbols.doc:
Versioned is one version of one secret: name, number, value, and when the
store recorded it.

symbols.name: WrappedKey
symbols.doc:
WrappedKey is one subject's wrapped data key, as a [SubjectKeyStore] keeps
it.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.doc: Config is the public alias for the memory store's construction parameters.

symbols.name: DirectoryUnsafe

code.public: The session store location is not private enough to use

symbols.doc:
DirectoryUnsafe is returned when the store location is readable beyond
its owner, or when the filesystem accepted a 0600 request without
enforcing it.

symbols.name: EntropyFailed

code.public: The session store could not generate a secure identifier

symbols.doc: EntropyFailed is returned when the random source could not be read.

symbols.name: Expired

code.public: That session has expired

symbols.doc:
Expired is returned when the record existed and its deadline had passed.
The record is dropped as this is reported, so the next call says NotFound.

symbols.name: FileConfig
symbols.doc:
FileConfig is the public alias for the file store's construction parameters.
Its Key field takes a pkg/v1/crypto.Key, and its Clock is a clock.Timed
because the store both stamps time and waits on it — the poll between lock
attempts is armed on it, so a test drives contention without sleeping.

symbols.name: FixationRefused

code.public: A session's subject cannot be changed without a new identifier

symbols.doc:
FixationRefused is returned by Save when the value's subject differs from
the stored record's. Regenerate is the operation that was wanted.

symbols.name: ID
symbols.doc: ID is the public alias for the opaque, redacting session identifier.

symbols.name: IDLen
symbols.doc: IDLen is the identifier length in bytes — 256 bits from crypto/rand.

symbols.name: IdentifierCollision

code.public: The session store could not mint a unique identifier

symbols.doc:
IdentifierCollision is returned when a freshly minted identifier already
names a live session, which at 256 bits means the random source is broken.

symbols.name: InvalidConfig

code.public: The session store configuration is not usable

symbols.doc:
InvalidConfig is returned by every constructor for a configuration it
cannot honour — a non-positive timeout, an idle window the ceiling makes
unreachable, a missing directory or key.

symbols.name: InvalidID

code.public: That is not a valid session identifier

symbols.doc: InvalidID is returned for a malformed or zero identifier.

symbols.name: InvalidPurpose

code.public: A sealer needs a non-empty purpose

symbols.doc: InvalidPurpose is returned by NewSealer for an empty purpose.

symbols.name: LockFailed

code.public: The session store is busy

symbols.doc:
LockFailed is returned when the store-wide exclusive lock could not be
taken; the operation is refused rather than run unserialised.

symbols.name: NewFileStore
symbols.doc:
NewFileStore returns a Store keeping one sealed file per session in cfg.Dir.
It refuses — at construction — an unusable configuration, an unsafe
directory, a location reached through a link anybody could have planted
([PathRedirected]), and a platform without flock(2), enforced Unix
permissions and a directory flush.

symbols.name: NewID
symbols.doc:
NewID builds an ID from exactly [IDLen] raw bytes. Most callers want
[ParseID]; this is for a Store implementation that holds raw identifier
bytes.

symbols.name: NewMemoryStore
symbols.doc:
NewMemoryStore returns a Store keeping every session in this process's
memory. It refuses a Config it cannot honour and never returns an inert
store.

symbols.name: NewSealer
symbols.spelled: func(key corecrypto.Key, purpose string) (sealer Sealer, err error)
symbols.doc:
NewSealer returns a Sealer binding key and purpose. purpose is required: it
is the domain separator between two things sealed under one key, and an empty
one is refused rather than read as "no separation needed".

symbols.name: NewSession
symbols.doc:
NewSession builds an immutable [Session] from a [State]. It is what a
framework implementing its own [Store] returns; ordinary callers get sessions
from a store and never call this.

symbols.name: NotFound

code.public: No session matches that identifier

symbols.doc: NotFound is returned for an identifier that names no live session.

symbols.name: ParseID
symbols.doc:
ParseID decodes the canonical form produced by [ID].Reveal — unpadded
base64url over exactly [IDLen] bytes. It is the inbound path: whatever
arrives from a cookie reaches the domain through here, and anything that is
not exactly that shape is refused before it can be used as a lookup key.

symbols.name: PathRedirected

code.public: The session store location is reached through a link

symbols.doc:
PathRedirected is returned by NewFileStore when the store's location is
reached through a link it refuses to follow: one at the lock file's
name, one at a component of FileConfig.Dir planted in a directory any
account can write, or a Dir that stopped naming the directory the store
had just opened. No retry helps; a human looks at the path.

symbols.name: PayloadTooLarge

code.public: That session holds more data than the store accepts

symbols.doc:
PayloadTooLarge is returned by Save for a payload above the store's caps,
and by Regenerate for a subject longer than 4096 bytes — refused before
anything is minted, so the old session is untouched.

symbols.name: RecordCorrupt

code.public: That session could not be read

symbols.doc:
RecordCorrupt is returned by the file store when a record could not be
read back — tampered, truncated, wrong key, or filed under another digest.

symbols.name: SealInvalid

code.public: That session value could not be opened

symbols.doc:
SealInvalid is returned by Sealer.Open for every failure, without
distinguishing them.

symbols.name: Sealer
symbols.doc:
Sealer is the public alias for the port that renders an [ID] as an opaque,
tamper-evident cookie VALUE. It does not write cookies.

symbols.name: Session
symbols.doc: Session is the public alias for the immutable session a Store hands back.

symbols.name: State
symbols.doc:
State is the public alias for the exported description [NewSession] builds a
[Session] from. It exists so a framework can implement [Store] over its own
backend; it is not a way around the fixation rule, since [Store].Save refuses
a subject the stored record does not have.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.doc:
Store is the public alias for the session-lifetime port. Its method set is
frozen: new capabilities arrive as sibling interfaces (ADR 0039).

symbols.name: StoreUnavailable

code.public: The session store is unavailable

symbols.doc: StoreUnavailable is returned when the backend itself failed. Retryable.

symbols.name: Sweeper
symbols.doc:
Sweeper is the public alias for the first such sibling — a store that can
drop its expired records on demand.

symbols.name: UnsupportedPlatform

code.public: This operation is not supported on this platform

symbols.doc:
UnsupportedPlatform is returned by NewFileStore on a platform without the
mechanics its guarantees rest on. It is the SDK-wide sentinel, shared
with pkg/v1/proc (ADR 0018).

symbols.name: Algorithm
symbols.doc:
Algorithm is the public alias for the signature algorithm a token issuer or
verifier is bound to.

symbols.name: AlgorithmES256
symbols.doc:
AlgorithmES256 is JOSE "ES256" — ECDSA on NIST P-256 with SHA-256 and the
fixed-width R||S signature encoding of RFC 7518 §3.4.

symbols.name: AlgorithmEdDSA
symbols.doc:
AlgorithmEdDSA is JOSE "EdDSA" — Ed25519 over the JWS signing input
(RFC 8037 §3.1).

symbols.name: AlgorithmHS256
symbols.doc:
AlgorithmHS256 is JOSE "HS256" — HMAC-SHA-256 over a 256-bit shared secret
(RFC 7518 §3.2). Symmetric: a verifier can also mint.

symbols.name: AlgorithmMismatch

code.public: The token algorithm is not the one this verifier accepts

symbols.doc:
AlgorithmMismatch is returned when the token's algorithm header is not
the algorithm the verifier is bound to. It is the verdict an
algorithm-confusion attempt produces, reached before any key is used.

symbols.name: AlgorithmNone

code.public: The token declares the unsecured none algorithm

symbols.doc:
AlgorithmNone is returned for a token declaring the unsecured "none"
algorithm. It is unconditional — no configuration accepts one.

symbols.name: AlgorithmPasetoV4Public
symbols.doc:
AlgorithmPasetoV4Public is PASETO v4.public — Ed25519 over the
pre-authentication encoding of the header, payload and footer.

symbols.name: AudienceMismatch

code.public: The token is not addressed to this audience

symbols.doc:
AudienceMismatch is returned when the configured audience is absent from
an authenticated token's aud (RFC 8725 §3.9).

symbols.name: ClaimAudience
symbols.doc: ClaimAudience is the registered claim "aud" (RFC 7519 §4.1.3).

symbols.name: ClaimExpiry
symbols.doc: ClaimExpiry is the registered claim "exp" (RFC 7519 §4.1.4).

symbols.name: ClaimID
symbols.doc: ClaimID is the registered claim "jti" (RFC 7519 §4.1.7).

symbols.name: ClaimIssuedAt
symbols.doc: ClaimIssuedAt is the registered claim "iat" (RFC 7519 §4.1.6).

symbols.name: ClaimIssuer
symbols.doc: ClaimIssuer is the registered claim "iss" (RFC 7519 §4.1.1).

symbols.name: ClaimNameInvalid

code.public: The claim name is empty or reserved

symbols.doc:
ClaimNameInvalid is returned for a private claim name that is empty or
shadows a registered one.

symbols.name: ClaimNotBefore
symbols.doc: ClaimNotBefore is the registered claim "nbf" (RFC 7519 §4.1.5).

symbols.name: ClaimSubject
symbols.doc: ClaimSubject is the registered claim "sub" (RFC 7519 §4.1.2).

symbols.name: Claims
symbols.doc: Claims is the public alias for a token's immutable claim set.

symbols.name: CodeAlgorithmMismatch
symbols.doc:
CodeAlgorithmMismatch identifies a header naming an algorithm other than the
bound one — what an algorithm-confusion attempt produces (0.2.13.3).

symbols.name: CodeAlgorithmNone
symbols.doc:
CodeAlgorithmNone identifies a token declaring the unsecured "none"
algorithm (0.2.13.2).

symbols.name: CodeAudienceMismatch
symbols.doc:
CodeAudienceMismatch identifies a configured audience absent from the token's
aud claim (0.2.13.8).

symbols.name: CodeClaimNameInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeClaimNameInvalid identifies an empty or reserved private-claim name
(0.2.13.15).

symbols.name: CodeDuplicateMember
symbols.doc:
CodeDuplicateMember identifies a header or claims object repeating a member
name (0.3.44.7).

symbols.name: CodeExpired
symbols.doc: CodeExpired identifies an authenticated token whose exp is past (0.2.13.5).

symbols.name: CodeExpiryRequired
symbols.doc:
CodeExpiryRequired identifies a token with no exp where the profile requires
one (0.2.13.7).

symbols.name: CodeFooterMismatch
symbols.doc:
CodeFooterMismatch identifies a PASETO footer that is not the expected one
(0.3.44.5).

symbols.name: CodeHeaderUnsupported
symbols.doc:
CodeHeaderUnsupported identifies a non-empty "crit", or a "typ" mismatch
(0.3.44.1).

symbols.name: CodeIssueFailed
symbols.doc:
CodeIssueFailed identifies claims that could not be rendered or signed
(0.2.13.14).

symbols.name: CodeIssuerMismatch
symbols.doc:
CodeIssuerMismatch identifies an iss that is not the configured issuer
(0.2.13.9).

symbols.name: CodeJWKInvalidEncoding
symbols.doc:
CodeJWKInvalidEncoding identifies a member that is not unpadded base64url, or
not the fixed length its curve mandates (0.3.42.5).

symbols.name: CodeJWKKeyMismatch
symbols.doc:
CodeJWKKeyMismatch identifies material that is not a key on the declared
curve: an off-curve point, an out-of-range scalar, or a "d" that does not
derive the declared public key (0.3.42.6).

symbols.name: CodeJWKMalformed
symbols.doc:
CodeJWKMalformed identifies a key document that is not the JSON shape
RFC 7517 describes — invalid JSON, a key that is not an object, or a set
whose "keys" is not an array (0.3.42.1).

symbols.name: CodeJWKMissingMember
symbols.doc:
CodeJWKMissingMember identifies a key missing a member its declared type
requires, or a set missing "keys" (0.3.42.2).

symbols.name: CodeJWKUnsupportedCurve
symbols.doc:
CodeJWKUnsupportedCurve identifies an unknown "crv", or one paired with the
wrong "kty" (0.3.42.4).

symbols.name: CodeJWKUnsupportedKeyType
symbols.doc:
CodeJWKUnsupportedKeyType identifies a "kty" other than EC, OKP or oct — RSA
included, since the SDK verifies nothing with RSA (0.3.42.3).

symbols.name: CodeKeyIDAmbiguous
symbols.doc:
CodeKeyIDAmbiguous identifies more keys sharing a kid than the verifier will
try (0.3.44.4).

symbols.name: CodeKeyIDMissing
symbols.doc:
CodeKeyIDMissing identifies a token presented to a set verifier with no kid
(0.3.44.3).

symbols.name: CodeKeyNotFound
symbols.doc: CodeKeyNotFound identifies a kid naming no key in the set (0.3.44.2).

symbols.name: CodeKeyUnsuitable
symbols.doc:
CodeKeyUnsuitable identifies a key that cannot serve the algorithm it was
handed to (0.2.13.12).

symbols.name: CodeLifetimeTooLong
symbols.doc:
CodeLifetimeTooLong identifies an exp-iat span past
VerifierConfig.MaxLifetime (0.2.13.16).

symbols.name: CodeMalformed
symbols.doc:
CodeMalformed identifies an input that could not be read as a token
(0.2.13.1).

symbols.name: CodeNotYetValid
symbols.doc:
CodeNotYetValid identifies an authenticated token whose nbf is in the future
(0.2.13.6).

symbols.name: CodePolicyMisconfigured
symbols.doc:
CodePolicyMisconfigured identifies a constructor given a configuration it
cannot honour; permanent, never a retry (0.2.13.13).

symbols.name: CodeSchemeUnsupported
symbols.doc:
CodeSchemeUnsupported identifies a PASETO version+purpose that is not
v4.public (0.3.44.6).

symbols.name: CodeSignatureInvalid
symbols.doc:
CodeSignatureInvalid identifies a signature or MAC tag that did not
authenticate (0.2.13.4).

symbols.name: CodeTooDeep
symbols.doc: CodeTooDeep identifies claims nested past MaxClaimDepth (0.2.13.11).

symbols.name: CodeTooLarge
symbols.doc: CodeTooLarge identifies an input past a declared size bound (0.2.13.10).

symbols.name: Curve
symbols.doc:
Curve is the public alias for a JWK's "crv" member, the curve [JWK].Crv
reports: [CurveP256], [CurveP384], [CurveP521] or [CurveEd25519]. A symmetric
key has no curve and reports the empty Curve.

symbols.name: CurveEd25519
symbols.doc: CurveEd25519 is the Edwards curve of an EdDSA key (RFC 8037 §2).

symbols.name: CurveP256
symbols.doc: CurveP256 is NIST P-256 (RFC 7518 §6.2.1.1), the curve of an ES256 key.

symbols.name: CurveP384
symbols.doc:
CurveP384 is NIST P-384. [ParseJWK] accepts it, but nothing in this package
signs or verifies with it, so [NewVerifierFromJWK] refuses it with
[KeyUnsuitable].

symbols.name: CurveP521
symbols.doc: CurveP521 is NIST P-521, accepted and refused exactly as P-384 is.

symbols.name: DuplicateMember

code.public: The token repeats a member name

symbols.doc:
DuplicateMember is returned when a header or claims object repeats a
member name (RFC 8725 §2.6).

symbols.name: Expired

code.public: The token has expired

symbols.doc: Expired is returned when an AUTHENTICATED token's exp is past.

symbols.name: ExpiryRequired

code.public: The token carries no expiry

symbols.doc:
ExpiryRequired is returned when a token carries no exp and the profile
requires one — the default on both the issuing and verifying side.

symbols.name: FooterMismatch

code.public: The token footer is not the expected one

symbols.doc:
FooterMismatch is returned for a PASETO footer that is not the expected
one, including a footer present where none was configured.

symbols.name: HeaderUnsupported

code.public: The token header carries parameters this verifier will not accept

symbols.doc:
HeaderUnsupported is returned for a header carrying a non-empty "crit",
or a "typ" other than VerifierConfig.RequireType.

symbols.name: IssueFailed

code.public: The token could not be issued

symbols.doc:
IssueFailed is returned when an issuer cannot render the given claims —
a claim the target format cannot express, or a signing fault.

symbols.name: Issuer
symbols.doc: Issuer is the public alias for the token-minting port.

symbols.name: IssuerConfig
symbols.doc: IssuerConfig is the public alias for the JWT issuing policy.

symbols.name: IssuerMismatch

code.public: The token issuer is not the expected one

symbols.doc:
IssuerMismatch is returned when an authenticated token's iss is not the
configured issuer (RFC 8725 §3.8).

symbols.name: JWK
symbols.doc:
JWK is the public alias for a parsed JSON Web Key (RFC 7517). Obtain one
from [ParseJWK]: the type has no exported field and deliberately no
UnmarshalJSON, so json.Unmarshal decodes nothing into a JWK — and reports no
error. A JWK field in a configuration struct therefore stays the zero JWK,
which [NewVerifierFromJWK] refuses with [KeyUnsuitable]; decode that field
as a json.RawMessage and hand it to ParseJWK instead.

json.Marshal renders a JWK's public members only. A symmetric ("oct") key
has no public form — its "k" member is the secret itself — so json.Marshal
refuses it rather than publish it; private members leave only through the
key's MarshalPrivate method, which says so at the call site.

symbols.name: JWKInvalidEncoding

code.public: JWK member is not valid unpadded base64url

symbols.doc:
JWKInvalidEncoding is returned for a member that is not unpadded
base64url, or not the fixed length its curve mandates.

symbols.name: JWKKeyMismatch

code.public: JWK material does not match the declared curve

symbols.doc:
JWKKeyMismatch is returned for well-encoded material that is not a key on
the declared curve: an off-curve point, an out-of-range scalar, or a "d"
that does not derive the declared public key.

symbols.name: JWKMalformed

code.public: JWK document is malformed

symbols.doc:
JWKMalformed is returned by ParseJWK / ParseJWKSet for a document that is
not the JSON shape RFC 7517 describes — invalid JSON, a key that is not an
object, or a set whose "keys" is not an array.

symbols.name: JWKMissingMember

code.public: JWK is missing a required member

symbols.doc:
JWKMissingMember is returned for a key missing a member its declared type
requires ("kty", "crv", "x", "y" or "k"), or a set missing "keys".

symbols.name: JWKSet
symbols.doc:
JWKSet is the public alias for a parsed JSON Web Key Set (RFC 7517 §5).
Obtain one from [ParseJWKSet], or assemble one from parsed keys with
[NewJWKSet].

symbols.name: JWKUnsupportedCurve

code.public: JWK curve is not supported

symbols.doc:
JWKUnsupportedCurve is returned for an unknown "crv", or a known one
paired with the wrong "kty" (P-256 under OKP, Ed25519 under EC).

symbols.name: JWKUnsupportedKeyType

code.public: JWK key type is not supported

symbols.doc:
JWKUnsupportedKeyType is returned for a "kty" other than EC, OKP or oct.
RSA is refused here on purpose: the SDK verifies nothing with RSA.

symbols.name: Key
symbols.doc:
Key is the public alias for the SDK's opaque, redacting 256-bit symmetric
key — the only type NewHS256Issuer / NewHS256Verifier accept. Build one with
pkg/v1/crypto.NewKey, or derive one with pkg/v1/crypto/kdf; never type one.

symbols.name: KeyIDAmbiguous

code.public: Too many keys share this token key identifier

symbols.doc:
KeyIDAmbiguous is returned when more keys share a kid than
VerifierConfig.MaxKeyCandidates allows the verifier to try.

symbols.name: KeyIDMissing

code.public: The token carries no key identifier

symbols.doc:
